etymology_story.zh: 借自法语 glacé，即 glacer（使结冰、给……上糖衣或作光亮处理）的过去分词，最终源于拉丁语 glacies（冰）。冰面般的光泽把结冰、糖衣和皮革或织物的亮面处理联系起来。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed French glacé, the past participle of glacer, meaning to freeze, ice, or glaze, ultimately from Latin glacies, meaning ice. An ice-like shine connects the sugary coating and glossy material senses. [Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/glace)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常把 glace／glacé 作为整体借词，不把末尾 e 当作英语后缀；法语来源可分析为 glac-（冰、结冰）+ -é（过去分词词尾）。动词形式有 glacés、glacéed、glacéing，去重音符号的对应形式为 glaces、glaceed、glaceing，另见 glaced。glacial（冰川的、冰冷的）、glacier（冰川）、glaciation（冰川作用）是同源词，并非由现代英语 glace 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, glace/glacé is normally treated as a whole loanword; its final e is not an English suffix. Its French source contains glac- (ice or freezing) + -é (a past-participle ending). Verb forms include glacés, glacéed, and glacéing; unaccented forms include glaces, glaceed, and glaceing, with glaced also recorded. Glacial, glacier, and glaciation share its historical root but are not direct modern derivatives. [Collins](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/glace)

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: candied（糖渍的）强调用糖保存；glazed（上釉的、裹亮面涂层的）强调表面涂层，未必涉及糖渍保存；glossy（有光泽的）只描述外观。glace／glacé 的食品义兼有糖处理和光亮外层的意味，材料义则强调加工所得的光泽。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Candied emphasizes preservation with sugar; glazed emphasizes a surface coating, which need not involve candying; glossy describes appearance alone. Glace/glacé combines sugar treatment with a shiny finish in food contexts and denotes a treated shine in material contexts.

etymology_story.zh: 这是由 globule（小球）一系词形加物质名称后缀 -in 构成的科学术语；globule 最终来自拉丁语 globulus（小球），即 globus（球）的指小形式。名称保留了“小球”的意象，但实际分类还涉及溶解性等性质。
etymology_story.en: This scientific term was formed from globule and the substance-forming suffix -in; globule ultimately comes from Latin globulus, a diminutive of globus, meaning ball. The name preserves the image of a small sphere, although the protein category also depends on properties such as solubility. [Collins](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/globulin)

morphology_enriched.zh: globul-（小球；对应 globule 去掉末尾不发音的 e）+ -in（物质名称后缀）→ globulin；复数 globulins。相关词有 globule（小球）、globular（球状的）、globularity（球状性）；主要复合词有 immunoglobulin（免疫球蛋白）、antiglobulin（抗球蛋白抗体）、macroglobulin（巨球蛋白）、thyroglobulin（甲状腺球蛋白），另有 alpha／beta／gamma globulin（α／β／γ 球蛋白）。
morphology_enriched.en: Globul- (small sphere, corresponding to globule without its final silent e) + -in (a substance-forming suffix) → globulin; plural globulins. Related forms include globule, globular, and globularity. Major compounds include immunoglobulin (an immune-system protein), antiglobulin (an antibody against globulins), macroglobulin (a large globulin), and thyroglobulin (a thyroid protein), alongside alpha, beta, and gamma globulin.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有覆盖全部义项的严格同义词。protein（蛋白质）是上位词；immunoglobulin（免疫球蛋白）指具有抗体功能的一类球蛋白；albumin（白蛋白）是另一类蛋白质，传统上以易溶于水等性质与球蛋白区分，不能互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no exact synonym covering every sense. Protein is the broader category; immunoglobulin denotes globulins with antibody functions; albumin is a different protein class, traditionally distinguished partly by water solubility, and is not interchangeable with globulin.

etymology_story.zh: 直接借自拉丁语 homunculus，是 homo（人）的指小形式，字面意思是“小小的人”。它后来用于炼金术和预成论中的微型人，并扩展为神经科学的人体表征模型及心灵哲学中的内部观察者意象。

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是整体借词；按拉丁语来源可用 hom-（人）+ -unculus（指小成分）辅助记忆，不应把这些部分当作现代英语中自由组合的词素。复数为 homunculi；形容词 homuncular 表示“小人形的、与微型人有关的”；homuncle、homuncule 是罕见变体。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English treats the word as a whole loanword. Its Latin structure can be remembered as hom- (human) + -unculus (a diminutive element), rather than as freely productive English components. The plural is homunculi; homuncular means relating to a homunculus. Homuncle and homuncule are rare variants.

synonyms_and_nuances.en: Manikin emphasizes a small human-shaped figure and is closest to the general miniature-figure sense; miniature person is a neutral explanatory phrase; inner observer approximates only the philosophy-of-mind sense, not the alchemical or cortical senses.

Its historical water-in-the-head image refers in modern medicine to cerebrospinal fluid rather than ordinary water. [Collins](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/hydrocephalus)

morphology_enriched.zh: hydro-（水、液体）+ cephal-（头）+ -us（拉丁化名词词尾）→ hydrocephalus。相关词有 hydrocephaly（脑积水，异形词）、hydrocephalic（脑积水的）、hydrocephalous（患脑积水的，较少用）、hydrocephaloid（类似脑积水的，罕见）。本词通常用作不可数病名；hydrocephalic 是另一个词，不能据此把 hydrocephalus 标作形容词。
morphology_enriched.en: Hydro- (water or fluid) + cephal- (head) + -us (a Latinized noun ending) → hydrocephalus. Related forms include hydrocephaly (an alternative noun), hydrocephalic (relating to hydrocephalus), hydrocephalous (affected by hydrocephalus, less common), and hydrocephaloid (resembling hydrocephalus, rare). Hydrocephalus normally functions as an uncountable disease name; the separate adjective hydrocephalic does not give hydrocephalus an adjective use.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: hydrocephaly（脑积水）是较少用的同义形式；water on the brain（脑中积水）是非专业俗称；ventriculomegaly（脑室扩大）指影像学上的脑室增大，可有不同原因，不能一律等同于脑积水。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Hydrocephaly is a less common synonym; water on the brain is a nontechnical expression; ventriculomegaly describes enlarged ventricles on imaging and can have different causes, so it is not an exact synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: hydro（水）+ cephal（头）：头内液体积多了；医学上记为脑室内脑脊液异常积聚。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Hydro means water and cephal means head: connect the name with excess cerebrospinal fluid in the brain's ventricles.

etymology_story.zh: 来自拉丁语 irruptio，常经法语 irruption 传入；其相关动词 irrumpere 由表示“向内”的 in- 和 rumpere（打破）组成。最初“突破而入”的方向感，后来延伸到动物种群的突然增多和鸟类的大规模异常迁入。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Latin irruptio, also transmitted through French irruption; the related verb irrumpere combines in-, meaning into, with rumpere, meaning break. The idea of bursting in later extended to sudden population increases and irregular mass arrivals of birds. [Merriam-Webster: irrupt](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/irrupt), [Merriam-Webster: irruption](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/irruption)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代词族关系可表示为 irrupt（闯入、数量骤增）+ -ion（行为或过程名词后缀）→ irruption；历史词根拆解为 ir-（in- 在 r 前的同化形式，向内）+ rupt（破裂）+ -ion。词族包括 irrupt、irrupts、irrupted、irrupting、irruption、irruptions、irruptive（突然侵入的；种群骤增的）；rupture（破裂）、eruption（喷发）、interruption（打断）是同根相关词。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern family relationship is irrupt (to rush in or increase suddenly) + -ion (an action or process noun suffix) → irruption. Historically, it contains ir- (in-, meaning into, assimilated before r) + rupt (break) + -ion. The family includes irrupt, irrupts, irrupted, irrupting, irruption, irruptions, and irruptive. Rupture, eruption, and interruption share the historical break root.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: incursion（侵入、袭扰）常指范围或时间有限的进入；influx（大量涌入）强调数量而不必猛烈；invasion（入侵）强调侵犯、占领或大规模侵入。irruption 尤其突出突然突破而入；其鸟类学义不能简单等同于规律性的 migration（迁徙）。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Incursion often suggests a limited intrusion; influx emphasizes large numbers arriving without necessarily implying force; invasion suggests intrusive entry, occupation, or overwhelming numbers. Irruption particularly stresses sudden bursting in, and its ornithological sense differs from regular migration.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: ir- 向内 + rupt 破：破门而入；对照 eruption 的向外喷发，再联想到鸟群突然大量涌来。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Ir- points inward and rupt means break: picture a door bursting inward, then a sudden flood of birds; compare eruption, which originally points outward.

etymology_story.en: This modern scientific term combines melano-, from Greek melas meaning 'black', with -cyte, from Greek kytos meaning 'a hollow vessel' and later used for a cell. The name reflects the cell's role in producing melanin.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词：melano-（黑色、黑色素）+ -cyte（细胞）。直接词族包括 melanocytes（复数）和 melanocytic（黑素细胞的）；相关同源词包括 melanin（黑色素）、melanogenesis（黑色素生成）和 melanoblast（成黑素细胞），这些不是由 melanocyte 直接派生而来。

The direct family includes melanocytes and melanocytic ('relating to melanocytes'); related formations include melanin, melanogenesis ('melanin production'), and melanoblast ('a precursor of a melanocyte'), rather than direct derivatives of melanocyte.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: melanin-producing cell（产生黑色素的细胞）是解释性近义表达；pigment cell（色素细胞）范围更广；melanophore（载黑素细胞）主要用于鱼类、两栖类等动物的特定色素细胞，不能在所有语境中替换 melanocyte。

mnemonic_anchor.zh: melano- 指黑色素，-cyte 指细胞：制造黑色素的细胞。

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词：micro-（微小的、局部的）+ environment（环境）；environment 内部为 environ（围绕）+ -ment（名词后缀）。直接词族包括 microenvironments（复数）和 microenvironmental（微环境的）；基础词族包括 environment、environmental（环境的）和 environmentally（在环境方面）。

etymology_story.zh: paginate 以拉丁语 pagina（页）的词干 pagin- 为基础，加上动词后缀 -ate 构成。它表示给页面编号，也用于将内容组织成独立页面，在数字出版和计算机领域进一步用于数据分页。
etymology_story.en: Paginate was formed from pagin-, the stem of Latin pagina meaning 'page', with the verb-forming suffix -ate. It denotes numbering or arranging pages and has extended to dividing digital content and data into pages.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词：pagin-（页）+ -ate（动词后缀）。词族包括 paginates、paginated、paginating、pagination（编页码；分页）、paginator（分页程序或编页码者），以及 repaginate（重新分页或编页码）、repaginated、repaginating 和 repagination（重新分页或编页码）。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: pagin- ('page') + -ate (a verb suffix). The family includes paginates, paginated, paginating, pagination ('page numbering or division into pages'), paginator ('a program or person that paginates'), repaginate, repaginated, repaginating, and repagination.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: number the pages（编页码）明确指添加页码；divide into pages（分页）强调划分页面；format（排版、设置格式）范围更广，还包括字体、间距和其他版式设置。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Number the pages specifically means adding page numbers; divide into pages emphasizes page boundaries; format is broader and also covers fonts, spacing, and other layout choices.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: pagin- 联想到 page：让内容成为一页页，并给页面定位。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect pagin- with page: turn content into pages and give those pages their place.

etymology_story.zh: 该词形成于16世纪，由 pie（喜鹊的旧称）和 bald（当时可指带白斑的）组成，借用了喜鹊黑白相间的羽色。它后来也用作名词，指具有这种毛色的动物，尤其是马。
etymology_story.en: The word arose in the sixteenth century from pie, an older name for the magpie, and bald in a sense referring to white markings, evoking the bird's black-and-white plumage. It also became a noun for an animal, especially a horse, with that colouring.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词：pie（喜鹊的旧称）+ bald（历史义为带白斑的）；现代通常将其作为整体词使用。词族包括 piebalds（名词复数）、piebaldness（黑白花斑这一特征）和 piebaldism（斑驳病，一种先天性色素缺失状况）；医学词 piebaldism 不等同于普通的动物花斑毛色。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: pie (an older word for 'magpie') + bald (historically referring to white markings); modern speakers generally treat it as a whole word. The family includes piebalds, piebaldness ('the quality of being piebald'), and piebaldism (a congenital condition involving patches lacking pigment); the medical term is distinct from ordinary animal coat colouring.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: pied（杂色的、花斑的）不限于黑白两色；skewbald（白色与黑色以外另一种颜色相间的）在马匹毛色中与 piebald 有明确区别；pinto（花斑马或花斑的）在美式用法中范围更广，可包括多种大片白斑毛色。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Pied means multicoloured or patched and is not limited to black and white; skewbald specifically describes white patches combined with a colour other than black in horses; pinto is broader in American usage and covers various coats with substantial white patches.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 想起喜鹊的黑白羽色：喜鹊配色的马，就是 piebald。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a magpie's black-and-white plumage: a horse in magpie colours is piebald.

etymology.text: 经中古英语和盎格鲁法语传来，源于拉丁语 prolixus（延伸的）；其更早成分与向前流淌有关，可联想话语一直流个不停。

usage_note: 正式且带贬义，形容文字或说话过长，不只是中性的长。

senses.meaning_zh: （言辞、文章或说话者）冗长啰嗦的
senses.meaning_en: Using too many words and becoming tediously long.
senses.english_definition: If someone's speech or writing is prolix, it uses more words than necessary and takes too long to express its point.

etymology_story.zh: 该词经法语进入中古英语，源自拉丁语 prolixus，原有“伸展的、漫长的”等意思。这个表示延伸的词后来用于言语，形成了“说得过长、冗长啰嗦”的含义。
etymology_story.en: The word entered Middle English through French from Latin prolixus, meaning extended or lengthy. Its sense of excessive length became especially associated with speech and writing.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 prolix 视为完整的形容词词基，不宜把它硬拆成能产词缀。主要词族：prolix + -ity → prolixity（冗长、啰嗦）；prolix + -ly → prolixly（冗长地）；prolix + -ness → prolixness（冗长，较少用）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, prolix functions as a whole adjective base rather than a transparently productive combination of affixes. Its principal derivatives are prolixity, the quality of being excessively wordy; prolixly, in an excessively wordy manner; and the less common prolixness.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: verbose（用词过多的）突出字词数量过多；wordy（啰嗦的）较日常，强调表达不够简洁；long-winded（长篇累牍的）突出说话或解释拖得太久。prolix 较正式，兼有冗长和令人厌倦之意。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Verbose emphasizes an excessive number of words; wordy is a more everyday criticism of insufficiently concise expression; long-winded emphasizes taking too long to finish speaking or explaining. Prolix is formal and suggests both excessive length and tediousness.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住历史上的“延伸”意象：一句话不断拉长，就成了冗长啰嗦。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture the historical idea of extension: a sentence keeps stretching until it becomes tediously long.

etymology.text: 由莱茵河的拉丁语名称 Rhenus 加英语后缀 -ish 形成，保留了这条欧洲河流的古老名字。

etymology_story.zh: 该词在中古英语时期已经出现，其词形最终与莱茵河的拉丁语名称 Rhenus 相联系。它先表示“莱茵地区的”，又通过省略 wine 而成为当地葡萄酒的旧称。
etymology_story.en: The word was already present in Middle English and is ultimately connected with Rhenus, the Latin name of the Rhine. Its geographical adjective also became a noun for the region's wine through the omission of wine.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代词形可分析为 Rhen-（与莱茵河有关的受限地名词基）+ -ish（……的），但 Rhen- 不能独立使用。Rhenish 兼作形容词和酒类名词；相关词有 Rhine（莱茵河）、Rhineland（莱茵地区）和 Rhinelander（莱茵地区居民），它们不是直接由 Rhenish 派生的。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern form can be analyzed as the bound geographical base Rhen- plus -ish, meaning relating to; Rhen- does not stand alone. Rhenish serves as both an adjective and a wine noun. Related geographical words include Rhine, Rhineland, and Rhinelander, although these are not direct derivatives of Rhenish.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Rhineland（莱茵地区，常作名词定语）主要指该地区，例如 Rhineland culture；Rhenish 可修饰与莱茵河或其周边地区有关的事物。Rhine wine（莱茵葡萄酒）对应其名词义，比单独使用 Rhenish 更直白，也更符合现代一般表达。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Rhineland, often used attributively, primarily identifies the region, as in Rhineland culture; Rhenish can describe connections with either the river or its surrounding region. Rhine wine corresponds to the noun sense and is more explicit and more natural in general modern usage.

etymology_story.zh: 该词源自拉丁语 rusticari（在乡间生活）及其分词词干 rusticat-，最终与 rus（乡村）有关。大学中的停学义来自把学生暂时送离大学的做法；建筑义则与 rustic 的“粗朴、乡野”意象相联系。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Latin rusticari, to live in the country, and its participial stem rusticat-, ultimately related to rus, countryside. The university sense developed from sending students away temporarily, while the architectural sense is associated with the rough or rustic appearance of masonry.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代学习可按 rustic（乡村的、粗朴的）+ -ate（动词后缀）理解，但这只是词族分析，英语实际借入了拉丁语词形。主要词族：rustic（乡村的；乡下人）、rustically（乡村式地）、rusticity（乡村特征；粗朴）、rusticate、rusticated（粗面凸石装饰的；被停学的）、rustication（乡居；大学停学；粗面凸石工法）。动词变化：rusticates、rusticated、rusticating。
morphology_enriched.en: For modern learning, the word can be associated with rustic plus the verb-forming suffix -ate, although English historically borrowed the Latin formation. The principal family includes rustic, rustically, rusticity, rusticate, rusticated, and rustication. Rustication can refer to country living, university suspension, or the architectural treatment. Verb forms are rusticates, rusticated, and rusticating.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: retire to the country（退居乡间）强调退出原有生活，常有长期定居意味，而 rusticate 可以只是短期乡居；suspend（使停学）是更通用的现代用语；expel（开除）通常意味着永久取消学籍，比大学语境中的 rusticate 更严重。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Retire to the country suggests withdrawing from one's previous life, often permanently, whereas rusticate can describe a short rural stay. Suspend is the more general modern term for temporary exclusion from study. Expel usually means permanent removal and is stronger than rusticate in university usage.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 以 rustic“乡村的、粗朴的”为中心：人去乡居，学生被暂时送离校园，石面则呈现粗朴质感。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor the word in rustic: people go to the country, students are temporarily sent away, and stonework takes on a rough rustic appearance.

senses.english_definition: A samosa is a small pastry, usually shaped like a triangle, that contains a savory filling and is fried or baked.

etymology_story.zh: 英语从印地语 samosā 或乌尔都语的相应形式借入该词，更早可追溯到波斯语 sambūsa 一类名称。这个名称随着包馅面点在不同地区传播，并在英语中主要指广受欢迎的南亚小吃。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed the word from Hindi samosā or its Urdu equivalent, with earlier ancestry in Persian forms such as sambūsa. The name traveled with the filled pastry and in English chiefly denotes the familiar South Asian snack.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 samosa 是不可进一步拆分的借入名词，没有常用的派生词族。规则复数为 samosas；常见组合有 vegetable samosa（蔬菜萨莫萨）、potato samosa（土豆馅萨莫萨）和 samosa filling（萨莫萨馅料），这些是修饰组合，不是词缀派生。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, samosa is an unanalyzed borrowed noun with no established common family of derivatives. Its regular plural is samosas. Vegetable samosa, potato samosa, and samosa filling are ordinary modifier combinations rather than affixal derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: savory pastry（咸味面点）是上位词，不能体现萨莫萨的具体形状和传统；turnover（折叠馅饼）与其制作结构相近，但可甜可咸；dumpling（饺子类面食）有时用于解释其外形，却不能准确替代 samosa 所指的酥皮小吃。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Savory pastry is a broad category that does not identify the samosa's particular form or tradition. Turnover describes a similar folded structure but may be sweet or savory. Dumpling is sometimes used as an explanatory comparison, but it is not an exact substitute for this pastry.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 整词配图记：三角薄皮包住香料土豆馅，就是常见的 samosa。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember the whole word with a picture: a crisp pastry triangle enclosing spiced potatoes is a typical samosa.

etymology_story.zh: 该词得名于德国塞尔特斯的矿泉水，与德语 Selterser Wasser（塞尔特斯的水）有关。它后来由特定产地的水名泛化为气泡水的名称，并出现在 hard seltzer 等现代饮料名称中。
etymology_story.en: The word takes its name from the mineral water of Selters in Germany and is associated with German Selterser Wasser, meaning water from Selters. It broadened from a geographical water name to carbonated water generally and later appeared in modern drink names such as hard seltzer.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 seltzer 作为完整名词词基，不把结尾 -er 当作英语中表示人的后缀。没有常用的直接派生词族；常见复合或修饰组合有 seltzer water（气泡水）、seltzer bottle（气泡水瓶；传统上可指喷瓶）和 hard seltzer（含酒精气泡饮料）。seltzers 可指多份、多种气泡水或多罐含酒精气泡饮料，具体取决于语境。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, seltzer is a whole noun base; its ending is not the English agent suffix -er. It has no common direct family of derivatives. Established combinations include seltzer water, seltzer bottle, and hard seltzer. The plural seltzers can refer to servings or varieties of carbonated water, or to alcoholic seltzer drinks, depending on context.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: carbonated water（碳酸水）是中性技术名称；sparkling water（气泡水）常与 seltzer 重合，也可指天然含气矿泉水；club soda（苏打水）通常添加矿物盐，而原味 seltzer 通常只是充入二氧化碳的水。这些名称在日常和商品用语中可能交叠。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Carbonated water is the neutral technical term. Sparkling water often overlaps with seltzer but can also denote naturally carbonated mineral water. Club soda usually contains added mineral salts, whereas plain seltzer is typically water carbonated with carbon dioxide. Everyday and commercial naming can overlap.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 记住“地名变水名”：Selters 的矿泉水让 seltzer 成了气泡水的名称；加上 hard，就带上了酒精。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember a place becoming a drink name: water from Selters gave seltzer its name; adding hard signals alcohol.

morphology.text: sero-（血清）+ negative（阴性）→ seronegative（血清反应阴性的）。

etymology.text: 这是英语医学构词，sero- 来自拉丁语 serum（血清），再与 negative 组合；可记成“血清检测结果为阴性”。

senses.meaning_zh: 血清学检测呈阴性的；尤指未检出某种特异性抗体的
senses.meaning_en: Showing a negative result in a serum test, especially for a particular antibody.
senses.english_definition: If someone is seronegative, a blood serum test has not detected the particular antibody or other marker being tested for.

etymology_story.zh: 由表示“血清”的 sero- 与 negative（阴性的）组成，其中 sero- 源自拉丁语 serum。这个医学词用于描述特定血清学检测的阴性反应。[词源与释义来源：Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/seronegative)
etymology_story.en: The word combines sero-, meaning 'serum' and derived from Latin serum, with negative. It developed as a medical description of a negative reaction in a particular serum test. [Etymology and definition: Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/seronegative)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：sero-（血清）+ negative（阴性的）→ seronegative；直接派生词：seronegativity（血清阴性状态）。相关构词包括 seropositive（血清阳性的）、seropositivity（血清阳性状态）和 seroconversion（血清转换），它们并非 seronegative 的直接派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: sero- ('serum') + negative → seronegative; the direct noun derivative is seronegativity. Related formations include seropositive, seropositivity, and seroconversion; these are related terms rather than direct derivatives of seronegative.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: antibody-negative（抗体阴性的）明确指抗体未检出；serologically negative（血清学检测阴性的）最接近原词；test-negative（检测阴性的）范围更广，并不限于血清学检测。这些表达均不自动等于“没有感染”。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Antibody-negative specifically concerns undetected antibodies; serologically negative is the closest paraphrase; test-negative is broader and can describe other types of testing. None automatically means that infection is absent.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: sero- 锁定“血清”，negative 锁定“阴性”：记检测结果，并记清检测对象。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Sero- identifies the serum; negative identifies the result: remember which marker was tested.

morphology.text: 历史构词可联系 till（耕作）+ -th（名词后缀）→ tilth（土壤经耕作后的状态）；现代拼写只保留一个 l。

etymology_story.en: Tilth comes through Middle English from an Old English cultivation noun historically related to tilian, 'to till.' From cultivation and cultivated land, its meaning developed to include the soil condition suitable for crop growth. [Etymology and definition: Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/tilth)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常作为整体名词使用；历史构词可联系 till（耕作）与名词后缀 -th，但不能把现代形式机械写成 tillth。相关词族：till（耕作）、tills、tilled、tilling、tiller（耕作者；耕耘机）、tillage（耕作）、tillable（可耕种的）、untillable（不可耕种的）；这些并非由 tilth 逐一派生。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, tilth is normally treated as a whole noun; historically it is related to till and the noun-forming suffix -th, rather than a productive modern form tillth. Its related family includes till, tills, tilled, tilling, tiller, tillage, tillable, and untillable; these are not successive derivatives of tilth.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: soil condition（土壤状况）范围较广；soil structure（土壤结构）强调颗粒形成团聚体及孔隙的排列，是耕性的重要组成部分；tillage（耕作）主要指处理土壤的作业，而 tilth 强调土壤所处的状态。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Soil condition is broader; soil structure concerns the arrangement of aggregates and pores and is a major component of tilth; tillage usually names the work done to soil, whereas tilth emphasizes its condition.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 till（耕作）连到 tilth：耕后土壤是否松散、透气、适合生长。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect till with tilth: think of soil becoming loose, aerated, and ready for growth.

senses.meaning_zh: 乙炔，化学式为 C₂H₂ 的无色可燃气体
senses.meaning_en: A colourless, flammable gas, C₂H₂, used in welding and chemical manufacture.
senses.english_definition: Acetylene is a colourless gas that is used with oxygen to produce a very hot flame for welding and cutting metal.
senses.collocation_zh: 乙炔气；乙炔气瓶
senses.sentence_en: The workshop uses acetylene and oxygen to cut thick steel plates.
senses.sentence_zh: 这间车间使用乙炔和氧气切割厚钢板。

etymology_story.zh: 英语借自法语 acétylène，由 acétyle（乙酰基的名称）与化学命名后缀 -ène 构成。这是历史命名关系；现代化学中 acetylene 指乙炔，并不表示它含有乙酰基。[词源与释义来源：Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/acetylene)
etymology_story.en: English borrowed French acétylène, formed from acétyle, the name of acetyl, and the chemical suffix -ène. This is a historical naming relationship: modern acetylene denotes C₂H₂, not a substance containing an acetyl group. [Etymology and definition: Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/acetylene)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代使用中是完整的化学名称；历史命名可拆为 acetyl + -ene，不能据此推断其化学结构。主要相关形式：acetylenic（乙炔的；含碳碳三键的）、acetylide（乙炔化物）、acetylenation（乙炔化）、oxyacetylene（氧乙炔的；氧乙炔混合气）；ethyne 是同一物质的系统名称。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern use, this is a complete chemical name; its historical formation is acetyl + -ene, which does not determine its molecular structure. Principal related forms include acetylenic, acetylide, acetylenation, and oxyacetylene. Ethyne is the systematic name for the same substance.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: ethyne（乙炔）是同一物质的系统名称；acetylene gas（乙炔气）是强调气态的表达。oxyacetylene（氧乙炔混合气）含氧气，并非纯乙炔的同义词；ethylene（乙烯，C₂H₄）则是另一种化合物。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Ethyne is the systematic name for the same compound; acetylene gas explicitly identifies its gaseous form. Oxyacetylene refers to acetylene combined with oxygen, not pure acetylene; ethylene, C₂H₄, is a different compound.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 acetylene 绑到焊炬：C₂H₂ 配氧，产生高温火焰；词尾 -ene 不代表它是烯烃。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor acetylene to a welding torch: C₂H₂ plus oxygen produces intense heat; its historical -ene ending does not make it an alkene.

morphology.text: bound（跳跃）+ -er（做某事的人）→ bounder；这个形式原可表示跳跃者，贬义用法作为整词记忆。

etymology.text: 英语以 bound 和表示人的 -er 构成这个词，后来也用作对男人的贬称。记住它在旧式英国小说里常是骂人的话，不要仅按“会跳的人”理解。

usage_note: bounder 是偏旧式的英式贬称，常指无礼或不讲道德的男人；本课不教字面上的“跳跃者”。

senses.meaning_zh: 品行卑劣或举止不体面的男人；无赖（英式、旧式、贬义）
senses.meaning_en: A dishonourable or socially objectionable man, in old-fashioned British usage.
senses.english_definition: If you call a man a bounder, you mean that he behaves dishonourably or treats other people badly.
senses.collocation_en: an absolute bounder; a complete bounder
senses.collocation_zh: 一个十足的无赖；一个彻头彻尾的无赖

senses.sentence_zh: 她发现他对她们两人都撒了谎，便骂他是个无赖。

senses.meaning_zh: 弹跳着前进的球，尤指棒球中的弹跳地滚球
senses.meaning_en: A ball that moves in bounds, especially a bouncing ground ball in baseball.
senses.english_definition: In baseball, a bounder is a ball that has been hit and bounces along the ground.
senses.collocation_en: a high bounder; a slow bounder
senses.collocation_zh: 高弹跳地滚球；缓慢弹跳的地滚球
senses.sentence_en: The shortstop fielded a high bounder and threw to first base.
senses.sentence_zh: 游击手接住一个高弹跳地滚球，然后将球传向一垒。

etymology_story.zh: 由 bound（跳跃、弹跳）与表示施事者的 -er 构成，早期字面义是“跳跃或弹跳的人或物”。后来又出现指品行或社交举止令人反感的男人的贬义，这一意义不能简单由“跳跃者”推导。[历史与释义来源：Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/bounder)
etymology_story.en: Bounder was formed from bound, 'to leap or bounce,' and the agent suffix -er, initially naming someone or something that bounds. It later acquired a disparaging sense for a socially objectionable man; that meaning is not predictable from 'one who leaps.' [History and definitions: Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/bounder)

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词：bound（跳跃、弹跳）+ -er（动作执行者）→ bounder；复数 bounders；派生形容词 bounderish（无赖般的，不常见）。相关动词形式为 bounds、bounded、bounding；此处 bound 不是 bind（捆绑）的过去式。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: bound ('leap or bounce') + -er ('performer') → bounder; plural bounders; the related adjective is bounderish, which is uncommon. Related verb forms are bounds, bounded, and bounding. This bound is not the past tense of bind.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 人物义：cad（卑鄙的男人）尤其强调对他人、传统上对女性的不体面行为；scoundrel（恶棍）强调不诚实或道德败坏；rotter（坏蛋）同样带旧式英式贬义。棒球义可近似用 grounder（地滚球），但 bounder 更突出弹跳。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For the personal sense, cad particularly suggests dishonourable treatment of others, traditionally women; scoundrel emphasizes dishonesty or moral wrongdoing; rotter is another dated British insult. In baseball, grounder is a near-equivalent, while bounder highlights bouncing.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 字面抓住 bound 的“弹跳”：球会弹跳；人物义另联想“举止越界的无赖”，后者仅为记忆联想。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Use bound's bouncing motion for the ball sense; picture a man overstepping social boundaries for the insult, as a memory association only.

etymology.text: 来自新拉丁语分类名 Bryozoa 再加英语 -an；分类名用表示“苔藓”和“动物”的希腊语词根组成。名字描绘的是苔藓般的动物群体。

etymology_story.zh: 来自新拉丁语分类名 Bryozoa 加 -an；Bryozoa 由表示“苔藓”的希腊语词根 bryo- 和表示“动物”的 -zoa 构成。这个名称描绘群体的苔藓状外观，并不表示它们是植物。[词源与释义来源：Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/bryozoan)
etymology_story.en: Bryozoan comes from the New Latin taxonomic name Bryozoa plus -an; Bryozoa combines Greek-derived bryo-, 'moss,' with -zoa, 'animals.' The name describes the mosslike appearance of colonies, rather than classifying them as plants. [Etymology and definition: Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/bryozoan)

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词：Bryozoa（苔藓动物门）+ -an（成员；与之有关的）→ bryozoan，可作名词和形容词；名词复数为 bryozoans。相关词族：bryozoology（苔藓动物学）、bryozoologist（苔藓动物学家）；词根为 bryo-（苔藓）和 zo-（动物）。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: Bryozoa + -an ('a member of' or 'relating to') → bryozoan, used as both noun and adjective; the noun plural is bryozoans. Related family members include bryozoology and bryozoologist; the combining elements are bryo- ('moss') and zo- ('animal').

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: moss animal（苔藓动物）是直观的通俗名称；ectoproct（外肛动物）在将 Bryozoa 限定为外肛动物的现代分类用法中可作对应名称。coral（珊瑚）虽然也可形成类似群体，却属于另一动物类群，并非同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Moss animal is the descriptive common name; ectoproct is an equivalent in modern classifications that restrict Bryozoa to Ectoprocta. Coral can also form superficially similar colonies, but belongs to a different animal group and is not a synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: bryo-＝苔藓，zo-＝动物：长得像苔藓的一群小动物。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Bryo- means moss and zo- means animal: picture tiny animals forming a mosslike colony.

senses.meaning_zh: 日历的；历法的；与历法计算有关的
senses.meaning_en: relating to calendars or systems of calculating dates
senses.english_definition: Calendrical systems, calculations, or rules concern how days, months, and years are organized and dates are determined.
senses.collocation_zh: 历法计算；历法体系
senses.sentence_en: The festival falls on a different date each year because of the calendrical system used.
senses.sentence_zh: 由于采用的历法体系不同，这个节日每年的公历日期都不一样。

etymology_story.zh: 该词由 calendar 的词干 calendr- 加形容词后缀构成。Calendar 经中古英语和法语追溯至拉丁语 kalendarium，原指按月记账的账簿，其名称与 kalendae（古罗马每月的第一天）有关。
etymology_story.en: The word was formed from the stem calendr- of calendar with an adjective-forming suffix. Calendar ultimately comes through Middle English and French from Latin kalendarium, an account book associated with the kalendae, the first day of each Roman month.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：calendr-（calendar 的词干变体）+ -ical（形容词后缀）→ calendrical。主要词族：calendar（日历；历法；把……列入日程）、calendric（历法的，较少用）、calendrically（按历法地；就历法而言）、calendaring（日程安排；编制日历）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: calendr-, a stem variant of calendar, + -ical, an adjective-forming suffix → calendrical. Principal family members include calendar, both a noun and a verb; calendric, a less common adjective; calendrically, an adverb; and calendaring, the activity of scheduling or preparing calendars.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: calendar-related（与日历或历法有关的）最直白；chronological（按时间顺序的）强调事件先后；temporal（时间的）泛指时间关系。Calendrical 专指日期编排、历法规则及其计算。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Calendar-related is a plain-language equivalent; chronological emphasizes the order of events; temporal concerns time more broadly. Calendrical specifically concerns calendar organization, rules, and calculations.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: calendar（日历）→ calendrical：研究日历怎样安排年月日。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Calendar → calendrical: how a calendar organizes days, months, and years.

etymology_story.zh: 该词借自植物学拉丁语属名 Calendula，与拉丁语 calendae 或 kalendae（月首）及指小后缀有关。这个名称通常被解释为暗指这种植物花期长，仿佛每个月都在开花。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from the botanical Latin genus name Calendula, associated with Latin calendae or kalendae, the first day of the month, and a diminutive ending. The name is usually explained as referring to the plant's prolonged flowering, as though it bloomed every month.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语通常把 calendula 作为完整借词处理，不宜拆成可自由构词的英语词根和后缀；历史上可联系 calend-（月首）与拉丁语指小成分 -ula。常用形式：calendulas（复数）；Calendula 为属名写法；calendula oil（金盏花油）和 calendula extract（金盏花提取物）是名词短语，其中 calendula 作名词定语。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, calendula is normally treated as an intact loanword rather than a productive combination of English roots and affixes; historically, calend- relates to the first day of the month and -ula is a Latin diminutive element. The regular plural is calendulas, and Calendula is the capitalized genus name; calendula oil and calendula extract are noun phrases with calendula used attributively.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: pot marigold（金盏花）通常特指 Calendula officinalis，是最接近的常用名称；marigold（金盏花或万寿菊类植物）含义较宽且容易混淆；Tagetes（万寿菊属植物）属于另一个属，不能作为严格同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Pot marigold usually identifies Calendula officinalis and is the closest everyday equivalent. Marigold is broader and potentially ambiguous; Tagetes refers to a different genus and is not an exact synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 calendar（日历）旁月月出现的金色花朵，联想到花期长的 calendula（金盏花）。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture golden flowers beside every month of a calendar: calendula has a long flowering season.

senses.english_definition: A cantonment is a camp or an area where soldiers are housed, sometimes as part of a permanent military settlement.
senses.collocation_zh: 军事营地；驻军区
senses.sentence_en: The regiment was stationed in a cantonment outside the city.
senses.sentence_zh: 该团驻扎在城外的一处军营里。

etymology_story.zh: 该词借自法语 cantonnement，源自动词 cantonner，意为把军队分配到指定地区驻扎。其基础词 canton 指地区或分区，因此词义从分区安置军队的做法发展为军队驻地本身。
etymology_story.en: The word was borrowed from French cantonnement, from cantonner, meaning to quarter troops in assigned districts. Its base, canton, means a district or division, so the meaning developed from the quartering of troops to the place where they are housed.

morphology_enriched.zh: 可分析为 canton（使军队分区驻扎，现代较少用的动词）+ -ment（表示行为、结果或相关处所的名词后缀）→ cantonment；整个词在历史上借自法语。相关词族：canton（行政区；使驻扎）、cantonal（州或行政区的）、cantoned（已分区驻扎的）、cantoning（分区驻扎）、cantonments（驻军区，复数）。
morphology_enriched.en: The word can be analyzed as canton, a now uncommon verb meaning to quarter troops, + -ment, a noun-forming suffix denoting an action, result, or associated place; historically, the whole word was borrowed from French. Related forms include canton, a district or the verb; cantonal, relating to a canton; cantoned; cantoning; and the plural cantonments.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: military camp（军营）泛指军队营地，常可为临时设施；barracks（兵营）侧重士兵居住的建筑；garrison（驻军；驻防地）侧重驻守部队或其据点。Cantonment 尤其强调供军队集中住宿的区域，在南亚英语中常指正式驻军区。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Military camp is a broad term and may describe temporary facilities; barracks emphasizes soldiers' accommodation buildings; garrison emphasizes the troops stationed somewhere or their post. Cantonment particularly denotes an accommodation area and often refers to an established military district in South Asian English.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: canton（分区）+ -ment（处所）：划出一片区，让军队驻扎。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Canton means a district: set aside a district for troops, and you have a cantonment.

senses.english_definition: Cunnilingus is sexual activity in which someone uses their mouth or tongue to stimulate another person's vulva.

senses.sentence_zh: 这本教科书将舔阴定义为对外阴进行的口部刺激。

etymology_story.zh: 该词的拉丁语来源结合了 cunnus（外阴）与 lingere（舔）；拉丁语 cunnilingus 原本指实施这种行为的人。现代英语将该词用于行为本身，主要见于医学、性学及正式讨论。
etymology_story.en: The Latin source combines cunnus, meaning vulva, with lingere, meaning to lick; Latin cunnilingus originally referred to a person performing the act. Modern English uses the word for the activity itself, chiefly in medical, sexological, and formal discussion.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语将 cunnilingus 作为完整借入的不可数名词；历史词源可分析为 cunni-（与外阴有关的拉丁语成分）+ ling-（舔）+ -us（拉丁语词尾），这些成分不能直接当作普通英语词缀使用。相关形式有 cunnilinguist（实施舔阴的人，较少用）和 cunnilingual（与舔阴有关的，罕用）；常见词组为 perform cunnilingus（进行舔阴）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English treats cunnilingus as an intact borrowed uncountable noun. Its historical components are cunni-, relating to the vulva, ling-, relating to licking, and the Latin ending -us; these are not ordinary productive English affixes. Related forms include cunnilinguist, an uncommon term for a person performing the act, and cunnilingual, a rare adjective; perform cunnilingus is the usual verbal phrase.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: oral sex（口交）是上位词，也包括其他针对生殖器的口部刺激；oral stimulation of the vulva（对外阴的口部刺激）是准确的描述性对应表达；going down on someone（给某人口交）属于口语，具体所指依语境而定。Cunnilingus 是指向明确的正式术语。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Oral sex is a broader category that includes other forms of oral genital stimulation; oral stimulation of the vulva is an accurate descriptive equivalent; going down on someone is informal and depends on context for its precise meaning. Cunnilingus is the specific formal term.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 历史词根直指含义：cunni-（外阴）+ ling-（舔）→ 舔阴。
mnemonic_anchor.en: The historical roots state the meaning directly: cunni- refers to the vulva and ling- to licking.

senses.meaning_en: a palm-like gymnosperm with stiff leaves and reproductive cones
senses.english_definition: A cycad is a plant with a stout stem and a crown of stiff leaves that resembles a palm but belongs to a different group of seed plants.

etymology_story.zh: 该词来自植物学拉丁语属名 Cycas 的词干 Cycad-，其更早来源与希腊语中一种棕榈的名称有关。这个名称保留了外形上的联想，但苏铁类植物在植物分类上并不属于棕榈。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Cycad-, the stem associated with the botanical Latin genus name Cycas, ultimately connected with a Greek name for a kind of palm. The name preserves a resemblance in appearance, although cycads are botanically distinct from palms.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语将 cycad 作为不可再作普通英语构词拆分的基础名词；cycad + -s → cycads（复数），cycad + -like → cycad-like（像苏铁的）。专业相关词包括 cycadaceous（苏铁类的）和 cycadophyte（苏铁类植物）；Cycas（苏铁属）、Cycadales（苏铁目）和 Cycadaceae（苏铁科）是相关分类学名称，范围各不相同。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, cycad is a base noun without a productive internal English breakdown. Cycad + -s gives the plural cycads, and cycad + -like gives cycad-like. Specialist relatives include cycadaceous, meaning relating to cycads, and cycadophyte, a cycad plant; Cycas, Cycadales, and Cycadaceae are related taxonomic names for a genus, order, and family respectively.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: cycadophyte（苏铁类植物）是较专业的近义表达；sago palm（西米铁；俗称的苏铁）可指某些苏铁类植物，但也有其他用法，不能覆盖整个类群；palm（棕榈）只是在外形上相似，并非严格同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Cycadophyte is a more technical near-equivalent. Sago palm can name certain cycads but also has other uses and does not cover the whole group; palm describes a superficially similar plant from a different botanical group and is not an exact synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Cycad: palm-like shape, stiff leaves, and cones identify this distinct plant group.

etymology_story.zh: 源自拉丁语 decennialis，相关形式 decennium 表示“十年”，由 decem（十）和 annus（年）构成。英语保留了“十年”的核心概念，既可指每十年发生一次，也可指持续十年。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Latin decennialis, related to decennium, meaning 'ten years', from decem ('ten') and annus ('year'). English retains this ten-year idea in both recurrence and duration.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可分析为 decenn-（十年，黏着词干）+ -ial（形容词后缀）；decenn- 不是独立常用词。词族包括 decennially（每十年一次地），以及同源词 decennium、decennia／decenniums（十年及其复数）、decade（十年）；decennial 的低频名词用法表示十周年纪念或庆典。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern structure is decenn- ('ten years', a bound stem) + -ial (an adjective suffix); decenn- is not an ordinary independent word. The family includes decennially, alongside related decennium, its plurals decennia/decenniums, and decade; decennial also has an uncommon noun use for a tenth anniversary or its celebration.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: every ten years（每十年一次）明确说明发生频率；ten-year（十年的）通常说明持续时间或期限；decadal（十年尺度的）常见于科学语境，强调以十年为单位的变化或统计，并不必然表示每十年发生一次。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Every ten years explicitly expresses frequency; ten-year usually describes duration or a fixed term; decadal is common in scientific contexts for changes or measurements on a ten-year scale and does not necessarily imply recurrence.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: dec- 联想“十”，ann- 联想“年”：十个年头构成一个周期或时段。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect dec- with 'ten' and ann- with 'year': ten years make the cycle or period.

forms: 第三人称单数 demythologizes；过去式、过去分词 demythologized；现在分词 demythologizing。英式 -ise 形式同样成立。
family: myth 神话；mythologize 将……神话化。

morphology.text: de-（去除）+ mythologize（使神话化）→ demythologize（去除神话色彩）。

etymology.text: 英语用 de- 与 mythologize 构成；myth 一支来自希腊语 mythos（故事、神话）。可记成把故事外面的神话光环一层层拿掉。

usage_note: demythologize 常用于宗教、历史或公众形象分析，强调剥离神话成分；不必然表示整件事都是假的。英式也写 demythologise。

senses.meaning_zh: 对宗教文本或叙事作非神话化解释
senses.meaning_en: to interpret a religious text or narrative without treating its mythical elements as literal accounts
senses.english_definition: If you demythologize a religious text, you interpret its mythical elements to explain the meaning they convey rather than taking them literally.
senses.collocation_en: demythologize the New Testament; demythologize biblical narratives
senses.collocation_zh: 对《新约》作非神话化解释；对《圣经》叙事作非神话化解释
senses.sentence_en: Some theologians demythologize biblical narratives to explore their meaning for modern readers.
senses.sentence_zh: 一些神学家对《圣经》叙事作非神话化解释，以探讨其对现代读者的意义。

etymology_story.zh: 由 de-（去除）与 mythologize（使神话化）构成，myth 一支最终源于希腊语 mythos（故事、传说）。该词与二十世纪神学中的“非神话化”解释方法密切相关，后来也广泛用于破除对人物、历史或事物的神化。
etymology_story.en: It combines de- ('remove') with mythologize ('give a mythical character to'), with myth ultimately tracing to Greek mythos ('story' or 'tale'). Closely associated with twentieth-century theological interpretation, it also developed a broader use for challenging idealized accounts of people, history, or other subjects.

morphology_enriched.zh: 直接构词为 de-（去除）+ mythologize（使神话化）；进一步可识别 mytholog-（与神话、神话叙述有关的词干）+ -ize（动词后缀）。主要词族包括 demythologise（英式拼写变体）、demythologized／demythologised、demythologizing／demythologising、demythologization／demythologisation（非神话化）、demythologizer／demythologiser（进行非神话化解释的人）；基础词族包括 myth、mythic、mythical、mythically、mythology、mythological、mythologically、mythologist、mythologize／mythologise、mythologization／mythologisation。
morphology_enriched.en: The immediate structure is de- ('remove') + mythologize ('give a mythical character to'); mythologize can further be analyzed as mytholog- (a stem associated with myth or mythical narration) + -ize. Principal family forms include demythologise, demythologized/demythologised, demythologizing/demythologising, demythologization/demythologisation, and demythologizer/demythologiser; the base family includes myth, mythic, mythical, mythically, mythology, mythological, mythologically, mythologist, mythologize/mythologise, and mythologization/mythologisation.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: debunk（揭穿）侧重证明某种说法虚假；demystify（使通俗易懂、消除神秘感）侧重解释原本难懂的事物；dispel myths about（破除关于……的迷思）侧重纠正常见误解。demythologize 尤其强调剥去神话式或理想化叙述，也可用于不否定宗教意义的文本解释。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Debunk emphasizes exposing a claim as false; demystify emphasizes making something understandable; dispel myths about emphasizes correcting common misconceptions. Demythologize particularly targets mythical or idealized narratives and can describe interpretation that preserves religious significance.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: de- 表示“去掉”：拿掉神话光环，看清真实面貌或深层意义。
mnemonic_anchor.en: De- means 'remove': take away the mythical halo to reveal reality or underlying meaning.

senses.sentence_en: The researchers detected dieldrin residues in the soil.

etymology_story.zh: 这是二十世纪形成的化学名称，为纪念化学家 Otto Diels 而命名；相关合成化学涉及以他和 Kurt Alder 命名的 Diels–Alder 反应。dieldrin 的名称纪念 Diels，而相关杀虫剂 aldrin 的名称纪念 Alder。
etymology_story.en: This twentieth-century chemical name honors the chemist Otto Diels; the relevant synthetic chemistry involves the Diels–Alder reaction, named after Diels and Kurt Alder. Dieldrin commemorates Diels, while the related insecticide aldrin commemorates Alder.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常把 dieldrin 视为不可再作常规构词拆分的化学名词，不把词尾硬解为具有稳定意义的普通后缀。没有常用的派生词族；专业复合形式包括 dieldrin-resistant（对狄氏剂有抗性的）、dieldrin-treated（经狄氏剂处理的）和 dieldrin-contaminated（受狄氏剂污染的）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, dieldrin is normally treated as an unanalyzed chemical noun, rather than divided into ordinary productive affixes. It has no common derivational family; technical compounds include dieldrin-resistant, dieldrin-treated, and dieldrin-contaminated.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: HEOD 是狄氏剂的另一化学名称或简称。aldrin（艾氏剂）和 endrin（异狄氏剂）只是相关化合物，并非近义词：前者可转化为狄氏剂，后者是狄氏剂的立体异构体；organochlorine insecticide（有机氯杀虫剂）则是上位类别。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: HEOD is an alternative chemical designation for dieldrin. Aldrin and endrin are related compounds, not synonyms: aldrin can be converted into dieldrin, while endrin is a stereoisomer of dieldrin; organochlorine insecticide names the broader category.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: Diels 对应 dieldrin，Alder 对应 aldrin：用两位化学家的姓氏区分两个名称。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Pair Diels with dieldrin and Alder with aldrin: the chemists' surnames distinguish the two names.

etymology_story.zh: 源自拉丁语 expectorare，原义涉及“从胸中排出”，由 ex-（向外）与 pectus、词干 pector-（胸）构成。英语将其用于从呼吸道咳出痰液，也可较正式地表示吐痰或吐唾液。
etymology_story.en: It comes from Latin expectorare, expressing the idea of expelling something from the chest, from ex- ('out') and pectus, with the stem pector- ('chest'). English uses it for coughing up respiratory mucus and, more formally, for spitting out phlegm or saliva.

morphology_enriched.zh: 可分析为 ex-（向外）+ pector-（胸，黏着词根）+ -ate（动词后缀）。主要词族包括 expectorates、expectorated、expectorating、expectoration（咳痰；吐痰；咳出的物质）、expectorant（祛痰药；祛痰的）；同根词 pectoral 表示“胸部的”或“胸肌”。
morphology_enriched.en: The structure is ex- ('out') + pector- ('chest', a bound root) + -ate (a verb suffix). Principal family members include expectorates, expectorated, expectorating, expectoration, and expectorant, which can be a noun for a medicine or an adjective describing its action; the related word pectoral refers to the chest or a chest muscle.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: cough up（咳出）是描述咳出痰液的日常说法；spit（吐）范围更广，也可指吐唾液或食物；hawk up（用力清嗓咳出）强调清嗓排痰的动作，语气较口语化。expectorate 属正式或医学用语。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Cough up is the everyday expression for bringing up phlegm by coughing; spit is broader and can involve saliva or food; hawk up emphasizes forcefully clearing phlegm from the throat and is more colloquial. Expectorate is formal or medical.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: ex- 向外 + pector- 胸：把胸中的痰咳出来。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Ex- means 'out' and pector- means 'chest': cough material out from the chest.

etymology_story.zh: 中古英语已有相关形式，通常追溯到表示“有酒桶味”的盎格鲁法语词，与 fust（木头、木桶）有关。含义从木桶或久闭物品的陈腐气味，扩展为思想、风格或机构的古板陈旧。
etymology_story.en: Middle English forms are generally traced to an Anglo-French word meaning 'tasting of the cask', associated with fust ('wood' or 'cask'). The meaning expanded from a stale smell associated with casks or enclosed objects to old-fashioned ideas, styles, and institutions.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代以整词 fusty 为基础，不把历史成分 fust 当作常用独立词来套用构词规则。主要词族为 fustier（比较级）、fustiest（最高级）、fustiness（霉味；陈旧古板）和较少见的 fustily（带霉味地；古板地）；这些形式均将词尾 y 变为 i 后接相应后缀。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern word formation starts from the whole adjective fusty; the historical element fust should not be treated as an ordinary independent base. Principal family forms are fustier, fustiest, fustiness, and the less common adverb fustily; each changes final y to i before adding its suffix.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: musty（有霉味的）最接近其气味义，常让人想到潮湿或霉菌；stale（不新鲜的、陈腐的）范围更广，可形容空气、食物或想法；stuffy（闷的、古板的）既可指空气不流通，也可指拘谨守旧。fusty 常带“久置积尘、跟不上时代”的负面联想。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Musty is closest to the smell sense and often suggests dampness or mold; stale is broader, covering air, food, or ideas that have lost freshness; stuffy can describe poor ventilation or rigid conventionality. Fusty often carries an unfavorable suggestion of dusty age and failure to keep up with change.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 久闭木桶有陈味，久不更新的观念有“旧味”：从霉味联想到守旧。
mnemonic_anchor.en: An unopened old cask smells stale; ideas left unchanged feel stale too: move from musty smell to outdated thinking.

etymology_story.zh: 该词经中古英语传自古英语 hassuc，早期指莎草或密生的草墩。后来，其厚实、隆起的形象延伸为供跪、坐或搁脚用的垫子。

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 hassock 是不可再作常规拆分的词干，不宜拆成 has + sock。屈折形式：hassocks（复数）；派生词：hassock + -y → hassocky（草墩密布的，较少用），保留的是草丛义。

synonyms_and_nuances.en: Cushion is a broad term that does not specifically imply kneeling; footstool emphasizes support for the feet and need not be padded; tussock matches the grassy-clump sense rather than the furniture senses.

etymology_story.zh: 该词是二十世纪的技术用语，由希腊语来源的 hexa-（六）与拉丁语来源的 decimal（十进制的）组合而成。名称以“六加十”表示十六，后来广泛用于计算机领域。
etymology_story.en: This twentieth-century technical term combines Greek-derived hexa-, meaning six, with Latin-derived decimal. The name expresses sixteen as six plus ten and became widely used in computing.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词：hexa-（六）+ decimal（十进制的）→ hexadecimal；decimal 可进一步联系 decim-（十、十分之一）与 -al（形容词后缀）。词族与形式：hexadecimal（形容词及名词）、hexadecimals（可数名词复数）、hexadecimally（以十六进制方式）；hex 是计算机语境中的简称。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: hexa- 'six' + decimal → hexadecimal; decimal contains the bound element decim-, associated with ten or a tenth, and adjectival -al. Forms include hexadecimal as adjective and noun, the count-noun plural hexadecimals, the adverb hexadecimally, and the computing abbreviation hex.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: base-16（十六进制的）直接说明基数，数学表达最明确；hex（十六进制）是程序员常用简称，语体较简略。两者在相应技术语境中都可与 hexadecimal 对应。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Base-16 states the numerical base explicitly and is especially clear in mathematical explanations; hex is the shorter form commonly used by programmers. Both can correspond to hexadecimal in suitable technical contexts.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: hexa 六 + decimal 十 → 十六；0–9 后再接 A–F。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Six plus ten gives sixteen: after 0–9, add A–F.

etymology_story.zh: 该词经盎格鲁法语及中古英语传自拉丁语 manumittere，由 manus（手）与 mittere（放开、送出）构成。其含义是将人从奴隶主的控制中释放出来。
etymology_story.en: The word passed through Anglo-French and Middle English from Latin manumittere, formed from manus 'hand' and mittere 'let go or send'. It refers to releasing an enslaved person from an owner's control.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中以 manumit 为完整动词词干；manu-（手）+ mit（放开）适合作历史词根分析，不是自由组合的现代构词。屈折形式：manumits、manumitted、manumitting，后两者双写 t；相关词族：manumission（释放奴隶）、manumitter（释放奴隶者）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English treats manumit as a complete verb stem; manu- 'hand' + mit 'let go' is a historical root analysis rather than freely productive modern formation. Inflections are manumits, manumitted, and manumitting, with doubled t in the latter two; related family members include manumission and manumitter.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: free（释放）适用范围最广；liberate（解放）突出摆脱压迫或控制后的自由；emancipate（解放、使获得自主权）常涉及法律或社会身份。manumit 则专指使人摆脱奴隶身份。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Free has the broadest application; liberate emphasizes freedom from oppression or control; emancipate often concerns legal or social independence. Manumit specifically concerns release from slavery.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: manu 手 + mit 放开 → 从奴隶主的掌控中放出来。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Hand plus let go: release someone from an enslaver's control.

etymology_story.zh: 该词经中古英语 marmusette 传自中古法语 marmoset，后者曾指怪诞的小形象。它进一步与拟声性的 marmouser（含混地说话、咕哝）有关，后来成为这类小猴的名称。
etymology_story.en: The word came through Middle English marmusette from Middle French marmoset, which referred to a grotesque little figure. It is further connected with imitative marmouser 'to mumble' and later became a name for these small monkeys.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 marmoset 是不可再作常规拆分的词干，不能把结尾直接当作现代后缀 -et。复数为 marmosets；marmoset-like（像狨猴的）是可按需构造的描述性复合形容词，并非常用的固定派生词；本词没有广泛使用的直接派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, marmoset is an unanalyzed stem; its ending should not simply be treated as a productive modern suffix -et. The plural is marmosets; marmoset-like is a possible descriptive compound rather than a common established derivative, and the word has no widely used family of direct derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 本词没有两个完全等义的常用单词。marmoset monkey（狨猴）是解释性同义表达；monkey（猴）是范围更广的上位词；tamarin（柽柳猴）指近缘的另一类小猴，不能作为狨猴的严格同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There are not two common single-word equivalents. Marmoset monkey is an explanatory equivalent; monkey is a broader category; tamarin names a related group of small monkeys and is not an exact synonym.

etymology_story.zh: 该词源于十九世纪的新拉丁语医学命名，组合了表示“肌肉”的希腊语来源构词成分与希腊语 kardia（心）。它据此命名心壁中的肌肉层。
etymology_story.en: The term originated in nineteenth-century New Latin medical terminology, combining a Greek-derived element meaning muscle with Greek kardia 'heart'. It names the muscular layer of the heart wall.

morphology_enriched.zh: 医学构词分析：myo-（肌肉）+ cardi-（心）+ -um（新拉丁语名词词尾）→ myocardium。复数为 myocardia；相关词族包括 myocardial（心肌的）、myocardially（在心肌方面或经心肌，较少用）、myocarditis（心肌炎）及 myocarditic（心肌炎的）；cardiomyopathy（心肌病）是使用相同核心词根的相关构词。
morphology_enriched.en: Medical formation: myo- 'muscle' + cardi- 'heart' + New Latin noun ending -um → myocardium. The plural is myocardia; related forms include myocardial, the uncommon adverb myocardially, myocarditis 'inflammation of the heart muscle', and myocarditic. Cardiomyopathy is a related formation using the same core roots.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: heart muscle（心肌）是最自然的通俗对应表达；cardiac muscle（心肌组织）强调肌肉组织的类型；myocardial tissue（心肌组织）强调该层的组织成分。myocardium 则明确指心壁的解剖学肌层。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Heart muscle is the natural plain-language equivalent; cardiac muscle emphasizes the type of muscle tissue; myocardial tissue emphasizes tissue belonging to this layer. Myocardium specifically names the anatomical muscular layer of the heart wall.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: myo 肌肉 + cardi 心 → 心脏负责收缩泵血的肌肉层。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Muscle plus heart: the contracting muscle layer that pumps blood.

etymology_story.zh: 源自拉丁语短语 in octavo，意为“以第八份的形式”，其中 octavo 是 octavus（第八）的屈折形式。传统印刷中，一张印张折三次成为八叶、十六页，名称由此指这种书籍规格及相应书本。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Latin in octavo, meaning 'in an eighth,' with octavo an inflected form of octavus, 'eighth.' In traditional printing, folding a sheet three times produces eight leaves, or sixteen pages, giving the format and its books their name.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中视为整体借词，不宜机械拆成英语词根和词缀；历史上与拉丁语 octo（八）相关。常用相关形式：octavos（名词复数）、octavo-sized（八开本大小的）、octavo-format（八开规格的，复合修饰语）；书目缩写为 8vo。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, octavo is a whole borrowed word rather than a productive combination of English roots and affixes; historically, it is related to Latin octo, 'eight.' Related forms include octavos, the plural, and the compound modifiers octavo-sized and octavo-format; its bibliographical abbreviation is 8vo.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 8vo 是 octavo 的书目缩写；octavo format（八开规格）明确指开本；octavo volume（八开本书）明确指实体书。它们都不能直接理解为某个固定厘米尺寸，因为原始印张的大小可以不同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: 8vo is the bibliographical abbreviation of octavo; octavo format explicitly names the format, while octavo volume identifies a physical book. None specifies a single fixed measurement, because the original sheets can differ in size.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“八”：一张纸折成八叶，正反合计十六页。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor it to eight: one sheet becomes eight leaves, with sixteen pages counting both sides.

etymology_story.zh: 借自意大利语 pianoforte，由 piano（轻声、弱）和 forte（响亮、强）组成，源于强调这种乐器能奏出强弱变化的早期名称。英语后来通常将其简称为 piano。
etymology_story.en: Borrowed from Italian, pianoforte combines piano, 'soft,' and forte, 'loud,' reflecting early names that emphasized the instrument's ability to produce contrasting dynamics. English later generally shortened the name to piano.

morphology_enriched.zh: 来源语言中的构词为 piano（弱）+ forte（强）；现代英语通常把 pianoforte 作为完整乐器名称使用。相关形式：pianofortes（复数）、piano（常用简称）、pianos（其复数）、pianist（钢琴演奏者）、pianistic（钢琴演奏的）、pianism（钢琴演奏技艺）；后三者属于相关词族，并非直接在完整的 pianoforte 后加后缀。
morphology_enriched.en: The source-language formation is piano, 'soft,' + forte, 'loud'; modern English normally treats pianoforte as a complete instrument name. Related forms include pianofortes, piano, pianos, pianist, pianistic, and pianism; the last three belong to the associated word family rather than being formed by adding suffixes to the full word pianoforte.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: piano（钢琴）是现代日常用语中的直接同义词；grand piano（三角钢琴）和 upright piano（立式钢琴）分别指两种结构类型，范围均小于 pianoforte。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Piano is the direct synonym used in everyday modern English. Grand piano and upright piano name particular structural types, so each is narrower in meaning than pianoforte.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: piano“弱”＋forte“强”：能轻弹，也能强奏的钢琴。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Piano means soft and forte means loud: remember a keyboard instrument that can play both.

etymology_story.zh: 英语由地区名 Silesia 加表示归属或来源的后缀构成，先表示“西里西亚的”，也用于称呼当地人和当地语言。Silesia 是该地区的拉丁化名称，其更早来源存在争议。
etymology_story.en: English formed Silesian from the regional name Silesia with a suffix expressing origin or association, using it for the region's characteristics, inhabitants, and speech. Silesia is a Latinized regional name whose more remote origin is disputed.

morphology_enriched.zh: Silesia 去词尾 -a，再加 -an → Silesian；也可将拼写关系表示为 Silesi- + -an。相关形式：Silesia（西里西亚）、Silesian（形容词或名词）、Silesians（指人的名词复数）、Upper Silesian（上西里西亚的／人）、Lower Silesian（下西里西亚的／人）；这些地名派生形式均保留大写字母。
morphology_enriched.en: Remove the final -a from Silesia and add -an to form Silesian, giving the spelling structure Silesi- + -an. Related forms include Silesia, Silesian, the personal plural Silesians, Upper Silesian, and Lower Silesian; these geographical forms retain their initial capitals.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: of Silesia（西里西亚的）是形容词义的释义性替换，inhabitant of Silesia（西里西亚居民）可解释指人的名词义。Upper Silesian（上西里西亚的／人）范围更窄；Polish（波兰的／人）和 German（德国的／人）不能作为通用同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Of Silesia paraphrases the adjective, and inhabitant of Silesia explains the personal noun. Upper Silesian is geographically narrower; Polish and German are not interchangeable synonyms for Silesian.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: Silesia 是地名，-an 把它连到“当地的、当地人”；语言义再由语境判断。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with the place Silesia: -an connects it to its people and characteristics, while context identifies the speech variety.

etymology_story.zh: 由英语 thick（厚实、密集）和 set（安置、排列；构成）复合而成，两个成分都具有古英语渊源。“紧密排列”的概念也用于描述身体紧凑、宽厚结实的外形。
etymology_story.en: Thickset combines English thick, meaning substantial or dense, with set, referring to placement or arrangement; both elements have Old English ancestry. The idea of close arrangement also describes a compact, broad, solid bodily build.

morphology_enriched.zh: thick + set → thickset，是复合形容词；这里 set 与动词 set 的过去分词形式相同。相关形式：thick（厚的；密的）、thickly（厚厚地；密集地）、thickness（厚度；浓密程度）、thicken（变厚；使变浓）；这些属于 thick 的相关词族，thickset 本身没有常用的直接派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Thick + set forms the compound adjective thickset; set has the same form as the past participle of the verb set. Related words in the thick family include thick, thickly, thickness, and thicken, but thickset itself has no widely used direct derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: stocky（敦实的）最接近，强调身体短而宽、结实紧凑；sturdy（结实的）强调强健稳固，不一定矮壮；在植物义中，dense（茂密的）强调生长紧密。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Stocky is closest for a short, broad, compact build; sturdy emphasizes strength and solidity without necessarily implying that shape. For vegetation, dense emphasizes closely packed growth.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: thick“厚实”＋set“排列成形”：人长得敦实，植物长得密实。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think 'thickly set': a body built compactly, or plants packed closely together.

morphology.text: 来源语言中的复合：aard（地）+ vark（猪）→ aardvark（土豚）；在现代英语中作为独立词素记忆。

etymology.text: 从早期南非荷兰语借入，来自表示“地”的 aarde 与表示“猪”的 vark。这个名称像“住地洞的猪”，但土豚并不是猪。

etymology_story.zh: 借自南非荷兰语，即南非语的前身，名称由表示“土地”的 aard 和表示“猪”的 vark 组成，字面意思是“土猪”。它因掘土习性和似猪的外形得名，但并不属于猪科。
etymology_story.en: The word was borrowed from South African Dutch, the predecessor of Afrikaans, combining aard, 'earth,' and vark, 'pig.' The name reflects the animal's digging habits and piglike appearance, although it does not belong to the pig family.

morphology_enriched.zh: 来源语言中的构词为 aard（土地）+ vark（猪）；现代英语中通常作为整体借词处理，不能把这两个成分当作常用英语词素。aardvarks 是规则复数；aardvark burrow（土豚洞穴）等是名词组合，本词没有常用的直接派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: The source-language structure is aard, 'earth,' + vark, 'pig'; modern English normally treats it as a whole borrowing rather than a combination of productive English elements. Aardvarks is the regular plural; expressions such as aardvark burrow are noun combinations, and the word has no widely used direct derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: antbear（蚁熊）和 earth pig（土猪）是较少见的别称，其中 antbear 也可能指其他食蚁哺乳动物；Orycteropus afer 是土豚的科学名称，指称最精确。anteater（食蚁兽）通常指另一类动物，不能作为严格同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Antbear and earth pig are less common alternative names, though antbear can also refer to other ant-eating mammals. Orycteropus afer is the precise scientific name; anteater usually names a different group of animals and is not an exact synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Earth + pig: picture a piglike African mammal digging into the ground.

etymology_story.zh: 英语借自俄语 агитпроп，这是表示“鼓动”与“宣传”的两个俄语词的缩合形式，曾用于苏联共产党的鼓动宣传部门名称。英语中的含义后来扩展到服务于政治宣传的戏剧、电影及其他文艺作品。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed Russian agitprop, a shortened combination of the Russian words for agitation and propaganda that was used for the Soviet Communist Party's agitation and propaganda department. Its English meaning broadened to include plays, films, and other artistic works serving political propaganda.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常作为整体借词使用；其俄语内部结构为 agit-（鼓动）+ prop-（宣传），不是英语 agent 或 proper 的缩写。词族包括名词及形容词 agitprop，以及较少见的 agitpropist（政治宣传鼓动者）；agitation（鼓动）、agitator（鼓动者）和 propaganda（宣传）是相关词，不是由 agitprop 派生的词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, agitprop is generally treated as a whole borrowed word; its internal Russian structure is agit- 'agitation' + prop- 'propaganda,' not abbreviations of English agent or proper. Its family includes the noun and adjective agitprop and the less common agitpropist; agitation, agitator, and propaganda are related words rather than derivatives of agitprop.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: propaganda（宣传）范围更广，不限于文艺形式；agitation（鼓动）侧重动员公众采取政治行动；political theatre（政治戏剧）可指探讨政治的戏剧，不一定具有 agitprop 那样直接的宣传目的。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Propaganda is broader and need not use artistic forms; agitation emphasizes mobilizing people for political action; political theatre may explore politics without the direct persuasive purpose associated with agitprop.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 鼓动 + 宣传：让政治主张登上舞台。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Agitation + propaganda: political ideas put on stage.

etymology_story.zh: alveoli 是 alveolus 的拉丁式复数；alveolus 来自拉丁语 alveus（槽、空腔）的指小形式，意为“小空腔”。解剖学借用这一名称来指肺泡、牙槽等微小腔隙。
etymology_story.en: Alveoli is the Latin plural of alveolus, a diminutive of Latin alveus, meaning a trough or cavity. Anatomy adopted the term for small cavities such as the air sacs of the lungs and the sockets of teeth.

morphology_enriched.zh: alveol-（小腔词干）+ -i（拉丁式复数词尾）→ alveoli；单数 alveolus 的 -us 替换为 -i。主要词族包括 alveolus（单个肺泡或牙槽）、alveolar（肺泡的；牙槽的）、alveolate（具有小窝的）、alveolation（形成小腔或小窝）、alveolitis（肺泡炎或牙槽炎）和 alveoloplasty（牙槽成形术）。
morphology_enriched.en: Alveol- 'small cavity' + the Latin plural ending -i forms alveoli; the singular ending -us in alveolus is replaced by -i. The main word family includes alveolus, alveolar, alveolate 'having small cavities,' alveolation 'the formation of small cavities,' alveolitis 'inflammation of lung alveoli or dental sockets,' and alveoloplasty 'surgical reshaping of the alveolar ridge.'

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: air sacs（气囊）可通俗解释肺泡，但也指其他含气结构；tooth sockets（牙槽）仅对应牙科义；cavities（空腔）是更宽泛的结构名称，不能在具体解剖语境中随意替换 alveoli。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Air sacs is a plain-language equivalent for lung alveoli but also describes other air-containing structures; tooth sockets matches only the dental sense; cavities is much broader and cannot freely replace alveoli in anatomical descriptions.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 一颗 alveolus，许多 alveoli：肺里小气囊，颌骨小牙窝。
mnemonic_anchor.en: One alveolus, many alveoli: tiny air sacs in lungs or tiny tooth sockets in jaws.

etymology_story.zh: apoptotic 派生自现代生物学术语 apoptosis，后者借自希腊语 apoptōsis，意为“脱落”，可用于描述树叶或花瓣的落下。生物学借此形象命名细胞有序死亡的过程。
etymology_story.en: Apoptotic derives from the modern biological term apoptosis, borrowed from Greek apoptōsis, meaning 'a falling off,' as of leaves or petals. Biology adopted this image to name an orderly process of cell death.

morphology_enriched.zh: apoptot-（与 apoptosis 对应的形容词构词词干）+ -ic（……的）→ apoptotic，不能机械分析为完整的 apoptosis + -ic。主要词族包括 apoptosis（细胞凋亡）、apoptotic（凋亡的）、apoptotically（以凋亡方式）、proapoptotic／pro-apoptotic（促凋亡的）、antiapoptotic／anti-apoptotic（抗凋亡的）和 nonapoptotic／non-apoptotic（非凋亡的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Apoptot-, the adjective-forming stem corresponding to apoptosis, combines with -ic to form apoptotic; the word is not formed by simply adding -ic to the complete noun apoptosis. The main family includes apoptosis, apoptotic, apoptotically, proapoptotic/pro-apoptotic, antiapoptotic/anti-apoptotic, and nonapoptotic/non-apoptotic.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: dying（正在死亡的）含义宽泛，不说明死亡机制；programmed（程序性的，用于细胞死亡语境）涵盖范围可能比 apoptotic 更广；necrotic（坏死的）是相关对比词而非近义词，指另一类细胞或组织死亡。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Dying is broader and does not identify the mechanism; programmed, when describing cell death, can cover processes beyond apoptosis; necrotic is a contrasting related term rather than a synonym and describes a different form of cell or tissue death.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 像叶片自然脱落：细胞有序退出。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Like a leaf falling away: a cell makes an orderly exit.

etymology_story.zh: brickbat 由 brick（砖）和表示“块、碎片”的 bat 复合而成，最初指碎砖块。由于碎砖可以被扔向他人，这个词后来引申为像投掷物一样袭来的尖刻批评。
etymology_story.en: Brickbat combines brick with bat in the sense of a lump or fragment and originally meant a piece of broken brick. Because such pieces could be thrown at people, the word developed a figurative sense of harsh verbal attacks.

morphology_enriched.zh: brick（砖）+ bat（块、碎片）→ brickbat，是透明度较低的名词复合词，因为 bat 的这一含义在现代英语中并不常见。常用词形为单数 brickbat 和复数 brickbats，没有常用的派生词族。

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: criticism（批评）最中性，可具有建设性；insult（侮辱）侧重冒犯或贬低个人；barb（尖刻的话）通常简短而带讥刺意味，brickbat 则更突出猛烈、直接的攻击。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Criticism is neutral and may be constructive; an insult primarily offends or demeans a person; a barb is usually a brief, pointed, often witty remark, while a brickbat suggests a forceful and direct attack.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 嘴里扔出的碎砖，就是尖刻批评。

etymology_story.zh: 该词来自新拉丁语属名 Campylobacter，由源于希腊语 kampylos（弯曲的）的成分和表示“杆菌”的命名成分组成。这个名称描述了这类细菌弯曲的杆状外形。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from the New Latin genus name Campylobacter, combining an element from Greek kampylos 'curved' with a bacterial naming element meaning 'rod.' The name describes the bacteria's curved, rodlike shape.

morphology_enriched.zh: campylo-（弯曲的）+ -bacter（杆菌）→ campylobacter；这是科学构词成分的组合，不是普通英语自由词根的组合。主要词族包括 campylobacter（弯曲杆菌）、复数 campylobacters、campylobacterial（弯曲杆菌的）及 campylobacteriosis（弯曲杆菌病）；正式属名写作首字母大写的 Campylobacter。
morphology_enriched.en: Campylo- 'curved' + -bacter 'rod-shaped bacterium' forms campylobacter through scientific combining forms rather than ordinary independent English roots. The main family includes campylobacter, plural campylobacters, campylobacterial, and campylobacteriosis 'infection caused by Campylobacter'; the formal genus name is capitalized as Campylobacter.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: bacterium（细菌）是更宽泛的上位词；germ（病菌）是日常泛称，不表示确切分类；pathogen（病原体）按致病能力分类，也包括病毒、真菌等。这些词都不是 campylobacter 的严格同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Bacterium is the broader biological category; germ is an informal general term without precise classification; pathogen identifies an organism or agent by its ability to cause disease and also includes viruses and fungi. None is an exact synonym for campylobacter.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: campylo- 弯曲 + -bacter 杆菌：一根弯弯的小菌杆。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Campylo- means curved and -bacter means rod: picture a tiny bent bacterial rod.

etymology_story.zh: 源自拉丁语 coniunctus，即 coniungere（连接、结合）的过去分词；该动词由表示“一起”的 con- 和表示“连接”的 iungere 构成。“连接在一起”的基本意义后来发展出音乐中的级进、逻辑中的合取项和语法中的并列项等专门用法。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Latin coniunctus, the past participle of coniungere, meaning 'join together', formed from con- 'together' and iungere 'join'. The central idea of connection developed into specialized musical, logical, and grammatical uses.

morphology_enriched.zh: 学术词根分析：con-（一起）+ junct-（连接），没有独立的现代英语形容词后缀；junct- 是黏着词根。主要相关词族包括 conjunction（连接；连词；合取）、conjunctive（连接的；连接成分）、conjunctively（连接地）；对照词族有 disjunct（分离的；评注性状语）、disjunction（分离；析取）和 disjunctive（分离的；析取的），这些词并非全部由现代英语 conjunct 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Learned-root analysis: con- 'together' + junct- 'join', with no separate modern English adjective suffix; junct- is a bound root. The main related family includes conjunction, conjunctive, and conjunctively; contrasting relatives include disjunct, disjunction, and disjunctive. These are not all direct modern derivatives of conjunct.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 音乐义：stepwise 强调逐级移动，通常最接近 conjunct；connected 泛指相连，不限定音程；joint 强调共同参与或共同产生作用，只对应一般性的联合义。在语法和逻辑中，conjunct 是专门术语，不能随意替换成 conjunction。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: In music, stepwise is usually the closest equivalent because it emphasizes movement by adjacent scale degrees. Connected describes a broader relationship without specifying intervals, while joint emphasizes shared participation or action. In grammar and logic, conjunct is a technical term and is not interchangeable with conjunction.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: con-＝一起，junct-＝连接：音符逐级相接，命题和语法成分连接成组。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Con- means 'together' and junct- means 'join': notes connect by steps, while propositions and grammatical units connect into groups.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：decathlon + athlete → decathlete，是有重叠和截短的缩合词，不是两个完整单词直接相加。主要词族：decathlete（十项全能运动员）、decathletes（复数）、decathlon（十项全能比赛）、decathlons（复数）；相关基础词有 athlete（运动员）、athletic（运动的；健壮的）和 athletics（田径运动）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: decathlon + athlete → decathlete, a blend involving overlap and shortening rather than simple addition of two complete words. The main family comprises decathlete, decathletes, decathlon, and decathlons; related base vocabulary includes athlete, athletic, and athletics.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: combined-events athlete（全能项目运动员）范围较广，也包括七项全能等项目的选手；track-and-field athlete（田径运动员）范围更广；all-round athlete（全面型运动员）强调多方面运动能力，不一定参加正式的十项全能比赛。这些表达都不完全等同于 decathlete。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: A combined-events athlete may compete in the heptathlon or another combined event, while a track-and-field athlete belongs to a much broader category. An all-round athlete has varied sporting abilities but need not compete in the decathlon. None is an exact substitute for decathlete.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: deca-＝十，athlete＝运动员：参加十项比赛的运动员。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Deca- means 'ten': a decathlete is the athlete who tackles ten events.

morphology.text: deoxyribo-（来自 deoxyribose，脱氧核糖）+ nucleic（核酸的）→ deoxyribonucleic；常与 acid 连用。

etymology.text: 现代英语科学造词，组合 deoxyribose（脱氧核糖）与 nucleic（核的、核酸的）；nucleic 一支来自拉丁语 nucleus（核）。抓住脱氧核糖与核酸这两个部分。

usage_note: 几乎总在 deoxyribonucleic acid 中出现，即 DNA；ribonucleic acid 是 RNA，少了 deoxy- 所表达的脱氧区别。

senses.meaning_zh: 脱氧核糖核酸的；用于 deoxyribonucleic acid（DNA）
senses.meaning_en: designating the nucleic acid that contains deoxyribose
senses.english_definition: Deoxyribonucleic is used in the name deoxyribonucleic acid, or DNA, the substance that carries genetic information.
senses.collocation_zh: 脱氧核糖核酸；脱氧核糖核酸序列
senses.sentence_en: DNA stands for deoxyribonucleic acid.
senses.sentence_zh: DNA 是 deoxyribonucleic acid（脱氧核糖核酸）的缩写。

etymology_story.zh: 这是现代生物化学术语，由表示脱氧核糖的 deoxyribo- 与 nucleic 组合而成；nucleic 最终来自拉丁语 nucleus（核、果仁）。名称体现了这种核酸含有脱氧核糖，也保留了核酸最初与细胞核研究相联系的命名历史。
etymology_story.en: This modern biochemical term combines deoxyribo-, referring to deoxyribose, with nucleic, ultimately from Latin nucleus 'kernel or nucleus'. Its name identifies its sugar component and preserves the historical association of nucleic acids with research on cell nuclei.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代科学构词：deoxyribo-（脱氧核糖）+ nucleic（核酸的）；deoxyribo- 来自 deoxyribose 去掉词尾 -se，nucleic 可分析为核相关词干 nucle- + -ic（……的）。主要相关词族：ribose（核糖）、deoxyribose（脱氧核糖）、ribonucleic acid（核糖核酸，RNA）、deoxyribonucleic acid（脱氧核糖核酸，DNA）、deoxyribonucleotide（脱氧核糖核苷酸）、deoxyribonucleoside（脱氧核糖核苷）、deoxyribonuclease（脱氧核糖核酸酶，DNase）；这些是共享成分的相关术语，并非全部由本形容词直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern scientific formation: deoxyribo- 'deoxyribose' + nucleic; deoxyribo- comes from deoxyribose with the ending -se removed, while nucleic contains the nucleus-related stem nucle- and adjectival -ic. Major related terms include ribose, deoxyribose, ribonucleic acid (RNA), deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA), deoxyribonucleotide, deoxyribonucleoside, and deoxyribonuclease (DNase). These share components rather than all being direct derivatives of this adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 本形容词没有常用的独立同义词。完整名称 deoxyribonucleic acid 可简称 DNA；genetic material（遗传物质）是功能性上位表达，在某些病毒中也可指 RNA；nucleic acid（核酸）是包含 DNA 和 RNA 的上位类别。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: The adjective has no common independent synonym. The complete name deoxyribonucleic acid is abbreviated DNA. Genetic material is a broader functional description that can include RNA in some viruses, while nucleic acid is the broader chemical category containing both DNA and RNA.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 脱氧糖＋核酸：DNA 的糖是脱氧核糖，比 RNA 的核糖少一个氧原子。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Deoxy sugar + nucleic acid: DNA contains deoxyribose, whose sugar molecule has one fewer oxygen atom than ribose.

etymology.text: 国际科学词汇，用取自新拉丁语植物属名 Digitalis 的 dig- 与 toxin 缩合命名。把它和洋地黄这一植物名称联系起来记。

usage_note: digoxin 是特定药物的通用名，通常小写；本卡只辨识药名，不据此判断剂量或用药安排。

senses.meaning_en: a cardiac glycoside medicine used for certain heart conditions
senses.english_definition: Digoxin is a medicine used to treat certain heart conditions by increasing the force of heart contractions and slowing electrical conduction through part of the heart.

etymology_story.zh: Digoxin 是二十世纪形成的科学药物名称，与其植物来源毛花洋地黄（Digitalis lanata）相联系。它属于洋地黄强心苷命名体系，不应将词首误解为英语动词 dig（挖）。
etymology_story.en: Digoxin is a twentieth-century scientific drug name associated with its plant source, Digitalis lanata, the woolly foxglove. It belongs to the naming vocabulary of digitalis cardiac glycosides; its opening letters do not represent the English verb dig.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中宜将 digoxin 作为固定药名整体学习；dig- 与 Digitalis（洋地黄属）相联系，词尾 -in 常见于化学物质名称，不宜仅凭拼写将其确定为 dig + toxin 的缩合。相关专业词有 digoxigenin（地高辛配基）和 digoxin-like（类似地高辛的）；digitoxin（洋地黄毒苷）是相关但不同的药物，digitalis（洋地黄；洋地黄制剂）是来源相关词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, digoxin is best learned as a fixed drug name: dig- is associated with Digitalis, and -in is a familiar substance-name ending. Its spelling alone does not establish a blend of dig and toxin. Related technical vocabulary includes digoxigenin and digoxin-like; digitoxin names a related but different drug, while digitalis is a source-related term.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: digoxin 没有常用的精确通名同义词。cardiac glycoside（强心苷）是其所属药物类别；digitalis（洋地黄或洋地黄制剂）涵盖的来源和制剂更广；digitoxin（洋地黄毒苷）是另一种强心苷，不能作为 digoxin 的同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Digoxin has no common exact generic synonym. Cardiac glycoside names its drug class; digitalis refers more broadly to the plant or its medicinal preparations. Digitoxin is another cardiac glycoside and is not a synonym for digoxin.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 看到 digoxin，就联系 Digitalis 洋地黄：植物来源的强心苷。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link digoxin with Digitalis: a foxglove-derived cardiac glycoside.

senses.meaning_en: an instrument that records the brain's electrical activity
senses.english_definition: An electroencephalograph is a machine that records electrical activity in the brain through electrodes placed on the scalp.
senses.collocation_zh: 数字脑电图仪；多通道脑电图仪
senses.sentence_en: The electroencephalograph recorded changes in brain activity while she slept.
senses.sentence_zh: 脑电图仪记录了她睡眠期间脑部电活动的变化。

etymology_story.zh: 这是为记录脑部电活动而形成的现代科学复合词，组合了希腊语来源的 electro-（电）、encephalo-（脑）和 -graph（记录仪器）。其中 encephalo- 可追溯到希腊语 enkephalos（脑），原义与“头内之物”有关。
etymology_story.en: This modern scientific compound was formed to name an instrument for recording the brain's electrical activity, using Greek-derived electro- 'electricity', encephalo- 'brain', and -graph 'recording instrument'. Encephalo- traces back to Greek enkephalos 'brain', literally associated with what is inside the head.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：electro-（电）+ encephalo-（脑）+ -graph（记录仪器）。主要词族：electroencephalograph（脑电图仪）、electroencephalographs（复数）、electroencephalography（脑电图检查或记录技术）、electroencephalographic（脑电图检查的）、electroencephalographically（通过脑电图检查）、electroencephalographer（脑电图检查专业人员）、electroencephalogram（脑电图）；区分 -graph 仪器、-graphy 技术或过程、-gram 记录结果。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: electro- 'electricity' + encephalo- 'brain' + -graph 'recording instrument'. The main family includes electroencephalograph, electroencephalographs, electroencephalography, electroencephalographic, electroencephalographically, electroencephalographer, and electroencephalogram. Distinguish -graph for the instrument, -graphy for the technique or process, and -gram for the resulting record.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: EEG machine（脑电图机）是常用的同义表达；EEG recorder（脑电记录仪）强调记录功能；brain monitor（脑功能监测仪）范围更广，可指使用其他监测技术的设备。electroencephalogram 指记录得到的脑电图，不能与仪器名称混用。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: EEG machine is a common equivalent, while EEG recorder emphasizes the recording function. Brain monitor is broader and may describe equipment using other monitoring techniques. Electroencephalogram names the resulting record and should be distinguished from the instrument.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 电 electro-＋脑 encephalo-＋记录仪 -graph＝把脑部电活动记下来的机器。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Electricity + brain + recorder: the machine that writes down the brain's electrical activity.

senses.meaning_zh: 华而不实的衣饰；浮华的装饰物
senses.meaning_en: Showy clothing or decoration with little practical value.
senses.english_definition: Frippery is clothing or decoration that looks elaborate or attractive but is considered unnecessary or unimportant.

etymology_story.zh: 借自法语 friperie，原指旧衣或旧衣买卖，与表示磨损、弄坏的 friper 有关。英语中的词义由旧衣服发展为廉价而花哨的衣饰，再泛指华而不实的东西。
etymology_story.en: Borrowed from French friperie, originally referring to old clothes or the secondhand clothing trade, and related to friper, meaning to wear out or spoil. In English, the meaning developed from old clothing to cheap finery and then to superficial or unnecessary extras.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常将 frippery 作为整体词基识记，不宜把它分析为仍具生产力的 frip + -ery。常用形式有 frippery 和复数 fripperies；没有常用的直接派生词。frippery-free 是可以临时构成的透明复合形容词，意为“没有浮华装饰的”。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, frippery is normally treated as a whole base rather than as a productive combination of frip + -ery. Its usual forms are frippery and the plural fripperies; it has no common direct derivatives. Frippery-free is a transparent compound adjective that can be formed when needed, meaning free of showy extras.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: finery 指精致或华丽的衣饰，本身不一定含贬义；trappings 指身份、地位或活动的外在标志；frills 指非必需的附加装饰或功能。frippery 更强调这些东西浮华、琐碎或缺乏实际价值。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Finery means elaborate or elegant clothing and need not be disapproving; trappings are the outward signs associated with a position or activity; frills are optional decorative or functional extras. Frippery more strongly suggests showiness, triviality, or little practical value.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 沿词义变化记：旧衣买卖 → 廉价华服 → 华而不实的点缀。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Follow the semantic path: secondhand clothes → cheap finery → showy, unnecessary extras.
