etymology_story.zh: 英语借自法语 chinoiserie，由 chinois（中国的）和后缀 -erie 构成。它与欧洲对中国艺术和器物的兴趣密切相关，通常指欧洲人对中国风格的借鉴与想象，而非中国艺术本身的统称。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed chinoiserie from French, where it was formed from chinois, meaning Chinese, and the suffix -erie. The term developed around European interest in Chinese art and objects and usually describes European interpretations of Chinese style.

morphology_enriched.zh: 借词内部结构为 chinois（中国的）+ -erie（相关活动、风格或制品）；在现代英语中通常作为整体使用。复数为 chinoiseries；没有常用的英语派生词，置于 wallpaper 等名词前时通常仍是名词作定语。
morphology_enriched.en: The borrowed French structure is chinois, meaning Chinese, + -erie, a suffix associated with activities, styles, or products; modern English normally treats the word as a whole. Its plural is chinoiseries, and it has no common English derivatives; use before nouns such as wallpaper is normally attributive noun use.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Chinese-inspired decoration（受中国艺术启发的装饰）是接近的解释性表达，但范围更广；Chinese style（中国风格）也更宽泛，可指真正源自中国的风格。chinoiserie 特别强调欧洲装饰艺术中的中国风想象。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Chinese-inspired decoration is a close explanatory equivalent but has a broader scope; Chinese style is also broader and may describe styles originating in China itself. Chinoiserie specifically emphasizes European decorative interpretations of Chinese art.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住 chinois＝“中国的”：欧洲装饰中的“中国想象”，就是 chinoiserie。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor chinois to Chinese: chinoiserie is China as imagined in European decoration.

senses.meaning_zh: 血亲关系；因具有共同祖先而形成的血缘关系
senses.meaning_en: A blood relationship resulting from shared ancestry.
senses.english_definition: Consanguinity is the relationship between people who have one or more ancestors in common.

etymology_story.zh: 该词源自拉丁语 consanguinitas，相关形容词 consanguineus 意为“同血统的”，由 con-（共同）和 sanguis（血，词干 sanguin-）构成。“共同的血”由此成为共同祖先及血亲关系的表达。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Latin consanguinitas, related to consanguineus, meaning of the same blood, formed from con-, meaning together, and sanguis, meaning blood, with the stem sanguin-. Shared blood thus became an expression for common ancestry and blood relationship.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代学术构词可分析为 con-（共同）+ sanguin-（血）+ -ity（状态或关系）；这是对继承借词的结构分析。主要词族有 consanguineous（有血亲关系的）、consanguineal（血亲的）、consanguine（血亲的，较少见）及 consanguineously（以血亲关系，少见）。
morphology_enriched.en: Its learned morphological structure is con-, meaning shared, + sanguin-, meaning blood, + -ity, marking a state or relationship; this analyzes an inherited borrowing. Principal family members are consanguineous and consanguineal, meaning related by blood, the less common adjective consanguine, and the rare adverb consanguineously.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: blood relationship（血缘关系）是最直接的日常对应表达；kinship（亲属关系）范围更广，也可包括婚姻、收养或社会认可形成的亲属联系。consanguinity 是强调共同祖先的正式术语。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Blood relationship is the closest everyday equivalent; kinship is broader and can include relationships established through marriage, adoption, or social recognition. Consanguinity is a formal term specifically emphasizing shared ancestry.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: con-＝共同，sanguin-＝血：共同祖先，连成血亲。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Con- means shared and sanguin- means blood: shared ancestry creates a blood relationship.

etymology_story.zh: Cripes 是感叹用法 Christ 的委婉变音形式，用替代读音减轻直接呼喊宗教名称的冒犯意味。它后来固定为表达惊讶或懊恼的非正式感叹词。
etymology_story.en: Cripes developed as a euphemistic alteration of Christ used as an exclamation, softening the perceived offensiveness of invoking a religious name. It became an informal expression of surprise or annoyance.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 cripes 是不可进一步作常规词缀拆分的感叹词；词尾 -s 不是复数标记。它由 Christ 委婉变音而来，没有常用派生词；Christian 等属于 Christ 的词族，并非 cripes 的派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, cripes is an interjection with no regular root-and-affix breakdown; its final -s is not a plural ending. It is a euphemistic alteration of Christ and has no common derivatives; words such as Christian belong to the family of Christ, not to a derivative family of cripes.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: gosh（天哪）通常温和，常表达惊讶；goodness（天哪）较委婉，也可带关切；crikey（天哪）尤见于英式和澳大利亚英语。cripes 常带突然惊讶或轻度懊恼的语气。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Gosh is usually mild and often expresses surprise; goodness is restrained and can also express concern; crikey is especially associated with British and Australian English. Cripes often conveys sudden surprise or mild exasperation.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把它记成 Christ 的委婉惊叹替身：脱口而出的“天哪”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember it as a softened substitute for an exclamation of Christ: a quick cry of surprise.

senses.meaning_en: An ancient unit of length based on the distance from the elbow to the tip of the middle finger.
senses.english_definition: A cubit is an ancient unit for measuring length, originally based on the distance from a person's elbow to the tip of their middle finger.

etymology_story.zh: Cubit 可追溯到拉丁语 cubitum，意为“肘”或“肘尺”。由于人们曾用肘到指尖的距离丈量物体，身体部位的名称也成了长度单位的名称。
etymology_story.en: Cubit goes back to Latin cubitum, meaning elbow or cubit. Because people measured objects using the distance from the elbow to the fingertips, the name of a body part also became the name of a unit of length.

morphology_enriched.zh: Cubit 在现代英语中是单纯词，没有可用的英语前缀或后缀；复数为 cubits。相关拉丁词干为 cubit-，词族包括 cubital（肘部的）、antecubital（肘前的）和解剖学名词 cubitus（肘或尺骨，依语境而定）；这些主要表示解剖结构，并非都表示肘尺单位。
morphology_enriched.en: Cubit is a simple word in modern English with no productive English prefix or suffix; its plural is cubits. The related Latin stem cubit- appears in cubital, meaning relating to the elbow, antecubital, meaning in front of the elbow, and the anatomical noun cubitus, referring to the elbow or ulna according to context; these primarily describe anatomy rather than the unit of measurement.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: forearm-length measure（以前臂长度为基础的量度）和 elbow-to-fingertip measure（从肘到指尖的量度）是解释性近义表达，并非另一套标准单位名称。cubit 特指历史上的肘尺单位，其实际长度并不完全统一。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Forearm-length measure and elbow-to-fingertip measure are explanatory equivalents rather than names of separate standardized units. Cubit specifically names the historical unit, whose actual length varied.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 肘到指尖就是随身尺：身体长度变成计量单位。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Elbow to fingertip makes a portable ruler: a body length becomes a unit.

senses.meaning_en: Either member of a pair of stereoisomers that are non-superimposable mirror images.
senses.english_definition: An enantiomer is one of two molecules that have the same connections between their atoms but are mirror images that cannot be placed on top of each other with every atom matching.

etymology_story.zh: 该化学术语采用希腊语来源的 enantio-（相对、相反）和 -mer（源自 meros，意为“部分”）构成。名称强调一对分子彼此呈镜像关系，而它的化学定义还要求这两个镜像不能重合。
etymology_story.en: This chemical term combines Greek-derived enantio-, meaning opposite, with -mer, from meros, meaning part. Its name highlights the mirror relationship between two molecular forms, while the chemical definition additionally requires that those mirror images cannot be superimposed.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代科学构词公式为 enantio-（相对、相反）+ -mer（部分或结构单位）。主要派生词有 enantiomeric（对映体的）、enantiomerically（在对映体组成或性质方面）和 enantiomerism（对映异构现象）；同构词成分的相关词有 enantioselective（对映选择性的）、enantioselectivity（对映选择性）、enantiospecific（对映专一性的）及 enantiospecificity（对映专一性）。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern scientific formation is enantio-, meaning opposite, + -mer, meaning part or structural unit. Principal derivatives are enantiomeric, meaning relating to enantiomers, enantiomerically, meaning with respect to enantiomeric composition or properties, and enantiomerism, the relationship or phenomenon involved; related combining-form words include enantioselective, enantioselectivity, enantiospecific, and enantiospecificity.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: mirror-image isomer（镜像异构体）是直观的近义表达，但仍须满足镜像不可重合；optical isomer（旋光异构体）常作为传统近义术语，强调与旋光性质的联系。stereoisomer（立体异构体）是更宽泛的上位词，也包括非对映异构体。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Mirror-image isomer is an intuitive equivalent, provided the mirror images are non-superimposable; optical isomer is a traditional near-synonym emphasizing the connection with optical activity. Stereoisomer is a broader category that also includes diastereomers.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: enantio-＝相对：像左右手，互为镜像，却无法完全叠合。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Enantio- means opposite: think of left and right hands, mirror images that cannot be superimposed.

etymology.text: 18世纪末美国英语中出现，追溯到拉丁语 eventus（发生、结果）以及 evenire（发生、结果为）。把它和最终出现的结果联系起来。

usage_note: 偏正式；eventuate in + 名词表示“结果成为”，也可单独表示“终于发生”。

etymology_story.zh: 该词于18世纪末进入英语，早期尤见于美国英语，与拉丁语 eventus（发生、结果）和 evenire（发生、结果为）有关。其意义围绕事情经过一段过程后最终发生或形成某种结果展开。
etymology_story.en: The word entered English in the late eighteenth century, especially in American usage, and is connected with Latin eventus, meaning an occurrence or outcome, and evenire, meaning to happen or turn out. Its meanings concern what eventually happens or emerges as a final result.

morphology_enriched.zh: 这是一个拉丁语源的动词，形式上可分析为 eventu-（发生、结果的词干）+ -ate（动词后缀）。屈折形式：eventuates（第三人称单数）、eventuated（过去式及过去分词）、eventuating（现在分词）；派生词：eventuation（最终发生；最终结果，少用）。同源相关词：event（事件）、eventual（最终的）、eventually（最终）。
morphology_enriched.en: This Latinate verb can be analyzed formally as eventu- (occurrence or outcome) + -ate (a verb-forming suffix). Inflections: eventuates, eventuated, and eventuating. Derivative: eventuation, an uncommon noun for an eventual occurrence or outcome. Related words from the same historical family include event, eventual, and eventually.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: happen（发生）最普通，不强调最终结果；materialize（成为现实）强调预期或计划终于实现；culminate in（最终达到；以……告终）强调过程的终点或高潮。eventuate 较正式，突出最终发生或产生结果，在澳大利亚英语中较常见。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Happen is the neutral general verb and does not emphasize an eventual outcome; materialize stresses that something expected or planned becomes real; culminate in emphasizes a process reaching its final or highest point. Eventuate is formal and highlights eventual occurrence or outcome; it is particularly associated with Australian English.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 eventuate 与 eventual result（最终结果）相连：事情走到最后，终于发生或有了结果。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect eventuate with an eventual result: after a process unfolds, something finally happens or results.

morphology.text: execr-（诅咒、痛恨的词干）+ -able → execrable（坏得让人想咒骂的）。

etymology.text: 中古英语从古法语 execrable 及拉丁语 execrabilis 借入，来自表示诅咒的 execrari。原来的“该受诅咒”后来也用来形容质量极差。

usage_note: 强烈贬义、偏书面；可形容服务、表演或写作。另有“可憎的”义，本课侧重质量。

etymology_story.zh: 该词经法语进入中古英语，源自拉丁语 exsecrabilis（应受诅咒的），来自 exsecrari（诅咒、憎恶）。原先表示道德上可憎、应受诅咒，后来也用于夸张地形容质量或表现极差。
etymology_story.en: The word entered Middle English through French from Latin exsecrabilis, meaning deserving a curse, from exsecrari, to curse or detest. Its original sense of moral abhorrence later extended to emphatic criticism of extremely poor quality or performance.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代词族关系可表示为 execrate（诅咒；痛斥）去掉末尾 e，再加 -able，形成 execrable（可憎的；极差的）；execr- 是该词族中的束缚词干。派生及相关词：execrably（极其糟糕地）、execrableness（可憎；恶劣，少用）、execrate（诅咒；憎恶）、execration（咒骂；憎恶）、execratory（表示诅咒或痛斥的）。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern family relationship can be represented as execrate minus final e + -able, producing execrable; execr- is the bound stem shared by the family. Derivatives and related words include execrably, execrableness (uncommon), execrate, execration, and execratory.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: atrocious（糟透的；残暴的）既可批评质量，也可谴责暴行；abominable（可憎的；极恶劣的）强调强烈厌恶；deplorable（应受谴责的；糟糕的）强调令人遗憾或不齿。execrable 语气强烈，带有较正式或文学性的痛斥意味。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Atrocious can describe either terrible quality or brutal wrongdoing; abominable emphasizes strong disgust; deplorable stresses that something deserves regret or disapproval. Execrable conveys forceful condemnation in a relatively formal or literary register.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住历史核心“应受诅咒”：坏到让人想咒骂，就是 execrable。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember the historical core, deserving a curse: something execrable is bad enough to make you curse it.

etymology_story.zh: 该词借自爪哇语 gamelan，与表示敲击或演奏打击乐器的 gamel 有关。英语借入这一名称，用来指主要见于爪哇和巴厘等地的相关乐器组合、合奏乐队及其音乐。
etymology_story.en: The word was borrowed from Javanese gamelan, associated with gamel, referring to striking or playing percussion instruments. English adopted the name for the instrument sets, ensembles, and music associated especially with Java and Bali.

morphology_enriched.zh: 在现代英语中，gamelan 是整体借入的单纯词，不按英语词根与后缀拆分。表示乐队或乐器组合时，复数为 gamelans；表示音乐时通常不可数。相关形式包括 gamelan player（加麦兰演奏者）、gamelan music（加麦兰音乐）及 gamelan-like（类似加麦兰的，临时复合形容词）；没有庞大的常用派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, gamelan is an unanalyzed loanword rather than an English root-and-suffix formation. Its plural is gamelans when it denotes ensembles or instrument sets; the music sense is normally uncountable. Related formations include gamelan player, gamelan music, and the freely formed compound adjective gamelan-like; there is no extensive common derivational family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: ensemble（合奏团）是泛称，不限定地区或乐器；orchestra（管弦乐队；大型器乐合奏团）通常让人想到西方管弦乐编制；percussion ensemble（打击乐合奏团）说明主要乐器类型。三者都不能精确替代 gamelan，因为它还指特定的印度尼西亚音乐传统与乐器体系。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Ensemble is a broad term without a specific regional or instrumental identity; orchestra usually suggests a Western orchestral organization; percussion ensemble identifies the main instrument type. None is an exact synonym for gamelan, which also names a particular Indonesian musical tradition and instrumental system.

senses.sentence_en: The biopsy showed granulomatous inflammation in the lung tissue.

etymology_story.zh: 该词由现代医学名词 granuloma（肉芽肿）加形容词后缀构成；granuloma 结合了拉丁语 granulum（小颗粒）和希腊语来源的 -oma（肿块、肿胀）。这里的“颗粒”意象与结节状组织聚集有关，-oma 在这个词中并不表示癌症。
etymology_story.en: The adjective was formed from the medical noun granuloma, which combines Latin granulum, a small grain, with Greek-derived -oma, a swelling or mass. The grain image relates to nodular tissue formations, and -oma here does not mean cancer.

morphology_enriched.zh: granulomat-（granuloma 的扩展词干）+ -ous（具有……特征的）→ granulomatous；-omat- 体现希腊语来源的 -oma 名词在相关构词中的词干变化。核心词族：granuloma（肉芽肿），复数 granulomas 或 granulomata；granulomatous（肉芽肿性的）；granulomatosis（肉芽肿病，指以肉芽肿形成为特征的病理状态）。同源相关词：granule（小颗粒）、granular（颗粒状的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Granulomat- (the extended stem of granuloma) + -ous (characterized by) forms granulomatous; -omat- reflects the stem pattern of Greek-derived nouns ending in -oma. The core family includes granuloma, with plurals granulomas and granulomata; granulomatous; and granulomatosis, a condition characterized by granuloma formation. Related words sharing the grain element include granule and granular.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: granuloma-forming（形成肉芽肿的）是接近本义的解释性表达；nodular（结节状的）只描述形态，不确定细胞组成；inflammatory（炎症性的）范围更广，不一定涉及肉芽肿。只有 granulomatous 明确指出肉芽肿这一组织病理特征。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Granuloma-forming is a close descriptive paraphrase; nodular describes shape without specifying cellular composition; inflammatory is broader and does not necessarily involve granulomas. Granulomatous specifically identifies the granuloma pattern in tissue.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: granuloma（肉芽肿）+ -ous（具有……的）：组织里有肉芽肿，就是 granulomatous；“小颗粒”只作形象线索。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Granuloma + -ous means having granulomas: picture small nodular clusters in tissue, using the grain image as a memory aid.

meaning: 逻各斯中心的；以语言或理性为权威中心的

morphology.text: logo-（言说、理性）+ -centric（以……为中心的）→ logocentric（逻各斯中心的）。

etymology.text: 属于现代国际学术词汇，用希腊语 logos（言说、理性）和表示中心的构词成分组合。在哲学阅读中，把它和“什么被放在解释的中心”联系起来。

etymology_story.zh: 该词由希腊语 logos（言说、论述、理性）对应的构词成分 logo- 与表示“以……为中心”的 -centric 组合而成。它在现代哲学中，尤其在与德里达相关的批判中受到重视，用来讨论思想如何赋予逻各斯、意义的在场或言语以优先地位。
etymology_story.en: The word combines logo-, from Greek logos, meaning speech, discourse, or reason, with -centric, meaning centered on. It became prominent in modern philosophy, especially in critiques associated with Derrida, concerning the priority given to logos, the presence of meaning, or speech.

morphology_enriched.zh: logo-（言说；理性）+ -centric（以……为中心的）→ logocentric。核心词族：logocentrism（逻各斯中心主义）、logocentric（逻各斯中心的）、logocentrically（以逻各斯为中心地）、logocentrist（逻各斯中心主义者）；这里的 logo- 与英语中表示“商标”的独立词 logo 含义不同。
morphology_enriched.en: Logo- (speech or reason) + -centric (centered on) forms logocentric. The core family includes logocentrism, logocentric, logocentrically, and logocentrist. The combining form logo- here has a different meaning from the independent English noun logo, a commercial emblem.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: language-centered（以语言为中心的）是较宽泛的描述，未必涉及哲学立场；phonocentric（语音中心的）专指赋予言语或声音优于文字的地位；rationalist（理性主义的）强调理性的认识论权威。三者分别与 logocentric 的部分含义重叠，但都不能覆盖其全部哲学含义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Language-centered is a broad description that need not imply a philosophical position; phonocentric specifically privileges speech or voice over writing; rationalist emphasizes the authority of reason in knowledge. Each overlaps with part of logocentric, but none covers its full philosophical meaning.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: logos（言说、理性）+ center（中心）：把言说或理性放在解释与意义的中心。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Logos plus center: place speech or reason at the center of explanation and meaning.

etymology_story.zh: 源自后期拉丁语 masticare（咀嚼）的过去分词词干 masticat-，进一步可追溯至希腊语 mastikhan（磨牙、咬嚼）。英语保留了其与牙齿磨碎食物有关的本义，主要用于正式或专业语境。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from masticat-, the past-participial stem of Late Latin masticare, meaning “to chew,” ultimately from Greek mastikhan, meaning “to gnash the teeth.” English retained the literal meaning of breaking down food with the teeth, chiefly in formal or technical contexts.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可分析为黏着词干 mastic-（咀嚼）+ 动词后缀 -ate；mastic- 不能单独作普通英语词使用。屈折形式：masticates、masticated、masticating；主要派生词：mastication（咀嚼）、masticatory（咀嚼的）、masticator（咀嚼者；咀嚼器）。
morphology_enriched.en: A useful modern analysis is the bound stem mastic- (“chewing”) + the verb-forming suffix -ate; mastic- does not normally stand alone. Inflections: masticates, masticated, masticating. Principal derivatives: mastication (“chewing”), masticatory (“relating to chewing”), and masticator (“a person, animal, or device that chews”).

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: chew（咀嚼）是日常通用词；chomp（大口用力地嚼）强调动作有力，常带声音；grind（磨碎）强调研磨结果，也可用于牙齿以外的工具。masticate 是描述咀嚼过程的正式或专业用词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Chew is the ordinary everyday word; chomp suggests vigorous, often noisy chewing; grind emphasizes crushing something into smaller particles and can involve tools as well as teeth. Masticate is the formal or technical term for the chewing process.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: mastic- 锚定“牙齿磨食物”：把食物嚼碎，就是 masticate。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor mastic- to teeth grinding food: breaking food down by chewing is to masticate.

etymology_story.zh: 这是十九世纪出现的学科名称，由表示“博物馆”的构词成分 museo- 与表示“研究、学科”的 -logy 构成。museum 最终源自希腊语 mouseion，原指献给缪斯的场所，后来与学术研究和收藏机构联系起来。
etymology_story.en: This nineteenth-century disciplinary term combines museo-, referring to museums, with -logy, meaning “study.” Museum ultimately comes from Greek mouseion, a place dedicated to the Muses, which became associated with scholarship and collections.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：museo-（博物馆）+ -logy（研究、学科）。主要词族：museological（博物馆学的）、museologically（从博物馆学角度）、museologist（博物馆学家）；museum（博物馆）提供词基，museography（博物馆陈列与实务研究）是相关术语。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: museo- (“museum”) + -logy (“study”). Principal family members are museological (“relating to museology”), museologically (“from a museological perspective”), and museologist (“a specialist in museology”). Museum supplies the base; museography, concerning museum presentation and practical methods, is a related term.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: museum studies（博物馆研究）与 museology 高度重合，常用作课程或学科名称；museography（博物馆陈列与实务）通常更侧重展示设计和实际技术；heritage studies（遗产研究）范围更广，还研究历史建筑、遗址及非物质文化遗产。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Museum studies substantially overlaps with museology and is common in academic program names. Museography usually emphasizes exhibition design and practical techniques. Heritage studies is broader, also covering historic buildings, sites, and intangible cultural heritage.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: museo- 是“博物馆”，-logy 是“研究”：研究博物馆，就是博物馆学。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Museo- means “museum” and -logy means “study”: museology studies museums.

etymology_story.zh: 源自古英语 nēp，见于表示“小潮”的复合词 nēpflōd，后经中古英语 neep 演变而来。其更早的来源并不确定；现代仍保留潮差较小这一古老的潮汐含义。
etymology_story.en: The word goes back to Old English nēp, found in nēpflōd, meaning “neap tide,” and continued through Middle English neep. Its deeper origin is uncertain; the modern word preserves its old association with a small tidal range.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代 neap 是不可再作透明拆分的单纯词，常见复数为 neaps。常见组合有 neap tide（小潮）、neap-tide conditions（小潮条件）；另有罕见航海动词 neap，其形式 neaped、neaping 表示船只因小潮水位不足而受困。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern neap is a simple word without a transparent internal breakdown; its usual plural is neaps. Common combinations include neap tide and neap-tide conditions. A rare nautical verb neap, with forms neaped and neaping, describes a vessel being held up by insufficient water at neap tides.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: neap tide（小潮）是名词 neap 的完整常用形式；quadrature tide（方照潮、小潮）是强调日月相对地球约成直角位置的专业近义表达。low tide（低潮）不是同义词：它指一次潮汐周期中的最低水位，而 neap 指高潮与低潮之间的差值较小。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Neap tide is the usual full equivalent of the noun neap. Quadrature tide is a technical near-equivalent emphasizing the approximately right-angled positions of the sun and moon relative to Earth. Low tide is different: it is the lowest water level within a tidal cycle, whereas neap describes a small difference between high and low water.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 记“小潮＝小潮差”：高潮与低潮靠得近，不是水位一直低。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember “neap = narrow tidal range”: high and low water are closer together.

etymology_story.zh: 英语借自法语 nougat，法语又借自奥克语 nogat，原指含坚果的糖食。这个名称与表示“坚果”的词有关，最终可追溯到拉丁语 nux，因此名称本身就点出了它的传统配料。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed nougat from French, which took it from Occitan nogat, a nut confection. The name belongs to a family of words for nuts ultimately tracing back to Latin nux, so it identifies a traditional ingredient.

morphology_enriched.zh: nougat 在现代英语中是整体借入的单纯词，不宜拆成英语词根和后缀。通常作不可数名词；nougats 可指多种牛轧糖或多个糖块。相关词 nougatine（坚果脆糖）也是法语借词；nougat-filled（夹有牛轧糖的）和 nougat-like（类似牛轧糖的）是透明的英语组合。
morphology_enriched.en: Nougat is a simple loanword in modern English and has no useful English root-and-suffix breakdown. It is usually uncountable, though nougats can refer to varieties or individual confections. Related nougatine (“a brittle nut confection”) is also borrowed from French; nougat-filled and nougat-like are transparent English formations.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有完全等义的日常替换词。divinity（蛋白软糖）是质地较轻、常含坚果的相近糖食；fudge（乳脂软糖）通常更突出奶油或牛奶的浓厚口感；brittle（脆糖，常含坚果）强调硬而易碎，与许多牛轧糖的韧性不同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no exact everyday substitute. Divinity is a related, lighter egg-white confection often containing nuts; fudge usually has a richer milk or cream character; brittle is hard and snaps easily, unlike many chewy varieties of nougat.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 沿词源记“坚果糖”：nougat 的名字就与坚果有关。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Use the historical link to nuts: nougat is traditionally a nut-filled sweet.

morphology.text: peregrin-（异乡、旅行）+ -ate（动词词尾）→ peregrinate（到各处漫游）。

etymology.text: 来自拉丁语 peregrinatus，与 peregrinari（在异乡旅行）相连，最终关联 peregrinus（外国人、外来的）。想象背着行囊走过异乡。

senses.meaning_zh: 漫游；四处旅行，尤指远行或在异乡游历
senses.meaning_en: To travel or wander from place to place, especially over long distances or abroad.
senses.english_definition: If someone peregrinates, they travel from place to place, often through unfamiliar or foreign regions.

etymology_story.zh: 源自拉丁语 peregrinari（在外旅行、旅居异乡）的过去分词词干 peregrinat-，与 peregrinus（外国的；异乡人）同源。其更深层的来源涉及 per（穿过）和 ager（田野、土地），语义由离开本土发展为在各地游历。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from peregrinat-, the past-participial stem of Latin peregrinari, meaning “to travel abroad or live away from home,” related to peregrinus, “foreign” or “a foreigner.” Its deeper history involves per (“through”) and ager (“field, land”), connecting travel with going beyond one's own territory.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代学习性分析：黏着词干 peregrin-（异乡、旅行）+ 动词后缀 -ate；不要把整个词当作现代英语中可自由拼接的 per + 其他成分。屈折形式：peregrinates、peregrinated、peregrinating；主要派生词：peregrination（漫游、游历）、peregrinator（漫游者）、peregrinatory（漫游的，罕用）。peregrine（外来的；游隼）与其同源，并非由该动词直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: A useful learning analysis is the bound stem peregrin- (“foreign travel”) + the verb-forming suffix -ate; the word is not a freely assembled modern English per- construction. Inflections: peregrinates, peregrinated, peregrinating. Principal derivatives: peregrination (“travel or wandering”), peregrinator (“a traveler”), and the uncommon peregrinatory (“relating to wandering”). Peregrine (“foreign”; a peregrine falcon) is a cognate rather than a direct derivative of the verb.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: travel（旅行）最中性，不限定路线或目的；wander（漫游、游荡）常暗示路线随意或目的不明确；roam（四处游走）强调在较大区域内自由移动。peregrinate 文体更正式，常使人联想到较长时间的异地游历，但不必然指步行。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Travel is neutral about route and purpose; wander often suggests an informal route or no clear destination; roam emphasizes free movement over an area. Peregrinate is more formal and often evokes extended journeys through unfamiliar places, without necessarily implying travel on foot.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 peregrin- 记成“人在异乡”：一路走过不同地方，就是 peregrinate。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor peregrin- to being away from home: moving through unfamiliar places is to peregrinate.

etymology_story.zh: 该词形成于19世纪的科学英语，由希腊语来源的 poly-（多）与 cyclic（环状的；周期性的）组合而成。其含义随 cycle 的两种意义展开，既可表示多个结构环，也可表示多个过程循环。
etymology_story.en: The word developed in nineteenth-century scientific English from Greek-derived poly-, meaning “many,” and cyclic, meaning “ring-shaped” or “occurring in cycles.” It reflects both meanings of cycle: a structural ring and a recurring sequence.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：poly-（多）+ cyclic（环状的；周期性的）→ polycyclic。基础词族：cycle（环；周期；循环）→ cyclic、cyclical（周期性的）、cyclically（周期性地）；直接派生词有 polycyclically（以多环或多周期方式）和 polycyclicity（多环性；多周期性）。平行构词包括 monocyclic（单环的）、bicyclic（双环的）、tricyclic（三环的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: poly- (“many”) + cyclic (“ring-shaped; occurring in cycles”) → polycyclic. The base family includes cycle, cyclic, cyclical, and cyclically; direct derivatives include polycyclically and polycyclicity. Parallel formations include monocyclic, bicyclic, and tricyclic.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: multicyclic（多循环的）在某些技术语境中意义接近；cyclic（环状的；周期性的）不限定环或循环的数量；fused-ring（稠环的）强调环之间共用一条边，只描述多环结构中的一类。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Multicyclic is close in some technical contexts; cyclic does not specify how many rings or cycles are involved; fused-ring describes the narrower case in which rings share an edge.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: poly- 是“多”，cycle 是“环或循环”：多个环，或多个循环。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Poly- means “many”; cycle supplies either “ring” or “cycle”: many rings or repeated cycles.

etymology_story.zh: 该词属于20世纪初生理学家查尔斯·谢灵顿引入的本体感觉术语，结合了拉丁语 proprius（自身的）和表示“接收”的 -ceptive。这个名称强调感觉信息来自身体自身，有别于来自外界的刺激。
etymology_story.en: The word belongs to the terminology of proprioception introduced by physiologist Charles Sherrington in the early twentieth century, combining Latin proprius, “one’s own,” with -ceptive, “receiving.” The name emphasizes sensory information arising within the body itself, as distinguished from external stimulation.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：proprio-（自身）+ -ceptive（接收的；感受的）→ proprioceptive。词族：proprioception（本体感觉）、proprioceptor（本体感受器）、proprioceptively（通过本体感觉地）；其中 -ception 表示接收或感知过程，-ceptor 表示接收器。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: proprio- (“one’s own”) + -ceptive (“receiving; sensing”) → proprioceptive. The family includes proprioception, proprioceptor, and proprioceptively. The related endings -ception and -ceptor denote a receiving or sensing process and a receptor, respectively.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 以下是相关术语，并非完全同义词：kinaesthetic（动觉的）侧重身体运动及其感觉；somatosensory（躯体感觉的）范围更广，还包括触觉等；postural（姿势的）侧重身体姿势，不直接表示一种感觉。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: These related terms are not exact synonyms: kinaesthetic emphasizes the sensation of bodily movement; somatosensory is broader and also includes senses such as touch; postural concerns body posture without necessarily referring to a sensory process.

etymology_story.zh: 英语 ribose 借自19世纪末的德语 Ribose，其名称与 Ribonsäure（核糖酸）有关；后者由 Arabonsäure（阿拉伯糖酸）的名称改造而来。因此，ribose 的名称源于早期糖类化学的命名关系，而不是 RNA 的缩写。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed ribose from late-nineteenth-century German Ribose, a name associated with Ribonsäure, “ribonic acid,” which was formed by altering Arabonsäure, “arabonic acid.” Its name therefore reflects early sugar-chemistry nomenclature rather than an abbreviation of RNA.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可分析为 rib-（核糖系列的命名词干）+ -ose（糖类后缀），但 rib- 不是独立单词。词族及相关构词：ribosyl（核糖基）、ribosylation（核糖基化）、ribonic acid（核糖酸）、ribose phosphate（磷酸核糖）；deoxy-（脱氧）+ ribose → deoxyribose（脱氧核糖）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern analysis: rib-, a naming stem in the ribose series, + -ose, the sugar suffix; rib- is not an independent word. Family members and related formations include ribosyl, ribosylation, ribonic acid, and ribose phosphate. Adding deoxy- gives deoxyribose.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有通用的严格同义词。D-ribose（D-核糖）特指生物体内常见的立体异构形式；aldopentose（醛戊糖）是包含核糖的上位类别；deoxyribose（脱氧核糖）是比相应核糖少一个氧原子的不同糖类，不能与核糖互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no ordinary exact synonym. D-ribose specifies the stereochemical form commonly found in living organisms; aldopentose is the broader class that includes ribose; deoxyribose is a different sugar with one fewer oxygen atom than the corresponding ribose and is not interchangeable with it.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: -ose 提示“糖”：RNA 含核糖，DNA 含脱氧核糖。
mnemonic_anchor.en: -ose signals a sugar: RNA contains ribose, while DNA contains deoxyribose.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词分析：sagac-（源自拉丁语，表示感知敏锐）+ -ious（形容词后缀）→ sagacious。词族：sagaciously（睿智地）、sagaciousness（睿智；明察）；同源名词 sagacity（睿智；敏锐的判断力）采用另一种派生形式。
morphology_enriched.en: Analysis: sagac-, a Latin-derived stem meaning keenly perceptive, + the adjective suffix -ious → sagacious. Derivatives include sagaciously and sagaciousness; the related noun sagacity expresses the same quality through a different derivational form.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: wise（明智的）范围最广，常强调经验与良好判断；astute（精明敏锐的）突出迅速看清局势及其实际影响；shrewd（精明的）常强调现实利益和策略判断。sagacious 更正式，通常带有对深刻洞察和稳健判断的赞许。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Wise is the broadest term and often suggests experience and good judgment; astute emphasizes quickly understanding a situation and its practical implications; shrewd often highlights practical advantage and strategic judgment. Sagacious is more formal and usually praises penetrating insight combined with sound judgment.

etymology_story.zh: 这是科学英语中由 uni-“一个”和 cellular“细胞的”组成的词，两部分分别追溯至拉丁语 unus“一个”和 cellula“小室”。生物学将细胞理解为生命的基本单位后，这个词便用于描述仅由一个细胞构成的生物。
etymology_story.en: This scientific formation combines uni-, meaning “one,” with cellular; these elements ultimately derive from Latin unus, “one,” and cellula, “a small room.” In biology, it describes organisms whose entire structure consists of one cell.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：uni-（单一）+ cellular（细胞的）；cellular 可分析为 cell（细胞）+ -ular（形容词后缀）。主要词族：cell（细胞）、cellular（细胞的）、unicellularity（单细胞性）；相关对照词有 multicellular（多细胞的）和 acellular（无细胞的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: uni- (“one”) + cellular (“relating to cells”); cellular can be analyzed as cell + the adjective-forming suffix -ular. Principal family members include cell, cellular, and unicellularity. Related contrasting formations include multicellular and acellular.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: single-celled 与 unicellular 基本同义，表达更直观；one-celled 也表示“单细胞的”，但较少见。acellular 意为“无细胞的”，不能与 unicellular 互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Single-celled is essentially synonymous with unicellular and is more immediately transparent; one-celled has the same meaning but is less usual. Acellular means “without cells” and is not interchangeable with unicellular.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: uni-＝一，cell＝细胞：一个细胞就是整个生物。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Uni- means one, and cell names the unit: one cell makes the whole organism.

etymology_story.en: This medical term combines vaso-, “blood vessel,” with dilator, “something that widens,” corresponding to French vaso-dilateur. Vaso- comes from Latin vas, “vessel,” specialized in medicine to mean a blood vessel, while dilator is related to Latin dilatare, “to widen.”

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：vaso-（血管）+ dilate（扩张，去掉词尾 e）+ -or（施事者或起作用的物质）。主要词族：vasodilate（使血管扩张）、vasodilating（扩张血管的）、vasodilation／vasodilatation（血管扩张）、vasodilatory（血管扩张的）；相关基础词有 dilate、dilation、dilatation 和 dilator。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: vaso- (“blood vessel”) + dilate, with final e removed, + -or (“an agent or something producing an effect”). Principal family members are vasodilate, vasodilating, vasodilation, vasodilatation, and vasodilatory. Related base-family words include dilate, dilation, dilatation, and dilator.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: vasodilating agent 与名词 vasodilator 基本同义；vasorelaxant 强调使血管平滑肌松弛，突出扩张的作用机制；形容词 vasodilatory 表示“具有血管扩张作用的”，可用于描述相关作用或反应。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Vasodilating agent is essentially equivalent to the noun vasodilator. Vasorelaxant emphasizes relaxation of vascular smooth muscle, highlighting a mechanism of widening. The adjective vasodilatory describes an action or response involving blood-vessel widening.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: vaso-＝血管，dilate＝扩张：让血管变宽的物质。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Vaso- identifies the blood vessel; dilate supplies the action: a vessel-widening agent.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：weather（天气）+ vane（风向标片），属于名词复合词。复数为 weathervanes；常见异体写法为 weather vane 和 weather-vane。weathercock（公鸡形风向标；随风转向的人）是相关复合词，不是本词的派生形式。

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 borax 是不可进一步分析的借入词；动词由名词零派生而来。动词形式：boraxes、boraxed、boraxing；boraxed 也可作分词修饰语。boron（硼）和 borate（硼酸盐）属于相关化学词汇，不是现代英语中由 borax 加后缀直接构成的形式。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, borax is an unanalyzed loanword; its verb is formed by conversion from the noun. Boron and borate are related chemical vocabulary, not forms produced by directly adding suffixes to borax.

etymology_story.en: Chambray derives from an altered form of Cambrai, the name of a French textile town also associated with the name cambric. The place-name became a fabric name, now usually referring to a lightweight plain weave with colored warp and white weft.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 chambray 作为一个完整的借入词使用，没有可分析的现代词根和词缀，通常为不可数名词。chambray shirt 中的 chambray 是作定语的名词；chambray-like（像钱布雷布的）是可按需构造的表达，并非必须收录的固定派生词。cambric 是词源相关词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English treats chambray as a whole borrowed word without productive internal roots or affixes; it is normally uncountable. etymology_story.zh: chloramphenicol 是20世纪形成的科学药名，由涉及氯、酰胺、苯基、硝基和乙二醇的命名片段缩合而成。这些片段反映其化学结构，整个名称后来固定指氯霉素。
etymology_story.en: Chloramphenicol is a twentieth-century scientific name formed by contracting naming elements associated with chlorine, amide, phenyl, nitro, and glycol. These elements reflect its chemical structure, and the resulting name identifies the antibiotic.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常把 chloramphenicol 作为不可自由拆分的药名整体使用；其历史命名可概括为 chlor-、amide、phen-、nitr- 和 glycol 的缩合，而非普通的词根加词缀构词。通常为不可数名词，没有常用的派生词族；相关复合表达有 chloramphenicol-resistant（耐氯霉素的）和 chloramphenicol resistance（氯霉素耐药性）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, chloramphenicol normally functions as a whole drug name rather than a freely analysable root-and-affix formation; its historical naming contracts elements from chlor-, amide, phen-, nitr-, and glycol. It is normally uncountable and has no established common derivational family; related compounds include chloramphenicol-resistant and chloramphenicol resistance.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Chloromycetin（历史商品名）曾用于指含氯霉素的制剂；antibiotic（抗生素）和 antibacterial agent（抗菌剂）都是更宽泛的类别名称，不能在需要明确药物名称时替换 chloramphenicol。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Chloromycetin is a historical trade name associated with chloramphenicol preparations. Antibiotic and antibacterial agent are broader category terms, so neither identifies this particular drug precisely.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: chlor- 提醒“氯”，全词锚定“氯霉素”；其余部分是化学命名缩合。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Let chlor- cue chlorine, then anchor the whole word to chloramphenicol, the antibiotic; the remaining sounds come from contracted chemical naming elements.

etymology_story.zh: codec 是电子通信领域将 coder（编码器）和 decoder（解码器）缩合而成的词，也常被解释为 compressor（压缩器）与 decompressor（解压器）的缩合。其应用后来扩展到数字音频和视频的存储、传输与播放。
etymology_story.en: Codec originated in electronic communications as a blend of coder and decoder; it is also commonly explained as a blend of compressor and decompressor. Its use subsequently extended to storing, transmitting, and playing digital audio and video.

morphology_enriched.zh: coder + decoder → codec，是缩合构词，不是词根加后缀；复数为 codecs。没有常用的直接派生词；相关词族包括 code（编码；代码）、coder（编码器；程序员）、encode（编码）、encoder（编码器）、decode（解码）、decoder（解码器）、encoding（编码）和 decoding（解码）。
morphology_enriched.en: Coder + decoder → codec is a blend rather than a root-plus-suffix formation; its plural is codecs. There are no common direct derivatives; its related lexical family includes code, coder, encode, encoder, decode, decoder, encoding, and decoding.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: coder-decoder（编码解码器）是 codec 的展开形式；encoder（编码器）只强调编码功能，decoder（解码器）只强调解码功能，二者单独使用时都不完全等同于 codec。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Coder-decoder is the expanded equivalent of codec. Encoder emphasizes the encoding function, while decoder emphasizes the decoding function; neither alone necessarily denotes a complete codec.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: co 来自 coder，dec 来自 decoder：编码进去，解码出来。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Co comes from coder and dec from decoder: encode on the way in, decode on the way out.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 feverfew 是不可自由拆分的植物名称，不能按 fever（发热）+ few（少数）分析。通常作不可数名词，没有常用的直接派生词；feverfew leaves（小白菊叶）、feverfew extract（小白菊提取物）是名词组合，feverfew-like（像小白菊的）是可按需构成的形容词。

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语把 flambeau 作为完整的法语借词使用，没有能产的英语词缀结构；历史上的 flambe + 指小成分属于法语构词。复数可为 flambeaux 或 flambeaus；没有常用的英语派生词族。

synonyms_and_nuances.en: Torch is the ordinary, general term. Link is a historical term for a torch, often a pitch-covered one used to light streets. Flambeau more readily suggests a large, decorative, or ceremonial torch.

etymology_story.zh: foursquare 由英语 four 和 square 组合而成，最初表示“四方的、方正的”。方形结构稳固、端正的形象后来引申出“坚定直率”的形容词义和“坚定地”的副词义。
etymology_story.en: Foursquare combines English four and square and originally described something square in shape. The image of a stable, upright structure later developed into the adjective meaning firm and straightforward and the adverb meaning firmly.

morphology_enriched.zh: four（四）+ square（方正的）→ foursquare，是复合词；同一形式兼作形容词和副词，副词不必加 -ly。派生名词 foursquareness 表示“方正；坚定直率”，但较少见；其构词基础 square 的相关形式包括 squarely（正对地；明确地）和 squareness（方形；方正）。
morphology_enriched.en: Four + square → foursquare is a compound that functions as both an adjective and an adverb; its adverbial use requires no -ly. The uncommon derivative foursquareness means squareness or firm straightforwardness; related forms of its base square include squarely and squareness.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 形容词义中，solid（坚实的）强调结构或基础牢固，forthright（直率的）强调表达坦诚直接；副词义中的 firmly（坚定地）强调态度稳定有力。foursquare 把稳固、直接和立场明确的意味结合在一起。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: As an adjective, solid emphasizes structural strength or a sound foundation, while forthright emphasizes open, direct expression. As an adverb, firmly emphasizes strength and steadiness of attitude. Foursquare combines suggestions of stability, directness, and a definite position.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Four square sides suggest a steady stance: solid in shape, firm in position.

etymology_story.zh: 英语 frangipani 与意大利 Frangipani 家族的姓氏有关，该姓氏曾用于一种香水的名称，后来又用于香气相似的花木。关于具体由哪位家族成员发明这种香水的传统说法并不完全一致。
etymology_story.en: English frangipani is associated with the Italian surname Frangipani, which was used for a perfume before being applied to the similarly scented flowering plant. Traditional accounts differ over which member of the family created the perfume.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中，frangipani 是不可再作有效词根、词缀拆分的借入名词。复数可用 frangipanis 或不变的 frangipani；frangipani-like 意为“像鸡蛋花的”，属于可临时构造的复合形容词，并非独立的常用派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, frangipani is a borrowed noun without a productive root-and-affix breakdown. Its plural is frangipanis or unchanged frangipani; frangipani-like means resembling frangipani and is a freely formed compound adjective rather than an established common derivative.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: plumeria（鸡蛋花属植物）是对应的植物学名称，也可作日常名称；temple tree（庙树）是某些地区的俗名，但也可能指其他树种。frangipani 是常见名称，可指植物及其花朵。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Plumeria is the corresponding botanical name and also occurs in everyday use; temple tree is a regional common name that can also refer to other trees. Frangipani is a common name for both the plant and its flowers.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“香水名”联想到“同样芳香的鸡蛋花”；这是意义联想，不是英语词根拆解。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect the perfume name with the similarly fragrant flower; this is a meaning-based link, not an English root analysis.

etymology_story.zh: Freon 是二十世纪初创用并作为商标推广的制冷剂名称，最初与早期氟碳制冷剂密切相关。随着这些产品广泛用于制冷设备，该名称也进入日常语言，被非正式地用于泛指某些制冷剂。
etymology_story.en: Freon was coined and promoted as a refrigerant trademark in the early twentieth century, initially becoming closely associated with early fluorocarbon refrigerants. As these products became widely used in cooling equipment, the name also entered everyday language as an informal term for certain refrigerants.

morphology_enriched.zh: Freon 是独立的商标词，没有可靠的现代英语词根、词缀拆分。常见组合有 Freon-free（不含氟利昂的）和 Freon-based（以氟利昂为基础的）；没有常用的动词、副词等派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: Freon is an independent trademark name without a reliable modern English root-and-affix breakdown. Common formations include Freon-free, meaning containing no Freon, and Freon-based, meaning based on Freon; it has no established common family of derived verbs or adverbs.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: refrigerant（制冷剂）是按功能划分的上位词，范围最广；fluorocarbon（氟碳化合物）是化学类别名称；CFC（氯氟烃）指一类含氯、氟和碳的化合物。三者都不是 Freon 的严格同义词，不能把所有制冷剂或所有 Freon 产品都等同于 CFC。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Refrigerant is the broad functional term; fluorocarbon names a chemical category; CFC identifies compounds containing chlorine, fluorine, and carbon. None is an exact synonym of Freon, and neither all refrigerants nor all Freon products should be equated with CFCs.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 Freon 与冰箱、空调里的制冷剂相连；可借 freezing（冰冻）辅助联想，但不要把它当作已证实的构词来源。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture Freon as refrigerant in a refrigerator or air conditioner; freezing can serve as a memory cue, but it is not a verified morphological derivation.

morphology_enriched.zh: gnu 是不可再拆分的借入名词，复数可用 gnus 或不变的 gnu。gnu-like（像角马的）是可临时构造的复合形容词；wildebeest（角马）是另一名称，并非它的派生词。大写 GNU 作为计算机项目名称时属于另一个用法。

senses.meaning_zh: 稳态的；与维持内部条件相对稳定有关的
senses.meaning_en: relating to the maintenance of relatively stable internal conditions
senses.english_definition: A homeostatic process helps an organism or system keep its internal conditions relatively stable when conditions change.

senses.sentence_zh: 出汗是身体在体温升高时作出的稳态调节反应的一部分。

etymology_story.zh: homeostatic 是 homeostasis（稳态）的形容词形式；homeostasis 由生理学家沃尔特·坎农在二十世纪初提出，以希腊语来源的“相似”和“维持状态”成分构成。其含义强调通过持续调节维持相对稳定，而非完全不变。
etymology_story.en: Homeostatic is the adjective corresponding to homeostasis, a term introduced by physiologist Walter Cannon in the early twentieth century from Greek elements meaning similar and standing or maintaining a state. It describes relative stability maintained through continuing adjustment rather than complete immobility.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词可分析为 homeo-（相似）+ stat-（站立、维持状态）+ -ic（形容词后缀）；也可理解为 homeostasis 对应的形容词 homeostatic。主要词族：homeostasis（稳态，名词）、homeostatic（稳态的，形容词）、homeostatically（以稳态调节方式，副词）、homeostat（稳态调节系统或装置，名词）。
morphology_enriched.en: The formation can be analyzed as homeo- meaning similar + stat- meaning standing or maintaining a state + the adjective suffix -ic; homeostatic is also understood as the adjective corresponding to homeostasis. The principal family comprises homeostasis, the noun for the stable condition or its maintenance; homeostatic, the adjective; homeostatically, the adverb; and homeostat, a regulating system or device.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: self-regulating（自我调节的）强调系统自行调整；stabilizing（起稳定作用的）强调使条件趋于稳定的效果；regulatory（调节的）含义更广，并不必然涉及稳态。homeostatic 特指对内部条件相对稳定的维持。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Self-regulating emphasizes a system's ability to adjust itself; stabilizing emphasizes the effect of making conditions more stable; regulatory is broader and need not involve homeostasis. Homeostatic specifically concerns maintaining relatively stable internal conditions.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: homeo- 表示“相近”：不断调整，让内部条件保持在相近范围。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Homeo- means similar: keep adjusting so that internal conditions remain within a similar range.

etymology_story.zh: lobule 由 lobe（叶、圆形突起）与表示“小”的后缀 -ule 构成，历史上与法语 lobule 和新拉丁语 lobulus 有关。它原本表示“小的叶或突起”，后来成为描述器官细小分区及耳垂的解剖学用语。
etymology_story.en: Lobule combines lobe with the diminutive suffix -ule and is historically associated with French lobule and New Latin lobulus. Its meaning of a small lobe or projection developed into an anatomical term for small organ subdivisions and the earlobe.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：lobe 去掉末尾不发音的 e，再加 -ule（小）→ lobule（小叶）；复数为 lobules。主要相关词族：lobe（叶）、lobed（有叶的、分叶的）、lobar（叶的）、lobular（小叶的）、lobulate／lobulated（分成小叶的）、lobulation（分叶；小叶形成）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: lobe loses its final silent e and takes the diminutive suffix -ule to form lobule; the plural is lobules. Principal related forms include lobe; lobed, having lobes; lobar, relating to a lobe; lobular, relating to lobules; lobulate or lobulated, divided into small lobes; and lobulation, division into or formation of lobes.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: small lobe（小的叶）是直接释义；acinus（腺泡）指某些腺体中更具体的分泌单位，不能普遍替换 lobule；earlobe（耳垂）仅与耳部解剖义对应。lobule 的一般含义是小的叶状结构或器官分区。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Small lobe is a direct paraphrase; acinus names a more specific secretory unit in certain glands and is not generally interchangeable with lobule; earlobe corresponds only to the ear-related sense. Lobule generally denotes a small lobelike structure or organ subdivision.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: lobe 是“叶”，-ule 表示“小”：lobule 就是“小叶”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Lobe means a lobe, and -ule means small: a lobule is a little lobe.

senses.meaning_zh: 长寿饮食法的；以全谷物、蔬菜等为主并强调饮食平衡的
senses.meaning_en: relating to a dietary system emphasizing whole grains, vegetables, and dietary balance
senses.english_definition: A macrobiotic diet or lifestyle follows a system of eating that emphasizes whole grains, vegetables, and balance in the choice and preparation of food.
senses.collocation_zh: 长寿饮食法；长寿饮食法烹饪
senses.sentence_en: Her macrobiotic diet includes brown rice, beans, and seasonal vegetables.
senses.sentence_zh: 她遵循长寿饮食法，食物包括糙米、豆类和时令蔬菜。

etymology_story.zh: 该词最终源于希腊语 makros“长的”和 bios“生命”，早期相关用语讨论延年益寿之道。现代饮食义在二十世纪得到推广，名称表达长寿理念，并不表示这种饮食已被证明能够延长寿命。
etymology_story.en: The word ultimately comes from Greek makros, meaning 'long,' and bios, meaning 'life'; earlier related terminology concerned the art of prolonging life. Its modern dietary meaning became widespread in the twentieth century, expressing an ideal of longevity rather than a demonstrated guarantee of longer life.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词可分析为 macro-（此处表示“长”，而非通常的“大”）+ biot-（生命）+ -ic（形容词后缀）。主要词族：macrobiotics（长寿饮食法及其理论）、macrobiotically（按照长寿饮食法地）；相关词：biotic（生命的；生物的）。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern learned formation is macro- ('long' here, rather than the usual 'large') + biot- ('life') + -ic (adjective suffix). Principal family members include macrobiotics (the dietary system and its principles) and macrobiotically (in accordance with that system); biotic ('relating to life') is related.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: whole-food（以完整、少加工食物为主的）强调加工程度；plant-based（以植物性食物为主的）强调食物来源；vegetarian（素食的）强调不吃肉。三者都与 macrobiotic 有交集，但都不等同于其特定饮食体系。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Whole-food emphasizes minimally processed ingredients; plant-based emphasizes foods of plant origin; vegetarian excludes meat. Each overlaps with macrobiotic, but none necessarily follows its particular dietary system.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: macro-＝长，bio-＝生命：从“长寿理念”记住这套饮食法。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think 'long life': macro- plus bio- points to the longevity ideal behind the dietary system.

morphology.text: menses 作为独立词素整体记忆，不从结尾删出单数。相关词的构词：menstru-（月经）+ -al（形容词后缀）→ menstrual（月经的）。

etymology.text: 直接来自拉丁语 menses，原意是“月份”，是 mensis“月”的复数；由周期性的月份联想到月经周期。

usage_note: 正式医学用语，日常交流通常用 period。

senses.meaning_zh: 月经；经期排出的血液及组织
senses.meaning_en: menstruation, or the blood and tissue discharged during menstruation
senses.english_definition: A person's menses are the regular discharge of blood and tissue from the uterus when pregnancy has not occurred.
senses.collocation_en: onset of menses; cessation of menses
senses.collocation_zh: 月经来潮；月经停止
senses.sentence_en: The clinician asked about the date of her last menses.
senses.sentence_zh: 临床医生询问了她末次月经的日期。

etymology_story.zh: menses 直接来自拉丁语 mensis“月”的复数形式，字面意思是“数个月”。这个表示月份的词后来用于月经，反映了月经通常按月出现的周期性。
etymology_story.en: Menses comes directly from the Latin plural of mensis, meaning 'month,' so its literal meaning is 'months.' The term came to denote menstruation through its association with a roughly monthly cycle.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 menses 作为整体借词记忆；其复数形式继承自拉丁语，不能按普通英语规则去掉 -s 得到常用单数。相关词族包括 menstruate（来月经）、menstruation（月经；行经）、menstrual（月经的）、premenstrual（经前的）、postmenstrual（经后的）、intermenstrual（月经间期的）；这些词共享历史词源，并非直接由 menses 加后缀构成。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, menses is best treated as a whole borrowed word with an inherited Latin plural form; removing -s does not produce a normal English singular. The related family includes menstruate, menstruation, menstrual, premenstrual, postmenstrual, and intermenstrual; these share its historical base rather than being formed by adding suffixes directly to menses.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: menstruation（月经；行经）是中性的医学过程名称；period（月经；经期）是最常见的日常表达；menstrual flow（经血；月经量）更侧重排出的经血及其流量。menses 主要用于医学或正式语境。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Menstruation neutrally names the physiological process; period is the usual everyday term; menstrual flow emphasizes the discharge or its amount. Menses belongs mainly to medical or formal usage.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 拉丁语“月份”→按月出现的月经；词尾 -s 是继承的复数形式。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Latin 'months' points to the monthly cycle; the final -s belongs to an inherited plural form.

morphology.text: mono-（单一）+ coque（法语：壳）→ monocoque（单壳承载结构）。

etymology.text: 英语借自法语 monocoque，由“单一”和“壳”组成；想象外壳本身承受载荷，而不是只包住内部骨架。

usage_note: 用于汽车、飞机、自行车结构，强调壳体承担结构载荷。

etymology_story.zh: 英语借自法语 monocoque，由 mono-“单一”和 coque“壳”组成。该词最初用于航空结构，后来也用于汽车等领域，核心含义是让外壳承担结构载荷。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed French monocoque, formed from mono-, meaning 'single,' and coque, meaning 'shell.' Initially used in aviation, the term later spread to cars and other structures whose shells carry structural loads.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词为 mono-（单一）+ coque（法语“壳”）；在英语中是保留法语构词形式的借词。主要相关形式：monocoques（名词复数）、semi-monocoque（半硬壳式结构；半硬壳式的）；名词与形容词形式相同。
morphology_enriched.en: The formation is mono- ('single') + coque (French for 'shell'), retained in English as a borrowed compound. Principal related forms are monocoques (plural noun) and semi-monocoque (a structure, or construction, combining a load-bearing skin with supporting members); the noun and adjective have the same form.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: stressed-skin construction（承力蒙皮结构）强调蒙皮参与承载，也可包含内部骨架；unibody（整体承载式车身）强调汽车车身与底盘结构的一体化，不一定是严格的纯单壳结构；shell structure（壳体结构）是更宽泛的结构名称。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Stressed-skin construction emphasizes a load-bearing skin and may include an internal framework; unibody emphasizes an integrated vehicle body and chassis and need not be a pure monocoque; shell structure is the broader structural category.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: mono-＝一个，coque＝壳：让“一个壳”承担主要载荷。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Mono- means 'one' and coque means 'shell': picture one shell carrying the main loads.

etymology_story.zh: 蔬菜名称 napa 源于日语 nappa，意为“菜叶；绿叶蔬菜”，进入英语后主要见于 napa cabbage。皮革义是另一个来源不同的同形词，得名于美国加利福尼亚州纳帕，与这种皮革的早期生产有关。
etymology_story.en: The vegetable name napa comes from Japanese nappa, meaning 'vegetable leaves' or 'leafy greens,' and occurs chiefly in napa cabbage. The leather term is a separate word named after Napa, California, associated with its early production.

morphology_enriched.zh: 两个义项中的 napa 都作为整体词使用，没有可用于现代英语分析的词根加词缀结构。蔬菜义构成复合词 napa cabbage；皮革义有拼写变体 nappa，并构成 napa leather、nappa leather；没有常用的派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: In both meanings, napa functions as a whole word without a productive English root-and-affix breakdown. The vegetable sense forms napa cabbage; the leather sense has the spelling variant nappa and appears in napa leather and nappa leather; neither has a common derivational family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 蔬菜义：Chinese cabbage（中国白菜）范围较宽，有时也指其他白菜类；wombok（大白菜）是澳大利亚英语常用名称；Chinese leaf（大白菜）常见于英国英语。皮革义的 nappa 是同义拼写变体，不能把一般的 soft leather“软皮革”都视为纳帕革。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For the vegetable, Chinese cabbage is broader and can refer to other related cabbages; wombok is common in Australian English; Chinese leaf is common in British English. For leather, nappa is an equivalent spelling, while soft leather is a broader description.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 蔬菜义联想日语“菜叶”：一层层浅色白菜叶；皮革义联想纳帕地名：柔软皮革。
mnemonic_anchor.en: For the vegetable, picture the layers of pale leaves behind Japanese 'leafy greens'; for leather, connect the soft material with the place name Napa.

etymology_story.zh: 该词是由希腊语来源的构词成分在近代英语中组成的科技词，结合了表示摄影的 photo- 与表示显微图像的 micrograph。它指通过显微镜获得的照片，后来也用作动词，表示拍摄这类照片。
etymology_story.en: The word is a modern English scientific formation combining Greek-derived photo-, referring to photography, with micrograph, an image of something viewed microscopically. It names a photograph taken through a microscope and also became a verb for producing such a photograph.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词为 photo-（光；摄影）+ micro-（微小）+ -graph（记录；图像），也可分析为 photo- + micrograph。主要词族：photomicrographs（名词复数或动词第三人称单数）、photomicrographed（过去式及过去分词）、photomicrographing（现在分词）、photomicrography（显微摄影）、photomicrographic（显微摄影的）、photomicrographically（以显微摄影方式）、photomicrographer（显微摄影人员）。
morphology_enriched.en: The formation is photo- ('light; photography') + micro- ('small') + -graph ('record; image'), or photo- + micrograph. Principal family forms are photomicrographs, photomicrographed, photomicrographing, photomicrography (microscope photography), photomicrographic, photomicrographically, and photomicrographer.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: micrograph（显微图像）范围更宽，可包括不同显微成像方法产生的图像；microphotograph（微缩照片）通常指缩小到需要放大观看的照片，与 photomicrograph 的方向不同；close-up（特写照片）只强调近距离或细节拍摄，不要求使用显微镜。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Micrograph is broader and covers images produced by different microscopic imaging methods; microphotograph usually means a photograph reduced to a very small size, reversing the emphasis of photomicrograph; close-up emphasizes detail or proximity without requiring a microscope.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: photo＝拍照，micro＝微小：把显微镜下的微小世界拍下来。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Photo means photography and micro means small: photograph the tiny world seen through a microscope.

etymology_story.zh: 这个词形成于二十世纪初，由表示“照片”的 photo- 与法语来源的 montage“组装、拼接”结合而成。随着照片拼贴在现代艺术中的发展，它既指创作技法，也指由此产生的作品。
etymology_story.en: The word emerged in the early twentieth century, combining photo-, referring to photographs, with montage, a French-derived word meaning assembly. As photographic collage developed in modern art, the term came to name both the technique and the resulting artwork.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：photo-（照片）+ montage（拼接、蒙太奇）→ photomontage。主要词族：photomontages（复数）；photomontagist（照片拼贴艺术家，较少见）。相关词有 photograph（照片；拍照）、photographic（摄影的）和 montage（蒙太奇；拼接作品），但它们不是由 photomontage 派生而来。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: photo- (photograph) + montage (assembly or montage) → photomontage. Principal family members: photomontages (plural) and photomontagist (an artist who makes photomontages; less common). Related vocabulary includes photograph, photographic, and montage; these are not derivatives of photomontage.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: photo collage（照片拼贴）最接近，日常表达中常可互换；collage（拼贴）范围更广，可使用纸张、布料等材料；montage（蒙太奇、组合画面）也可指电影镜头或其他图像材料的组合。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Photo collage is the closest equivalent and is often interchangeable in everyday use; collage is broader and may incorporate paper, fabric, or other materials; montage can also describe arrangements of film shots or other visual material.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: photo 是照片，montage 是拼接：把照片拼成一幅新画面。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Photo means photographs; montage means assembly: assemble photographs into one new picture.

senses.sentence_zh: 作为皮亚杰学派的研究者，她强调儿童在建构知识中的主动作用。

etymology_story.zh: 这个词由瑞士心理学家 Jean Piaget（让·皮亚杰）的姓氏加后缀 -ian 构成。随着他的儿童认知发展理论传播，它既用作表示理论归属的形容词，也用作指称该学派支持者的名词。
etymology_story.en: The word combines the surname of Swiss psychologist Jean Piaget with the suffix -ian. As his account of children's cognitive development spread, it became both an adjective identifying his approach and a noun for someone who follows it.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：Piaget（皮亚杰）+ -ian（与……有关的；……学派的人）→ Piagetian。主要词族：Piagetians（名词复数）、Piagetianism（皮亚杰学说）、neo-Piagetian（新皮亚杰学派的；该学派成员）、post-Piagetian（后皮亚杰的）。通常保留首字母大写。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: Piaget + -ian (relating to, or an adherent of) → Piagetian. Principal family members include Piagetians, Piagetianism, neo-Piagetian (adjective or noun), and post-Piagetian (adjective). The initial capital is normally retained.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: cognitive-developmental（认知发展的）范围更广，不专指皮亚杰；constructivist（建构主义的）同样强调学习者主动建构知识，但不一定接受皮亚杰的阶段理论；neo-Piagetian（新皮亚杰学派的）指对其理论作进一步修订和发展的取向。这些都是相关表达，并非完全同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Cognitive-developmental is broader and does not identify Piaget specifically; constructivist likewise emphasizes the learner's active construction of knowledge but need not accept Piaget's stages; neo-Piagetian identifies approaches that revise and extend his theory. These are related expressions rather than exact synonyms.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: Piaget + -ian：连到皮亚杰本人、他的理论或他的学派成员。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Piaget + -ian connects the person, his theory, and the people who follow it.

etymology_story.en: The hairstyle takes its name from the title of Madame de Pompadour, the French royal mistress. In English it came to denote a hairstyle with a high front, and its use later extended to men's hairstyles.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语通常把 pompadour 作为不可再分析的借入词处理，不宜拆成貌似有意义的英语词根。主要词族：pompadours（复数）；pompadour + -ed → pompadoured（梳着蓬巴杜发型的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English generally treats pompadour as an unanalyzed borrowing; it should not be divided into apparent English roots. Principal family members are pompadours (plural) and pompadoured (wearing or arranged in a pompadour), formed with -ed.

synonyms_and_nuances.en: Quiff is the closest term but usually focuses on a raised section at the front; bouffant emphasizes overall fullness rather than specifically the front; updo is a broader category of hair arranged upward and need not have a pompadour's raised front.

senses.meaning_zh: 前列腺炎

etymology_story.zh: 这个医学词由表示“前列腺”的 prostat- 与希腊语来源的炎症后缀 -itis 构成。prostate 的名称最终源自希腊语中表示“站在前面者”的词，反映了早期解剖命名中的位置观念。
etymology_story.en: This medical term combines prostat-, meaning the prostate gland, with the Greek-derived inflammatory suffix -itis. Prostate ultimately comes from a Greek word meaning one who stands before, reflecting an anatomical idea of position.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：prostat-（前列腺）+ -itis（炎症）→ prostatitis，通常作不可数名词。共享同一医学词干的相关词有 prostate（前列腺）、prostatic（前列腺的）、prostatectomy（前列腺切除术）和 prostatism（前列腺症）；这些不是在 prostatitis 后直接加缀形成的词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: prostat- (prostate gland) + -itis (inflammation) → prostatitis, normally an uncountable noun. Related words sharing the medical stem include prostate, prostatic, prostatectomy (surgical removal of the prostate), and prostatism (a syndrome of urinary symptoms traditionally associated with prostate disorders). These are not formed by adding suffixes directly to prostatitis.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: prostatic inflammation、inflammation of the prostate 和 prostate inflammation 均表示“前列腺炎症”，属于解释性同义表达，而非三种不同疾病；其中 prostatic inflammation 更具医学语体，后两者更容易被普通读者理解。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Prostatic inflammation, inflammation of the prostate, and prostate inflammation are explanatory equivalents, not names for different diseases. Prostatic inflammation has a more technical register, while the other two expressions are more accessible to general readers.

etymology_story.zh: 这个词在十七世纪的宗教争论中进入英语，与法语 quiétisme 等欧洲语言中的对应形式相关，最终可追溯到拉丁语 quietus“安静的、安息的”。它后来从宗教上的内心静止与意志交托，扩展为对社会或政治行动的退避。
etymology_story.en: The word entered English in seventeenth-century religious controversy, alongside related European forms such as French quiétisme, ultimately tracing back to Latin quietus, meaning quiet or at rest. Its meaning later broadened from inward religious stillness and surrender of the will to withdrawal from social or political action.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可分析为 quiet（安静的）+ -ism（思想、主义）→ quietism，但这种现代分析不等于完整的历史借词路径。直接相关词族：quietist（寂静主义者；寂静主义的）、quietistic（寂静主义的；消极不干预的）；基础词 quiet 的常见词族还有 quietly（安静地）、quietness（安静）和 quieten（使安静；安静下来）。
morphology_enriched.en: Synchronically, the word can be analyzed as quiet + -ism (a doctrine or attitude), though this modern analysis does not fully describe its borrowing history. Its immediate family includes quietist (noun and adjective) and quietistic (adjective). Common members of the base word's family include quietly, quietness, and quieten.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: contemplation（静观、沉思）指精神活动，本身不意味着交托个人意志或退出公共事务；passivity（被动、消极）强调缺少主动行动，通常带贬义；nonintervention（不干预）指不介入的立场或政策，不一定出于宗教信念。这些词分别接近 quietism 的不同侧面。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Contemplation names reflective or spiritual activity without necessarily implying surrender of the will or withdrawal from public affairs; passivity emphasizes a lack of initiative and is often critical; nonintervention describes a position or policy of staying out of affairs without necessarily having a religious basis. Each overlaps with a different aspect of quietism.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: quiet + -ism：把“静下来”变成一种立场——内心静观，或退避行动。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Quiet + -ism turns stillness into a position: inward contemplation or withdrawal from action.

senses.meaning_zh: 幸灾乐祸；因他人的不幸而产生的快意
senses.meaning_en: Pleasure at someone else's misfortune.
senses.english_definition: Schadenfreude is the pleasure you feel when something unfortunate happens to someone else.

etymology_story.zh: 英语在十九世纪借入德语 Schadenfreude，由 Schaden“损害、不幸”和 Freude“快乐”组成。这个组合直接表达了从别人遭遇的不幸中获得快乐的含义。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed Schadenfreude from German in the nineteenth century, combining Schaden, meaning damage or misfortune, with Freude, meaning joy. The compound directly expresses the idea of taking pleasure in another person's troubles.

morphology_enriched.zh: 这是整体借入英语的德语复合词：Schaden（损害、不幸）+ Freude（快乐）；这两个部分不是能在英语中自由构词的词缀。通常作不可数名词，现代常用英语中没有稳定、常见的派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: This is a German compound borrowed intact into English: Schaden (damage or misfortune) + Freude (joy); its components are not productive English affixes. It is normally an uncountable noun and has no established family of common English derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: gloating（得意扬扬的幸灾乐祸）强调明显表现出来的满足感；malicious pleasure（恶意的快感）含义更宽；glee（欢喜、窃喜）本身不一定涉及他人的不幸。schadenfreude 专指以别人的不幸为快乐来源。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Gloating emphasizes conspicuous satisfaction; malicious pleasure is broader; glee means lively delight and need not involve anyone's suffering. Schadenfreude specifically identifies another person's misfortune as the source of pleasure.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 别人的“不幸”加上自己的“快乐”，就是幸灾乐祸。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Someone else's misfortune plus your joy equals schadenfreude.

etymology_story.zh: 英语在十九世纪以 sextuple“六重的”为基础，仿照 triplet 等词构成 sextuplet；sextuple 可追溯至表示“六重”的中世纪拉丁语 sextuplus。这个词既用于一次出生的六个孩子，也用于其他六个一组的事物及音乐中的六连音。
etymology_story.en: English formed sextuplet in the nineteenth century from sextuple, meaning sixfold, on the model of words such as triplet; sextuple ultimately comes from Medieval Latin sextuplus. The word is used for children born six at a time, other groups of six, and musical groups of six notes.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：sextuple（六重的）去掉末尾不发音的 e + -et（仿照 triplet 等词的结尾）→ sextuplet。词族包括 sextuplet、sextuplets，以及相关基础词 sextuple（六重的；使增至六倍）、sextuples、sextupled、sextupling；sixfold 是同义表达，不是派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: sextuple (sixfold), with its final silent e removed, + -et, modeled on endings in words such as triplet, gives sextuplet. The family includes sextuplet, sextuplets, and the related base sextuple (sixfold; multiply by six), with sextuples, sextupled, and sextupling; sixfold is an equivalent expression rather than a derivative.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: one of six siblings born together（同次出生的六名手足之一）是婴儿义的解释性近义表达；group of six（六个一组）适用于一般分组；sextet（六人组、六重奏）常用于音乐家或表演组合，不表示其中的某一个孩子。六连音义没有同样常用且完全等值的单词近义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: One of six siblings born together paraphrases the birth sense; group of six covers the general grouping sense; sextet commonly describes six performers or a musical composition for them, rather than one child from a multiple birth. The musical sense has no equally common exact single-word synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从 sextuple“六重”抓住“六个一起”：六胞胎、六个一组、六连音。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with sextuple, meaning sixfold: six babies together, six things together, or six notes together.

etymology_story.zh: 英语借自法语 trappiste，名称来自法国诺曼底的 La Trappe 修道院，该院与十七世纪熙笃会的严格修行改革密切相关。名称后来用于这一传统的成员，并作形容词修饰其修道院、生活方式和相关产品。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed French trappiste, named after La Trappe Abbey in Normandy, which was closely associated with a seventeenth-century reform promoting stricter Cistercian observance. The name came to identify members of this tradition and to describe their monasteries, way of life, and associated products.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词关系：Trapp-（源于地名 La Trappe）+ -ist（成员、追随者）→ Trappist；不是由英语 trap“陷阱”构成。词族包括 Trappist、复数 Trappists、Trappistine（特拉普派修女；修女的）、复数 Trappistines，以及较少见的 Trappism（特拉普派的制度或修行方式）；名词和形容词通常都保留首字母大写。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: Trapp-, from the place name La Trappe, + -ist (member or follower) gives Trappist; it is not formed from English trap. The family includes Trappist, plural Trappists, Trappistine (a Trappist nun; relating to such nuns), plural Trappistines, and the less common Trappism (the system or practices of the Trappists); both noun and adjective normally retain the capital letter.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Cistercian（熙笃会成员）范围较广，Trappist 属于其中的严规传统；monk（修士）泛指男性修道者；monastic（修道院的、修道生活的）可作相关形容词，但不指明特拉普派身份。这些词只能在相应语境中近似替换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Cistercian is broader, with Trappist identifying the strict-observance tradition; monk means a male member of a religious community more generally; monastic is a related adjective that does not specify the Trappist order. These are contextual alternatives rather than exact equivalents.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: La Trappe 是修道院名；Trappist 就是这一修行传统的成员或相关事物。
mnemonic_anchor.en: La Trappe names the abbey; Trappist names a member of its religious tradition or something associated with it.

etymology_story.zh: trigeminal 源于解剖学拉丁语 nervus trigeminus“三叉神经”；拉丁语 trigeminus 意为“三重的”，由 tri-“三”和与 geminus“成双的、孪生的”相关的成分构成。名称指这条神经的三条主要分支，不能把它机械地理解为“三乘二”。
etymology_story.en: Trigeminal derives from anatomical Latin nervus trigeminus, the trigeminal nerve; Latin trigeminus means threefold and combines tri-, meaning three, with an element related to geminus, meaning twin or paired. The name refers to the nerve's three main divisions, rather than literally meaning three times two.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代专业构词可分析为 trigemin-（三叉神经词干）+ -al（……的）；历史上可进一步联系 tri-“三”和 gemin-“孪生、成双”。相关形式包括 trigeminus（拉丁语解剖名称）、trigeminal、较少见的 trigeminally（经由三叉神经地）；trigeminy（三联律）与其有词源联系，但不是 trigeminal 的直接派生词，也不是同义词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern technical vocabulary, the structure is trigemin- (the trigeminal nerve stem) + -al (relating to); historically, the stem connects with tri- (three) and gemin- (twin or paired). Related forms include trigeminus (the Latin anatomical name), trigeminal, and the uncommon adverb trigeminally (through or by means of the trigeminal nerve); trigeminy is etymologically related but is neither a direct derivative nor a synonym.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: fifth cranial nerve（第五脑神经）是名词义的等值名称；cranial（脑神经的、颅的）范围更广；facial（面部的、面神经的）只表示相关部位或另一条神经，不能与 trigeminal 直接互换。形容词义没有常用的精确单词近义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Fifth cranial nerve is an equivalent anatomical name for the noun; cranial is broader; facial refers to the face or, in nerve terminology, a different cranial nerve, so it is not interchangeable with trigeminal. The adjective has no common exact single-word synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: tri- 提示“三”：一条脑神经分出三大支，通向面部。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Tri- cues three: one cranial nerve with three major divisions serving the face.

etymology_story.en: Wastrel was formed in the nineteenth century from waste with the disparaging ending -rel. It applies the idea of waste to a person who squanders money, time, or opportunities.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：waste（浪费）去掉末尾不发音的 e + -rel（带贬义的人称名词结尾）→ wastrel；复数为 wastrels。相关词族包括 waste、wastes、wasted、wasting、waster、wasters、wasteful、wastefully、wastefulness 和 wastage；这些词主要由共同基础词 waste 派生，并非全部由 wastrel 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: waste, with its final silent e removed, + -rel, a disparaging personal-noun ending, gives wastrel; the plural is wastrels. The related family includes waste, wastes, wasted, wasting, waster, wasters, wasteful, wastefully, wastefulness, and wastage; these mainly derive from the shared base waste rather than from wastrel itself.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: spendthrift（挥霍者）侧重花钱无度；idler（懒汉、闲人）侧重不工作、无所事事；profligate（放荡挥霍者）兼有挥霍和生活放纵的意味。wastrel 常把浪费钱财、虚度人生和无所作为几层贬义合在一起。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Spendthrift emphasizes excessive spending; idler emphasizes avoiding work; profligate suggests both extravagance and self-indulgent living. Wastrel often combines the judgments that someone wastes resources, squanders their life, and achieves little.

synonyms_and_nuances.en: Automatic focusing is the full descriptive equivalent; AF is the standard photographic abbreviation; auto-focusing is a hyphenated form often used to emphasize the focusing process.

morphology_enriched.en: Baobab is an unanalyzable borrowed base in modern English; its plural is baobabs, and it has no common direct derivatives. Baobab fruit and baobab powder are noun combinations; baobab-like is a freely formed descriptive word.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 无适用于所有语境的常用精确同义词。Adansonia（猴面包树属）是科学属名；upside-down tree（倒栽树）是形象俗称；bottle tree（瓶树）强调膨大的树干，也用于其他树种，不能随意替换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no common exact synonym suitable for every context. Adansonia is the scientific genus name; upside-down tree is an informal descriptive name; bottle tree refers to a swollen trunk and also names other trees, so it is not an exact substitute.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 整词绑定一个轮廓：粗大的树干，加上像倒置树根的枝条。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Attach the whole word to one silhouette: an enormous trunk topped by branches resembling upside-down roots.

etymology_story.zh: carob 经法语及中世纪拉丁语形式传入英语，最终源自阿拉伯语 kharrūb，指角豆树或其豆荚。英语中的含义由树木和果实进一步扩展到以豆荚制成的食品原料。
etymology_story.en: Carob entered English through French and medieval Latin forms, ultimately from Arabic kharrūb, referring to the tree or its pods. Its English meanings extended from the tree and fruit to food ingredients made from the pods.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 carob 是不可进一步分析的借入词，没有常用的直接派生词。表示树或单个豆荚时可数，复数为 carobs；表示食品原料时通常不可数。常见组合有 carob tree（角豆树）、carob pod（角豆荚）、carob powder（角豆粉）和 carob flour（角豆粉）。
morphology_enriched.en: Carob is an unanalyzable borrowed base in modern English and has no common direct derivatives. It is countable for trees or individual pods, with plural carobs, but usually uncountable for the food ingredient. Common combinations include carob tree, carob pod, carob powder, and carob flour.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: locust bean（角豆）和 Saint John's bread（圣约翰面包）都是角豆或其豆荚的传统名称，后者较少见；carob powder（角豆粉）则专指加工后的粉末，不能替代指树木的 carob。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Locust bean and Saint John's bread are traditional names for carob or its pods, with the latter less common; carob powder specifically identifies the processed powder and cannot replace carob when the tree is meant.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 一条实物链：角豆树 → 甜豆荚 → 磨成棕色粉，常代替可可。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Follow one physical chain: carob tree → sweet pods → brown powder often used instead of cocoa.

etymology_story.zh: coextensive 由表示“共同”的 co- 与 extensive 构成；extensive 最终与拉丁语 extendere“伸展”有关。其核心是“两者延伸到相同范围”，后来也用于抽象领域和逻辑学中的外延比较。
etymology_story.en: Coextensive combines co-, 'together,' with extensive, ultimately related to Latin extendere, 'to stretch out.' Its central idea is that two things extend equally far, also applied to abstract scope and logical extension.

morphology_enriched.zh: 直接构词：co-（共同）+ extensive（延伸的、范围广的）→ coextensive。直接相关形式有 coextensively（范围相同地）、coextensiveness（范围相同性）和 coextension（共同延伸；外延一致）；较大的相关词族包括 extend、extended、extension、extent、extensive、extensively、extensiveness、extendable、extensible 和 extensibility。此处 extensive 不能机械译成“广泛的”。
morphology_enriched.en: Immediate formation: co- ('together') + extensive → coextensive. Directly related forms include coextensively, coextensiveness, and coextension; the broader related family includes extend, extended, extension, extent, extensive, extensively, extensiveness, extendable, extensible, and extensibility. Here extensive contributes the idea of extent, rather than simply 'very broad.'

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: coterminous（边界或期限相同的）强调共同边界或起止点；coincident（重合的）强调位置或发生时间重合；congruent（全等的、一致的）在几何中强调形状和大小相同，而 coextensive 强调覆盖范围或外延完全一致。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Coterminous emphasizes matching boundaries or endpoints; coincident emphasizes matching positions or timing; congruent emphasizes matching shape and size in geometry, whereas coextensive emphasizes identical coverage or extension.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: co-＝共同，extent＝范围：两张透明地图叠起来，覆盖区域完全重合。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link co- with 'together' and extent with 'coverage': two transparent maps overlap across exactly the same area.

etymology_story.zh: 该词经法语进入中古英语，源自中世纪拉丁语 confraternitas，意为“兄弟情谊；兄弟团体”，其中 con- 表示“共同”，frater 表示“兄弟”。它主要用于宗教互助组织，后来也可泛指因共同兴趣或职业而结成的团体。
etymology_story.en: The word entered Middle English through French from Medieval Latin confraternitas, meaning brotherhood, with con- meaning together and frater meaning brother. It became associated especially with religious societies and also developed a broader use for groups united by shared interests or professions.

morphology_enriched.zh: 可按学术词素分析为 con-（共同）+ fratern-（兄弟）+ -ity（状态或集合）；fratern- 是黏着词干，不能单独使用。复数为 confraternities；同族词包括 confraternal（兄弟会的，少用）、confrater（同会成员，少用），以及 fraternity（兄弟情谊；兄弟会）、fraternal（兄弟般的）、fraternally（友爱地）、fraternize/fraternise（友好交往）和 fraternization/fraternisation（友好交往）。
morphology_enriched.en: A learned morphological analysis is con- (together) + fratern- (brother) + -ity (a state or collective entity); fratern- is a bound stem. The plural is confraternities; family members include the uncommon confraternal and confrater, alongside fraternity, fraternal, fraternally, fraternize/fraternise, and fraternization/fraternisation.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: brotherhood（兄弟情谊；兄弟团体）更强调成员间的纽带；fraternity（兄弟会；同业群体）也常指大学男生联谊会；association（协会）最中性，不含宗教或兄弟情谊意味。confraternity 较正式，尤其容易使人联想到宗教组织。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Brotherhood emphasizes bonds between members; fraternity can denote a professional group or a male university society; association is neutral and carries no necessary religious or brotherly implication. Confraternity is formal and particularly associated with religious organizations.

etymology_story.en: Middle English borrowed covey from Anglo-French covee, meaning a brood, related to a verb meaning to brood or incubate and ultimately to Latin cubare, to lie down. Its meaning broadened from a brood to a small group of birds and then figuratively to a small group of people.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 covey 是不可再作常用词缀拆分的单纯词，复数为 coveys。它没有常用的固定派生词；covey-like（像一小群鸟或人的）可临时组合，但不是常见的独立词族成员。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, covey is a simple base with no productive internal affix structure; its plural is coveys. It has no common established derivatives; covey-like can be formed freely but is not a common independent member of its word family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: flock（鸟群）适用范围最广，数量可大可小；brood（一窝幼鸟）强调由同一亲鸟孵育的幼鸟；bevy（一群）可用于某些鸟或人。covey 尤其指鹌鹑、鹧鸪等组成的小群。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Flock is the broad term for a group of birds of varying size; brood emphasizes young birds hatched or cared for together; bevy describes groups of certain birds or people. Covey particularly suggests a small group of quail, partridges, or similar birds.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“一窝雏鸟”想到“一小群鸟”，再想到“一小群人”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture one brood becoming a little bird group, then a little group of people.

etymology_story.zh: 该词源自希腊语 diptychos“折成两部分的”，由表示“二”的 di- 和表示“折叠”的词干组成，经晚期拉丁语 diptycha 传入英语。它早先指可折合的双叶书写板，后来用于双联画，并扩展到其他由两部分组成的作品。
etymology_story.en: The word comes through Late Latin diptycha from Greek diptychos, meaning folded in two, combining elements meaning two and fold. It first referred to paired folding writing tablets and later to two-panel artworks and other works arranged in two related parts.

morphology_enriched.zh: 可按古典词素分析为 di-（二）+ -ptych（折叠；面板），但在现代英语中通常作为完整艺术术语使用；复数为 diptychs。少用形容词为 diptychal（双联画的）；相关构词系列包括 triptych（三联画）和 polyptych（多联画），它们是共享词素的相关词，并非由 diptych 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Its classical components are di- (two) + -ptych (fold or panel), though modern English generally treats it as a complete art term; the plural is diptychs. Diptychal is an uncommon adjective; related formations include triptych and polyptych, which share a combining element rather than deriving directly from diptych.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: two-panel work（双面板作品）是直接说明结构的中性表达；pair（成对物）只表示数量关系，不保证艺术上的整体性；pendant（配对作品）指与另一件作品相配的一件。diptych 明确把两个部分视为一个整体。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Two-panel work neutrally describes the physical structure; pair indicates two items without necessarily implying artistic unity; pendant denotes one artwork designed as a companion to another. Diptych explicitly presents two parts as a single artistic whole.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: di- 是“二”：两扇画板合成一件作品。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Di- means two: two panels, one artwork.
