morphology_enriched.zh: spatio-（空间的组合形式，含连接元音 -o-）＋temporal（时间的；tempor-＋-al）→ spatiotemporal；也写作 spatio-temporal。直接派生：spatiotemporally（在时空上）、spatiotemporality（时空性，专业用语）。相关词族：spatial（空间的）、spatially（在空间上）、spatiality（空间性）、temporal（时间的）、temporally（在时间上）、temporality（时间性）；该词中的 temporal 不指“颞部的”。
morphology_enriched.en: Spatio- is the combining form for space, including the linking vowel -o-; it combines with temporal, analysable as tempor- + -al, to form spatiotemporal. The spelling spatio-temporal also occurs. Direct derivatives include spatiotemporally and the specialized noun spatiotemporality. Related family members include spatial, spatially, spatiality, temporal, temporally, and temporality; temporal here concerns time rather than the anatomical temple.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: spatial and temporal（空间和时间的）是最直接的释义性近义表达；space-time（时空的，作前置修饰语）常见于物理学，尤其用于把时空视为整体；four-dimensional（四维的）强调维数，只有在三维空间加一维时间的语境中才与 spatiotemporal 接近，并非普遍同义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Spatial and temporal is the closest explanatory equivalent. Attributive space-time is common in physics, especially when space and time are treated as a unified framework. Four-dimensional emphasizes the number of dimensions and overlaps only when these comprise three spatial dimensions and one temporal dimension.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: spatio- 问“在哪里”，temporal 问“何时” → 同时看地点与时间。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Spatio- asks 'where'; temporal asks 'when' → examine place and time together.

etymology_story.en: Terabyte combines the metric prefix tera- with the computing term byte; tera- comes from Greek teras, meaning 'monster,' and represents 10 to the twelfth power in measurement. Older and some informal usage also applies terabyte to 2 to the fortieth bytes, a binary quantity explicitly named a tebibyte (TiB).

morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: tera- (10¹², one trillion) + byte; the plural is terabytes and the symbol is TB. Gigabyte and petabyte belong to the same unit-naming series; tebibyte (TiB) is a related unit with a different value, not an inflected form of terabyte.

synonyms_and_nuances.en: One trillion bytes is an exact equivalent, and TB is the unit symbol. Tebibyte (TiB, 2⁴⁰ bytes) is a commonly confused related unit, approximately 1.10 TB; terabit (Tb) counts bits and equals one eighth of a terabyte.

etymology_story.en: Zirconium is a New Latin element name based on zircon, the zirconium-bearing mineral. Zircon reached English through German and other languages and is generally traced to Persian zargun, meaning 'gold-coloured,' referring to the colour of some zircon stones.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词分析：zircon（锆石）+ -ium（元素名称词尾）。相关词族包括 zirconia（氧化锆，通常指二氧化锆）、zirconic（锆的，主要见于专业化学术语）、zirconate（锆酸盐）和 zirconiferous（含锆的）；这些词共享 zircon- 词干，并非全都直接由 zirconium 加后缀构成。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern analysis: zircon + -ium, an element-name ending. Related family members include zirconia ('zirconium oxide, usually the dioxide'), zirconic ('relating to zirconium,' chiefly in technical chemical terminology), zirconate ('a salt of a zirconic acid'), and zirconiferous ('containing zirconium'); these share the zircon- stem rather than all being direct suffixal derivatives of zirconium.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Zr 是锆的化学符号，可在技术语境中指同一元素；zirconium metal（锆金属）强调金属形态。zircon（锆石）是含锆的硅酸盐矿物，zirconia（氧化锆）是锆的氧化物，两者都不是元素锆的同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Zr is the chemical symbol and can denote the same element in technical contexts; zirconium metal emphasizes its metallic form. Zircon is a zirconium-bearing silicate mineral, while zirconia is zirconium oxide, so neither is a synonym for the element.

senses.meaning_zh: 具有严整整体结构的；有关体系构建的
senses.meaning_en: relating to the systematic organization of a complex whole

etymology_story.zh: architectonic 经拉丁语 architectonicus 源自希腊语 arkhitektonikos，与 arkhitekton（总工匠、建筑师）有关，其历史成分包含 arkhi-（首要的）和 tekton（工匠、建造者）。词义从建筑的规划与构造延伸到哲学体系、艺术作品等复杂整体的组织。
etymology_story.en: Architectonic comes through Latin architectonicus from Greek arkhitektonikos, related to arkhitekton ('master builder'), historically combining arkhi- ('chief') and tekton ('builder or craftsman'). Its meaning extended from architectural planning and construction to the organization of complex wholes such as philosophical systems and works of art.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代分析可写为 architecton-（建筑师、整体构造这一学术词干）+ -ic（……的）；architecton- 在现代普通英语中不是能自由使用的词。直接相关形式有 architectonically（在建筑构造上；在整体组织上）和 architectonics（建筑构造；体系构造学）；architect（建筑师）、architecture（建筑学；架构）、architectural（建筑的）属于同源词族。
morphology_enriched.en: A modern learned analysis is architecton- (a stem associated with building and overall organization) + -ic ('relating to'); architecton- is not a freely used word in ordinary modern English. Closely related forms are architectonically and architectonics ('architectural or systematic organization'); architect, architecture, and architectural belong to the same historical word family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: architectural（建筑的）是谈论建筑时更常用的词；structural（结构的）强调各部分的配置与关系；systematic（系统的）强调按明确方法或体系组织。architectonic 更突出复杂整体经过统筹形成的结构，常见于正式或学术语境。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Architectural is the more usual word for matters concerning buildings. Structural emphasizes the arrangement and relationships of parts, while systematic emphasizes organization according to a method or system. Architectonic particularly suggests the planned structure of a complex whole and is chiefly formal or academic.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把建筑师组织整座建筑的思路，迁移到组织整部作品或整个体系。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a master builder organizing a whole building, then extend that idea to an entire work or system.

etymology_story.zh: 借自法语 beaucoup，法语历史结构为 beau（大的、好的）＋ coup（击打，也曾引申指一堆或一份），整体发展为“很多”。英语至少在十九世纪已将其用作带诙谐色彩的数量修饰语。[词源说明](https://www.etymonline.com/word/beaucoup)；[英语用法史](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/beaucoup)。
etymology_story.en: Borrowed from French beaucoup, historically beau ('fine, great') + coup ('stroke,' also extended to a heap or quantity), which developed the meaning 'a lot.' English has used it as a playful quantity modifier since at least the nineteenth century. [Etymology](https://www.etymonline.com/word/beaucoup); [English usage history](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/beaucoup).

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中视为不可再作生产性拆分的整体借词；beau＋coup 是法语历史结构，不是英语词根加词缀。限定词、形容词和副词用法均不变形；罕见名词用法表示“大量”，复数为 beaucoups；另有 bookoo、boocoo、buku 等非正式拼写，无常用英语派生词。[词形与词类](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/beaucoup)。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, this is a whole-word borrowing without a productive English root-and-affix analysis; beau + coup belongs to its French history. Determiner, adjective, and adverb uses are invariant; a rare noun meaning 'an abundance' has the plural beaucoups. Informal spellings include bookoo, boocoo, and buku; there are no common English affixal derivatives. [Forms and word classes](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/beaucoup).

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: many（许多）用于复数可数名词；much（大量）用于不可数名词；a lot of（许多、大量）两类名词均可用。beaucoup 也能修饰这两类名词，但具有鲜明的美式俚语和诙谐色彩；副词用法可对应 a lot 或 very much（很多、非常）。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Many modifies plural count nouns; much modifies uncountable nouns; a lot of works with both. Beaucoup can also modify either type but sounds distinctly slangy and playful in American English; its adverbial equivalents are a lot and very much.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住历史上的“一大堆”：beaucoup bucks＝一大堆钱；作副词则表示“多得很”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor it to the historical idea of a great heap: beaucoup bucks means a heap of money; adverbially, it means a lot.

usage_note: 药理学中常指给药后活性物质进入全身循环的程度及速度；不能仅凭生物利用度判断疗效。

senses.meaning_zh: 生物利用度；物质被吸收并可供机体利用的程度与速率
senses.meaning_en: The extent and rate at which a substance is absorbed and becomes available for biological activity.
senses.english_definition: The bioavailability of a drug or nutrient is how much of it becomes available for use in the body and how quickly this happens.
senses.collocation_zh: 口服生物利用度；提高生物利用度
senses.sentence_en: The researchers compared the oral bioavailability of the two formulations.
senses.sentence_zh: 研究人员比较了这两种制剂的口服生物利用度。

etymology_story.zh: 这是二十世纪形成的科学术语，由源自希腊语 bios（生命）的 bio- 与 availability（可利用性）结合而成。该词将一般的“可获得、可利用”具体化为物质被吸收并到达生理作用部位的程度与速率。[术语释义与历史](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/bioavailability)。
etymology_story.en: This twentieth-century scientific term combines bio-, ultimately from Greek bios ('life'), with availability. It specializes the general idea of being available into the extent and rate at which a substance is absorbed or becomes available at a site of biological activity. [Definition and history](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/bioavailability).

morphology_enriched.zh: bio-（生物、生命）＋availability（可利用性）→bioavailability；availability 由 available＋-ity 构成，词尾 -able 在名词化时变为 -ability。核心词族：available（可获得的、可利用的）、availability（可获得性、可利用性）、unavailable（不可获得的）、unavailability（不可获得性）、bioavailable（可被生物体吸收利用的）、bioavailability（生物利用度）；后者通常为不可数名词，比较不同数值或类型时可用复数 bioavailabilities。
morphology_enriched.en: Bio- ('life, biological') + availability → bioavailability; availability is formed from available + -ity, with -able becoming -ability. The core family comprises available, availability, unavailable, unavailability, bioavailable, and bioavailability. Bioavailability is normally uncountable, but bioavailabilities can refer to different values or types.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有适用于所有语境的严格同义词。absorption（吸收）侧重物质进入机体的过程；bioaccessibility（生物可及性）侧重物质从食物等基质中释放、可供吸收的程度；systemic availability（体循环可利用性）在药代动力学中与生物利用度关系密切，侧重物质进入体循环后的可利用程度。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no exact synonym that works in every context. Absorption concerns entry into the body; bioaccessibility concerns release from a matrix, such as food, so that absorption can occur; systemic availability is closely related in pharmacokinetics and emphasizes availability in the systemic circulation.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: bio＝生命，availability＝可利用性：吃进去多少之外，还要看身体实际能用到多少、多快能用到。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Bio means life and availability means being usable: ask how much the body can actually use, and how quickly.

etymology_story.zh: 英语 blockhouse 的确切来源尚有争议，可能与中古荷兰语 blokhuis 或德语 Blockhaus 等相关，早期指封锁通道或据点的独立小堡。后来可指厚木构筑的防御建筑，并扩展到用于危险作业的坚固防护观察室。[词源说明](https://www.etymonline.com/word/blockhouse)；[现代义项](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/blockhouse)。
etymology_story.en: The precise origin of English blockhouse is uncertain, but it may be connected with Middle Dutch blokhuis or German Blockhaus, originally describing a detached fort blocking an approach. It later denoted a heavy-timber defensive building and extended to a protected observation building for hazardous operations. [Etymology](https://www.etymonline.com/word/blockhouse); [Modern senses](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/blockhouse).

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代形式可分析为 block（阻挡；大块材料）＋house（建筑物）组成的复合名词，但这种分析不能证明其确切历史来源。复数 blockhouses；没有常用的直接词缀派生形式；blockhouse wall（碉堡墙体）等结构中的 blockhouse 仍是名词作前置修饰语。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern form is analyzable as the compound noun block ('obstruction; solid piece of material') + house ('building'), although this analysis does not establish its precise historical origin. The plural is blockhouses; there are no common direct affixal derivatives. In expressions such as blockhouse wall, blockhouse remains a noun used attributively.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: bunker（掩体、地堡）强调防护，常位于地下或半地下；pillbox（小型机枪碉堡）通常更小，专供从射孔开火；fort（堡垒）是更宽泛的防御工事名称，规模也可能更大。blockhouse 强调可独立据守的坚固建筑，另有危险作业防护室之义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Bunker emphasizes shelter and is often underground or partly underground; pillbox usually denotes a small firing position with loopholes; fort is a broader term and may describe a much larger defensive structure. Blockhouse emphasizes a strong building that can be defended independently and also has a hazardous-operation shelter sense.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: block＋house：一座能挡住进攻或危险冲击的坚固房屋。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Block + house: picture a strong building that blocks an attack or shields people from a dangerous blast.

senses.meaning_zh: 棉铃虫；以棉铃为食的某些蛾类幼虫，也可指相应蛾类
senses.meaning_en: A caterpillar that feeds on cotton bolls, or a moth species with such larvae.
senses.english_definition: A bollworm is a caterpillar that damages cotton by feeding on its developing seed capsules, and the name can also refer to the moth it becomes.

etymology_story.zh: 这是 boll（棉铃，即棉花的果实）与 worm（虫状幼体）的英语复合词，名称直接描述幼虫取食棉铃的习性。该名称在十九世纪已有记录，可用于不止一种具有这种食性的蛾类。[释义与历史](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/bollworm)。
etymology_story.en: This English compound joins boll ('the seed capsule of cotton') with worm ('a wormlike larva'), naming the insect after its feeding habit. Recorded in the nineteenth century, it can designate more than one moth species whose larvae feed on cotton bolls. [Definition and history](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/bollworm).

morphology_enriched.zh: boll（棉铃）＋worm（虫状幼体）→bollworm；复数 bollworms。没有常用的直接词缀派生形式；cotton bollworm（棉铃虫）、pink bollworm（红铃虫）和 African bollworm（非洲棉铃虫）是相关名称，不是派生词，其中不同名称的物种对应关系取决于地区和专业语境。
morphology_enriched.en: Boll ('cotton seed capsule') + worm ('wormlike larva') → bollworm; plural bollworms. There are no common direct affixal derivatives. Cotton bollworm, pink bollworm, and African bollworm are related names rather than derivatives, and their species references depend on region and technical context.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: caterpillar（毛虫、鳞翅目幼虫）范围更广，不一定危害棉花；cotton bollworm（棉铃虫）可用作更具体的害虫名称；corn earworm（玉米穗虫）在北美可与 bollworm 指同一种昆虫 Helicoverpa zea，但不能替代所有地区、所有物种的 bollworm。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Caterpillar is broader and does not imply damage to cotton; cotton bollworm can be a more specific pest name; corn earworm can refer to the same North American species, Helicoverpa zea, but is not interchangeable with every regional or species-specific use of bollworm.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: boll＝棉铃，worm＝虫状幼体：记住钻进棉铃取食的幼虫。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Boll means cotton capsule and worm suggests a larva: picture a caterpillar feeding inside a cotton boll.

etymology_story.zh: 该词通常分析为 cock（公鸡）＋sure（确信的），但具体形成动因仍有不确定性。早期可较中性地表示“确信的”，后来主要发展为带贬义的“过分自信、自以为是”。[词源与早期含义](https://www.etymonline.com/word/cocksure)；[现代释义](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/cocksure)。
etymology_story.en: The word is usually analyzed as cock ('rooster') + sure, although the precise motivation remains uncertain. Earlier uses could mean 'certain' without strong criticism, whereas modern usage chiefly suggests excessive or presumptuous confidence. [Etymology and earlier meaning](https://www.etymonline.com/word/cocksure); [Modern definitions](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/cocksure).

morphology_enriched.zh: cock（公鸡）＋sure（确信的）构成复合形容词；直接派生词为 cocksurely（过分自信地）和 cocksureness（过分自信、自以为是）。通常用 more cocksure、most cocksure 表示比较级和最高级；相关基础词族有 sure（确信的）、surely（肯定地）、sureness（确信）和 unsure（不确定的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Cock ('rooster') + sure forms a compound adjective; its direct derivatives are cocksurely ('in an excessively confident manner') and cocksureness ('excessive confidence'). Comparison normally uses more cocksure and most cocksure. The related base-word family includes sure, surely, sureness, and unsure.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: overconfident（过于自信的）最直接地表示信心超过实际依据；cocky（自负的）更强调外露的得意和神气；arrogant（傲慢的）更强调自视高人一等、轻视他人。cocksure 尤其突出“认定自己绝不会错或绝不会失败”。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Overconfident directly describes confidence exceeding its justification; cocky emphasizes visibly smug or swaggering confidence; arrogant emphasizes superiority and disregard for others. Cocksure particularly suggests certainty that one cannot be wrong or fail.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 sure 想成昂首公鸡般的“我准没错”：这是帮助记忆的形象，不是已证实的完整词源。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture sure with a rooster's swagger: 'I cannot possibly be wrong.' This image is a memory aid, not a proven full etymology.

etymology_story.zh: 由 crotchet 的“怪念头、执拗想法”义加 -y 构成。Crotchet 原指“小钩”，经法语追溯至表示“钩”的词，后来发展出古怪念头的比喻义，crotchety 则用于描述相应的乖戾性情。
etymology_story.en: Crotchety was formed from crotchet, meaning a peculiar or stubborn notion, plus -y. Crotchet originally meant a small hook and came through French; its later figurative meaning supplied the basis for the adjective describing an irritable, contrary temperament.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：crotchet（怪念头）+ -y（具有……特点的）→ crotchety。常见相关形式：crotchets（名词复数）、crotchetiness（乖戾；易怒）、crotchetily（乖戾地）；比较级和最高级通常用 more crotchety、most crotchety。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: crotchet (a peculiar notion) + -y (characterized by) → crotchety. Related forms include crotchets, crotchetiness, and crotchetily; comparison is normally expressed with more crotchety and most crotchety.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: grumpy 强调当下或惯常的坏脾气；irritable 强调容易受到刺激而生气；cantankerous 强调爱争执、难相处。Crotchety 常兼有古怪、执拗和爱抱怨的意味。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Grumpy emphasizes a bad mood; irritable emphasizes being easily provoked; cantankerous emphasizes being argumentative and difficult. Crotchety often combines irritability with eccentricity, stubbornness, and habitual complaining.

etymology_story.en: Dura is short for the Latin anatomical term dura mater, literally 'hard mother,' with dura meaning 'hard.' The name describes the tough protective outer membrane surrounding the brain and spinal cord.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 dura 是 dura mater 的缩略名称，不宜拆成英语前后缀。相关形式：dura → dural（硬膜的，去掉词尾 a 加 -al）；durae（拉丁式复数）；subdural（硬膜下的）、epidural／extradural（硬膜外的）、intradural（硬膜内的）、durotomy（硬膜切开术）、duraplasty（硬膜成形术）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, dura is a shortened form of dura mater rather than an English prefix–suffix construction. Related forms include dural (dura minus final a + -al), the Latin plural durae, subdural, epidural/extradural, intradural, durotomy, and duraplasty.

synonyms_and_nuances.en: Dura mater is the full name for the same structure; pachymeninx is a less common technical synonym. Meninges is broader, referring collectively to the dura, arachnoid, and pia.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 fervid 通常作为完整词干使用；从历史词根看，可分析为 ferv-（沸腾、热）+ -id（形容词词尾）。直接派生词有 fervidly（热烈地）、fervidness（炽烈），以及较少见的 fervidity（炽烈）；同源词族包括 fervent、fervently、fervency、fervor／fervour。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, fervid normally functions as a whole adjective stem; historically, it contains ferv- (boil, heat) and the adjective ending -id. Direct derivatives include fervidly, fervidness, and the less common fervidity; related words include fervent, fervently, fervency, and fervor/fervour.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: fervent 强调真挚而强烈的信念或愿望；ardent 强调热烈的投入和追求；passionate 强调强烈情感。Fervid 较有文学色彩，有时暗示情感过热或表达过于激烈。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Fervent emphasizes deeply felt conviction or desire; ardent emphasizes eager devotion; passionate emphasizes powerful emotion. Fervid is more literary and can suggest overheated feeling or expression.

etymology_story.zh: 由 flint“燧石”和 lock“枪机、击发装置”合成，因燧石击钢产生火花的工作原理而得名。该词既指这种点火装置，也借指装有这种装置的整支枪。
etymology_story.en: Flintlock combines flint with lock in its firearm sense of a firing mechanism, naming the device after its spark-producing action. The word denotes both the mechanism and a gun equipped with it.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：flint（燧石）+ lock（枪机）→ flintlock，属于复合名词；复数为 flintlocks。没有常用的直接派生动词或副词；flintlock pistol 等结构中的 flintlock 是名词作前置修饰语。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: flint + lock (a firing mechanism) → flintlock, a compound noun; its plural is flintlocks. It has no common directly derived verb or adverb; in expressions such as flintlock pistol, the noun functions attributively.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: firelock 是历史用语，可与 flintlock 重叠，但使用范围因时期而异；musket 指一种长管军用枪，不限定使用燧发枪机；pistol 指手枪，只说明枪型。后两者是相关类别词，并非严格同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Firelock is a historical term that can overlap with flintlock, though its scope varies by period. Musket names a type of long military firearm, while pistol names a handgun; neither specifies flintlock ignition, so these are related categories rather than exact synonyms.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: flint 燧石 + lock 枪机：燧石打出火花，枪机点燃火药。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Flint makes the spark; the lock fires the gun. Together they name the mechanism and the gun.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 ghee 是不可再拆分的借入名词，通常作不可数名词，没有常用的直接派生词。Ghee-based（以印度酥油为基础的）和 ghee-rich（富含印度酥油的）是透明复合形式，并非 ghee 的固有派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, ghee is an unanalyzable loanword, normally used as a mass noun, with no common direct derivatives. Ghee-based and ghee-rich are transparent compounds rather than established members of a derivational family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: clarified butter 是最接近的通用名称；ghee 通常加热得更久，可能带有坚果香。Butter oil 指除去绝大部分水分和非脂乳固体的乳脂，属于较宽泛的技术名称；butter 则仍含水分和乳固体，不与 ghee 完全等同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Clarified butter is the closest general equivalent; ghee is usually cooked longer and may develop a nutty flavor. Butter oil is a broader technical term for milk fat with nearly all water and nonfat solids removed; ordinary butter still contains water and milk solids.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Remove the water and milk solids from butter; picture the golden fat left behind as ghee.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：heli-（helicopter 的截短形式）+ pad（起降平台）→ helipad；复数为 helipads。相关构词族包括 helicopter（直升机）、heliport（直升机场）、helideck（直升机起降甲板）和 helistop（直升机临时起降点）；它们不是 helipad 的直接派生词。

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: landing pad（起降平台）用途更宽，也可供航天器等使用；helideck（直升机起降甲板）通常位于船舶或海上设施；heliport（直升机场）指供直升机使用的机场设施，范围通常比单个 helipad 更大。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Landing pad is broader and can also refer to a platform for spacecraft; helideck usually means a helicopter landing deck on a ship or offshore structure; heliport denotes a helicopter airport, generally encompassing more than an individual helipad.

senses.meaning_zh: 俗套煽情的；做作而老套的
senses.meaning_en: Corny, overly sentimental, or embarrassingly old-fashioned.

etymology_story.zh: hokey 出现于20世纪早期的美式英语，通常分析为 hoke（使显得做作、刻意煽情）加 -y，与指俗套表演或胡扯的 hokum 属于相关词群。这个词群的更早来源并不完全确定，其意义从表演中的做作延伸到一般事物的俗套或不可信。
etymology_story.en: Hokey appeared in early twentieth-century American English and is usually analyzed as hoke, meaning to make something contrived or sentimental, plus -y; it belongs to the same word group as hokum. The group's earlier origins are not entirely certain, and the meaning broadened from theatrical artificiality to general corniness or implausibility.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：hoke 去掉词尾 e + -y → hokey。常见词族及变化形式：hokier（更俗套的）、hokiest（最俗套的）、hokily（做作地）、hokiness（俗套、做作）；相关动词为 hoke，变化形式为 hokes、hoked、hoking，常见于 hoke up（把……弄得夸张做作）；相关名词为 hokum（俗套煽情的内容；胡扯）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: hoke drops its final e before -y → hokey. Family members and inflected forms include hokier, hokiest, hokily, and hokiness. The related verb hoke has the forms hokes, hoked, and hoking and commonly occurs in hoke up; the related noun hokum means corny entertainment or nonsense.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: corny（老套可笑的）强调陈旧套路，有时仍令人喜爱；contrived（刻意安排的）强调不自然、人工设计的痕迹；phony（虚假的）更直接质疑真实性或诚意，而 hokey 也可以只是俗套煽情。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Corny emphasizes tired devices that may still be endearing; contrived emphasizes an unnatural, deliberately manufactured effect; phony more directly challenges authenticity or sincerity, whereas hokey can simply mean embarrassingly sentimental.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: hoke 是刻意加工，-y 表示具有这种特点：加工得太过，就显得 hokey。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Hoke something up too much, and it becomes hokey: visibly manufactured emotion or effect.

senses.collocation_zh: 一个忘恩负义的家伙；一个自私而不知感恩的人
senses.sentence_en: After everything she had done for him, he behaved like an ingrate.
senses.sentence_zh: 她为他付出了那么多，他却表现得像个忘恩负义的人。

etymology_story.zh: ingrate 可追溯到法语 ingrat 和拉丁语 ingratus，后者由 in-（不）与 gratus（令人感激的；心怀感激的）组成。英语历史上也用它作形容词表示“不知感恩的”，现代常用法则是带贬义的名词，指忘恩负义的人。
etymology_story.en: Ingrate traces to French ingrat and Latin ingratus, formed from in-, meaning 'not', and gratus, meaning 'pleasing' or 'grateful'. English historically also used it as an adjective meaning 'ungrateful', but its usual modern use is a disapproving noun for an ungrateful person.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语通常把 ingrate 作为完整词使用，并非 in- + 独立英语词 grate 的组合；历史结构为 in-（不）+ grat-（感激、令人愉悦），词尾 e 属于既有拼写。复数为 ingrates；同源词族包括 ingratitude（忘恩负义）、gratitude（感激）、grateful（感激的）、gratefully（感激地）、gratefulness（感激之情）、ungrateful（不知感恩的）、ungratefully（不知感恩地）和 ungratefulness（不知感恩）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English generally treats ingrate as a whole word, not as in- plus the independent English word grate. Its historical structure is in- ('not') + grat- ('grateful' or 'pleasing'), with final e belonging to the established spelling. The plural is ingrates; the related family includes ingratitude, gratitude, grateful, gratefully, gratefulness, ungrateful, ungratefully, and ungratefulness.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: ungrateful person（不知感恩的人）是中性、直接的描述；thankless person（不领情的人）突出对帮助或好意毫无谢意。ingrate 把这种行为概括为对人的贬斥性称呼，语气通常更强。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Ungrateful person is a neutral, direct description; thankless person emphasizes a failure to appreciate help or kindness. Ingrate turns that judgment into a disapproving label for the person and usually sounds stronger.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: in- 是否定，grat- 关联 gratitude：得到恩惠却没有感激，就是 ingrate。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect in- with 'not' and grat- with gratitude: an ingrate receives kindness without gratitude.

pronunciation.note: 采用英语常用读法；重音符号 ˈ 标在主重读音节前。

forms: 抽象名词，通常不可数。
family: irredentist 领土收复主义者；irredentists 其复数

morphology.text: irredent-（尚未收回的领土） + -ism（主义） → irredentism（领土收复主义）。

etymology.text: 这一政治词属于意大利语 irredento（尚未赎回、收回的）及 irredentist 的词族；英语用 -ism 形成表示主张的名词，后来扩展到其他国家的类似领土诉求。

usage_note: 政治学用语，指以历史或族群联系为依据主张收回他国所辖领土；不泛指一切爱国情感。

senses.meaning_zh: 领土收复主义；以历史归属或民族联系为由主张并入他国领土的政治主张
senses.meaning_en: A policy or movement seeking to incorporate territory held by another state on historical or ethnic grounds.
senses.english_definition: Irredentism is the belief or policy that a country should take control of territory outside its borders because of claimed historical ownership or ethnic ties.
senses.collocation_zh: 领土收复主义；民族主义式的领土收复主张
senses.sentence_en: The movement's irredentism centered on a neighboring region inhabited by people of the same ethnic group.
senses.sentence_zh: 该运动的领土收复主张主要针对邻国一个由同一族群居民聚居的地区。

etymology_story.zh: 这个词源于19世纪意大利统一运动中的 Italia irredenta，字面义为“尚未赎回的意大利”，指民族主义者主张并入意大利、当时主要受奥地利统治的地区。英语沿用相关词族并以 -ism 表示主义，后来将其用于其他国家类似的历史或民族领土诉求。
etymology_story.en: The word arose from nineteenth-century Italian nationalism and the expression Italia irredenta, literally 'unredeemed Italy', for territories nationalists sought to unite with Italy, chiefly under Austrian rule at the time. English adopted the related vocabulary with -ism and later extended it to comparable historical or ethnic territorial claims elsewhere.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代词族分析：irredent-（与 irredentist 共用的借入词干）+ -ism（主义）→ irredentism；irredent- 不是现代英语中可独立使用的词。核心词族包括 irredentist（领土收复主义者；领土收复主义的）和 irredentist 的复数 irredentists。更早的意大利语 irredento 含否定成分与表示“赎回”的词干，不能按英语 dent（牙齿、凹痕）拆解。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern family analysis: irredent- (the borrowed stem shared with irredentist) + -ism ('doctrine or movement') → irredentism; irredent- is not an independent modern English word. The core family includes irredentist, used as both a noun and an adjective, and the noun plural irredentists. Earlier Italian irredento combines negation with a stem meaning 'redeemed'; it should not be analyzed using English dent.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 以下是相关概念，并非严格同义词：revanchism（复仇主义、失地收复主义）强调逆转战败或领土损失；expansionism（扩张主义）泛指扩大国家领土或影响力；nationalism（民族主义）强调民族认同与利益，本身不必包含对他国领土的要求。irredentism 特指以历史归属或民族联系为依据的境外领土并入主张。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: These are related concepts rather than exact synonyms: revanchism emphasizes reversing defeat or territorial loss; expansionism broadly seeks greater territory or influence; nationalism emphasizes national identity and interests without necessarily claiming foreign territory. Irredentism specifically seeks incorporation of territory outside existing borders on historical or ethnic grounds.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“尚未赎回的土地”记起：把境外土地视为尚待收回的家园，就是 irredentism 的核心逻辑。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember 'unredeemed land': irredentism treats territory beyond the border as a homeland still to be recovered.

meaning: 峰度（反映分布尾部特征的统计量）
aliases: 峰度（反映分布尾部特征的统计量）

pronunciation.note: 采用英语常用读法；重音符号 ˈ 标在主重读音节前。

forms: 统计量名词，通常不可数。
family: kurtotic 峰度的；leptokurtic 高峰度的；platykurtic 低峰度的

morphology.text: kurt-（弯曲、隆起） + -osis（状态） → kurtosis（峰度，历史造词结构）。

etymology.text: 统计学借用了希腊语 kurtosis（隆起、凸起）来命名此量；名称像在谈峰形，实际理解还要关注分布尾部。

usage_note: 常规总体峰度是标准化四阶矩；excess kurtosis 要再减3。不能只凭峰顶尖不尖来理解，也不要与衡量不对称性的偏度混淆。

senses.meaning_zh: 峰度：标准化四阶矩，用于描述分布尾部极端值的倾向；也常指减去3后的超额峰度
senses.meaning_en: The standardized fourth moment of a distribution, reflecting its propensity for extreme values; also commonly reported as excess kurtosis.
senses.english_definition: Kurtosis is a statistical measure that uses fourth powers of standardized deviations to describe how strongly extreme values feature in a distribution; excess kurtosis subtracts three from this measure.
senses.collocation_zh: 超额峰度；高峰度
senses.sentence_en: A normal distribution has a kurtosis of three and an excess kurtosis of zero.
senses.sentence_zh: 正态分布的峰度为3，超额峰度为0。

etymology_story.zh: kurtosis 来自表示“隆起、凸起”的希腊语词，统计学家卡尔·皮尔逊在20世纪初将其用于分布形态的研究。名称容易让人只想到峰的尖平，但这个统计量对尾部极端值十分敏感，不能简单理解为峰高。
etymology_story.en: Kurtosis comes from a Greek word meaning 'bulging' or 'convexity' and was introduced into statistical work by Karl Pearson in the early twentieth century. Although the name suggests the shape of a peak, the statistic is highly sensitive to extreme tail values and should not simply be interpreted as peak height.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语把 kurtosis 作为完整的统计学术语使用；历史构词可分析为 kurt-（弯曲、凸起）+ -osis（状态或过程），并非日常英语中的自由构词。复数为 kurtoses；相关形容词有 kurtotic（峰度的）、leptokurtic（峰度高于正态分布的）、mesokurtic（峰度等于正态分布的）和 platykurtic（峰度低于正态分布的）；对应名词有 leptokurtosis、mesokurtosis 和 platykurtosis，另有术语 excess kurtosis（超额峰度）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English treats kurtosis as an established statistical term; its historical formation can be analyzed as kurt- ('curved or bulging') + -osis ('state or process'), rather than as a freely productive everyday construction. The plural is kurtoses. Related adjectives include kurtotic, leptokurtic (having higher kurtosis than a normal distribution), mesokurtic (having the same kurtosis), and platykurtic (having lower kurtosis); corresponding nouns include leptokurtosis, mesokurtosis, and platykurtosis. Excess kurtosis is a related technical expression.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: fourth standardized moment（标准化四阶矩）是通常定义下的精确数学名称；excess kurtosis（超额峰度）等于峰度减3，数值不能直接混用；tail heaviness（尾部厚重程度）是相关的定性概念，并非峰度的严格同义词，峰度也不等同于峰的尖峭程度。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Fourth standardized moment is the precise mathematical name under the usual definition; excess kurtosis equals kurtosis minus three, so their numerical values are not interchangeable; tail heaviness is a related qualitative concept rather than an exact synonym, and kurtosis is not simply peak sharpness.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 名字想到“隆起”，计算记住“四次方”：离中心很远的值被大幅放大，因此读峰度要关注尾部极端值。
mnemonic_anchor.en: The name suggests a bulge, but the calculation uses fourth powers: far-out values receive enormous weight, so think about the tails.

meaning: 浸软；用液体浸泡使软化
aliases: 浸软；用液体浸泡使软化

forms: 第三人称单数 macerates；过去式、过去分词 macerated；现在分词 macerating。
family: maceration 浸软；macerator 浸软机、粉碎机。

morphology.text: macerate + -ion → maceration（浸软过程，词尾 e 脱落）；macerate 作为独立词素记忆。

usage_note: 烹饪和技术语境中使用。macerate something in liquid 表示把某物浸在液体中使其软化。

senses.meaning_en: to soften skin or tissue through prolonged exposure to moisture
senses.english_definition: When moisture macerates skin or other tissue, it makes it unusually soft after remaining in contact with it for a long time.
senses.collocation_zh: 浸渍发软的皮肤；浸软的组织

etymology_story.zh: 该词于16世纪末进入英语，源自拉丁语 macerare，意为“浸泡、使软化”。其核心含义延续至今，既用于食物的浸渍，也用于描述组织因水分而软化。
etymology_story.en: The word entered English in the late sixteenth century from Latin macerare, meaning “to soak or soften.” This central meaning survives in both food preparation and descriptions of tissue softened by moisture.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中可将 macerate 作为整体动词词基，不宜强拆成独立词根和后缀。屈折形式：macerates、macerated、macerating；主要派生词：maceration（浸渍、浸软，去掉词尾 e 后加 -ion）、macerator（浸软器、粉碎处理机，去掉词尾 e 后加 -or）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, macerate is best treated as a whole verb base rather than divided into independent productive elements. Inflections: macerates, macerated, macerating. Principal derivatives: maceration, the process of soaking or softening, formed by dropping final e and adding -ion; macerator, a softening or waste-processing device, formed by dropping final e and adding -or.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: soak（浸泡）强调置于液体中，不一定变软；steep（浸泡、浸提）常强调萃取味道或成分；soften（使软化）只说明结果。macerate 同时突出液体浸泡及由此产生的软化。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Soak emphasizes immersion without necessarily implying softening; steep often emphasizes extracting flavor or other substances; soften describes the result without specifying a method. Macerate specifically connects soaking with softening.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“浸泡→变软”：果干泡软、皮肤泡皱，都连到同一个核心过程。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor it to “soak → soften”: softened dried fruit and moisture-softened skin share the same process.

etymology_story.zh: 英语于19世纪借入意大利语 minestrone，它由 minestra（汤）加增大后缀 -one 构成，表示一大份或丰盛的汤。minestra 更早与意为“端上、供应”的动词相连，最终可追溯至拉丁语 ministrare（服侍、供应）。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed minestrone from Italian in the nineteenth century; it combines minestra, “soup,” with the augmentative suffix -one, suggesting a large or substantial soup. Minestra is historically connected with serving food and ultimately with Latin ministrare, “to serve or supply.”

morphology_enriched.zh: 英语中是整体借入的名词，没有可自由拆用的英语词缀；其意大利语内部结构为 minestra（汤，去掉末尾 -a）+ -one（增大后缀）。通常用作不可数名词，无常用英语派生词；minestras 或 minestrones 不应机械套作常规词族，后者仅可在指不同种类或份数时作复数。
morphology_enriched.en: In English, this is a whole borrowed noun without productive English affixes. Its Italian structure is minestra, “soup,” with final -a replaced by the augmentative suffix -one. It is normally uncountable and has no common English derivatives; minestrones is possible when referring to varieties or individual servings.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: vegetable soup（蔬菜汤）是范围更广的上位表达；vegetable broth（蔬菜清汤）通常更清淡，强调汤液。两者都不能完整表达 minestrone 特有的意大利风格及丰富配料。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Vegetable soup is a broader category; vegetable broth usually suggests a lighter liquid preparation. Neither fully captures the Italian identity and substantial mixture of ingredients associated with minestrone.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 意大利语“汤”加“增大”后缀：记成一大碗配料丰富的意大利蔬菜汤。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Italian “soup” plus an augmentative ending: picture a big bowl of Italian soup packed with vegetables.

family: neurotoxicity 神经毒性；neurotoxin 神经毒素。

morphology.text: neuro-（神经）+ toxic（有毒的）→ neurotoxic（有神经毒性的）。

etymology.text: 近现代英语科学用语，以源自希腊语 neuron（神经、筋腱）的 neuro- 和 toxic 组合。词首提示毒性所针对的是神经。

usage_note: 常修饰 substance、effect、chemical 等；描述毒性作用的部位，不表示所有器官都同样受损。

senses.meaning_zh: 有神经毒性的；能损害神经系统的
senses.meaning_en: poisonous or harmful to the nervous system
senses.english_definition: A substance or effect that is neurotoxic can damage the nervous system.
senses.collocation_zh: 神经毒性作用；具有神经毒性的物质
senses.sentence_en: The researchers tested the compound for neurotoxic effects.
senses.sentence_zh: 研究人员检测了这种化合物是否具有神经毒性作用。

etymology_story.zh: 这是现代科学英语中由 neuro-（神经）与 toxic（有毒的）构成的词。neuro- 源自希腊语 neuron（筋腱、神经），而 toxic 最终与希腊语中表示“箭毒”的词有关。
etymology_story.en: This modern scientific formation combines neuro-, “nerve,” with toxic. Neuro- comes from Greek neuron, “sinew or nerve,” while toxic ultimately derives from a Greek expression for poison used on arrows.

morphology_enriched.zh: neuro-（神经）+ toxic（有毒的）→ neurotoxic（有神经毒性的）。主要派生词为 neurotoxicity（神经毒性）；相关词族包括 neurotoxin（神经毒素）、neurotoxicant（神经毒性物质）、neurotoxicology（神经毒理学）、neurotoxicological（神经毒理学的）和 neurotoxicologist（神经毒理学家）。
morphology_enriched.en: Neuro- (“nerve”) + toxic (“poisonous”) → neurotoxic. The principal derivative is neurotoxicity. Related family members include neurotoxin, a toxin affecting the nervous system; neurotoxicant, a substance toxic to the nervous system; neurotoxicology, the study of such effects; neurotoxicological; and neurotoxicologist.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: toxic（有毒的）泛指毒性，不限定作用部位；nerve-damaging（损害神经的）是较通俗的近义表达，也可能涵盖非毒性机制。neurotoxic 明确指向神经系统的毒性损伤或功能障碍。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Toxic describes poisonous effects without identifying the target; nerve-damaging is a plainer near-equivalent that can also include damage caused by non-toxic mechanisms. Neurotoxic specifically identifies toxic injury or dysfunction affecting the nervous system.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: neuro- 指目标“神经”，toxic 指作用“有毒”：毒性瞄准神经系统。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Neuro- identifies the target, nerves; toxic identifies the effect, poisoning: toxicity aimed at the nervous system.

pronunciation.note: 主重音见 ˈ，次重音见 ˌ；按本卡音标连读各音节。

forms: 可数名词；复数 organophosphates。
family: phosphate 磷酸盐、磷酸酯；organophosphatic 有机磷酸酯的。

morphology.text: organo-（有机的）+ phosphate（磷酸酯）→ organophosphate（有机磷酸酯）。

etymology.text: 现代英语化学命名把 organo- 与 phosphate 组合起来，表示磷酸的有机酯类。organo- 的远源是希腊语 organon（器官、工具）。

usage_note: 化学类别名；部分成员用于杀虫剂，也可出现在阻燃材料中。不可把整个类别等同于单一商品。

senses.meaning_zh: 有机磷酸酯；尤指用作杀虫剂的此类或相关有机磷化合物
senses.meaning_en: an organic ester of phosphoric acid, or a related compound, especially one used as an insecticide
senses.english_definition: An organophosphate is an organic phosphate compound, especially one belonging to a group widely used as insecticides.
senses.collocation_zh: 有机磷中毒；接触有机磷化合物

senses.meaning_en: belonging to or involving the organophosphate class of compounds
senses.english_definition: An organophosphate pesticide or other substance belongs to the organophosphate class of chemicals.
senses.collocation_zh: 有机磷农药；有机磷杀虫剂
senses.sentence_en: The study measured residues of organophosphate pesticides on vegetables.
senses.sentence_zh: 这项研究测定了蔬菜上的有机磷农药残留量。

etymology_story.zh: 该词形成于现代化学英语，由表示“有机的”的 organo- 与 phosphate（磷酸盐或磷酸酯）组合而成。随着相关杀虫剂的广泛使用，它在农业和毒理学中也常用于指称包括相关含硫化合物在内的有机磷农药类别。
etymology_story.en: The word was formed in modern chemical English from organo-, meaning “organic,” and phosphate. With the widespread use of related insecticides, agricultural and toxicological usage also came to cover an organophosphate pesticide class that includes related sulfur-containing compounds.

morphology_enriched.zh: organo-（有机的）+ phosphate（磷酸盐、磷酸酯）→ organophosphate；复数为 organophosphates，也可作形容词置于名词前。相关术语包括 phosphate（磷酸盐、磷酸酯）和 organophosphorus（有机磷的）；后者涵盖范围更广，并非直接派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Organo- (“organic”) + phosphate → organophosphate; the plural is organophosphates, and the same form also functions adjectivally before nouns. Related terms include phosphate and organophosphorus; the latter describes a broader chemical category and is not a direct derivative.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: organic phosphate（有机磷酸酯）在严格化学语境中最接近；phosphate ester（磷酸酯）强调酯的结构；organophosphorus compound（有机磷化合物）范围更广。这些表达与农药语境下的 organophosphate 并非始终完全等同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Organic phosphate is the closest equivalent in strict chemical usage; phosphate ester emphasizes ester structure; organophosphorus compound is broader. These expressions are not always interchangeable with organophosphate as used for a pesticide class.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: organo- 锁定“有机”，phosphate 锁定“磷酸酯”；农业语境再联想到有机磷杀虫剂。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Organo- signals “organic,” and phosphate signals the phosphate chemistry; in agricultural contexts, connect the combination with organophosphate insecticides.

pronunciation.note: 主重音见 ˈ，次重音见 ˌ；按本卡音标连读各音节。

forms: 可数名词；复数 porkers。
family: pork 猪肉；porky 肥胖的。

morphology.text: pork（猪肉）+ -er（与某用途有关的动物或事物）→ porker（供食用的育肥猪）。

etymology.text: 17世纪英语在 pork 后构成 porker，用来称供食用而养肥的小猪。pork 经古法语 porc 来自拉丁语 porcus（猪）。

usage_note: 畜牧语境用词；也有拿来辱骂胖人的用法，对人使用很不礼貌。本卡学习猪的意思。

senses.meaning_zh: 供食用的育肥猪，尤指较年轻的猪

senses.english_definition: A porker is a pig that is being fattened or has been fattened for its meat.

senses.meaning_en: an insulting informal term for a fat person
senses.english_definition: If someone calls a person a porker, they are rudely referring to that person's weight.

etymology_story.zh: 该词在17世纪由 pork（猪肉）加 -er 构成，最初指供食用而育肥的猪；pork 经古法语 porc 源自拉丁语 porcus（猪）。后来，人们将肥猪的形象转用于人，产生了带侮辱性的“胖子”义。
etymology_story.en: The word was formed in the seventeenth century by adding -er to pork, originally naming a pig fattened for meat; pork comes through Old French porc from Latin porcus, “pig.” The image of a fat pig was later applied insultingly to a person's weight.

morphology_enriched.zh: pork（猪肉）+ -er（此处构成与某用途相关的动物名称）→ porker；复数为 porkers。相关词族有 pork（猪肉）、porky（像猪的；非正式语体中指肥胖的）和 porkiness（肥胖、像猪的状态）；porky 与 porkiness 属于以 pork 为基础的旁支，并非 porker 的直接派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Pork (“pig meat”) + -er, here forming an animal name associated with a particular use, → porker; plural porkers. Related family members are pork, porky, meaning piglike or informally fat, and porkiness. Porky and porkiness belong to a related branch based on pork rather than deriving directly from porker.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: fattening pig（育肥猪）是农业义的中性近义表达；hog（猪）在美式英语中较常见，但不总突出育肥用途；fatso（胖子）仅对应指人的侮辱义。porker 的语义和语气取决于它指猪还是指人。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Fattening pig is a neutral equivalent for the agricultural sense; hog is common in American English but does not always emphasize fattening for meat; fatso corresponds only to the insulting human sense. The meaning and tone of porker depend on whether it refers to an animal or a person.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从 pork“猪肉”想到“养来产肉的猪”；把这个形象套在人身上，就成了侮辱性称呼。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with pork: a porker is a pig raised for meat. Transferring that image to a person produces the insulting sense.

meaning: 产生有利或不利的影响；归于
aliases: 产生有利或不利的影响；归于

pronunciation.note: 主重音见 ˈ，次重音见 ˌ；按本卡音标连读各音节。

forms: 第三人称单数 redounds；过去式、过去分词 redounded；现在分词 redounding。
family: redound to someone’s credit 为某人增光；redundant 冗余的，与它有历史词根联系。

morphology.text: 历史词根 re-（回、再）+ undare（涌动）→ 拉丁语 redundare（涌出）；英语 redound 整体记忆，常接 to。

etymology.text: 拉丁语 redundare（涌出）经古法语 redonder 进入中古英语；后来把结果像水流一样回到某人身上，用于荣誉或损害等影响。

usage_note: 正式、不及物。常用 redound to someone’s credit 或 redound to someone’s disadvantage，后面接结果归属。

sentence: These improvements will redound to the benefit of local residents.
translation: 这些改善最终会使当地居民受益。

senses.meaning_zh: 产生某种结果；使某人获得荣誉、利益或遭受损害
senses.meaning_en: to produce a result that benefits or harms someone
senses.english_definition: If something redounds to someone's credit, advantage, or disadvantage, it produces a result that brings them praise, benefit, or harm.
senses.collocation_en: redound to someone's credit; redound to someone's advantage
senses.collocation_zh: 使某人赢得赞誉；对某人有利
senses.sentence_en: Her willingness to acknowledge the mistake redounded to her credit.
senses.sentence_zh: 她愿意承认错误，反而为自己赢得了赞誉。

etymology_story.zh: 经古法语 redonder 源自拉丁语 redundare，原义为“满溢、涌回”，其中 re- 表示“向后”，undare 表示“涌动”，与 unda“波浪”有关。水流涌回的意象后来发展为结果或影响归到某人身上。
etymology_story.en: The word came through Old French redonder from Latin redundare, meaning 'to overflow or surge back,' from re- 'back' and undare 'to surge,' related to unda 'wave.' The image of flowing back developed into the idea of consequences returning to someone.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常把 redound 视为不可再作能产拆分的动词；历史构成为 re-（回）+ 与拉丁语 undare（涌动）有关的词干。屈折形式：redounds、redounded、redounding；redundant（多余的）和 redundancy（冗余）是同源词，并非由现代 redound 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, redound is normally treated as a verb without a productive internal breakdown; historically, it contains re- 'back' and a stem related to Latin undare 'to surge.' Inflected forms are redounds, redounded, and redounding; redundant and redundancy are etymological relatives, not direct modern derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: contribute to（促成）强调对结果有所助益，语域较中性；accrue to（归于、逐渐获得）强调利益等累积到某人名下；rebound on（反过来损害）通常强调不良后果。redound 较正式，突出结果最终归到某人身上，常与 credit、advantage 或 disadvantage 连用。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Contribute to neutrally emphasizes helping to produce a result; accrue to emphasizes benefits accumulating or coming to someone; rebound on usually emphasizes harmful consequences returning to their source. Redound is formal and highlights the resulting credit, advantage, or disadvantage for someone.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 想象“结果像波浪涌回来”：好结果带来荣誉，坏结果带来损害。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture consequences flowing back like waves: favorable ones bring credit, unfavorable ones bring harm.

pronunciation.note: 主重音见 ˈ，次重音见 ˌ；按本卡音标连读各音节。

etymology_story.en: Roundworm combines round and worm, describing the animal's circular cross section in contrast with a flatworm's flattened body. Worm continues Old English wyrm, which could refer broadly to worms, snakes, and other creeping creatures.

morphology_enriched.zh: round（圆的）+ worm（蠕虫）→ roundworm（线虫），属于名词复合词；复数为 roundworms。该词没有常用的直接派生动词或形容词，常以名词修饰语用于 roundworm infection 等结构。
morphology_enriched.en: Round 'circular' + worm forms the compound noun roundworm; its plural is roundworms. It has no common directly derived verb or adjective and often functions as a noun modifier in expressions such as roundworm infection.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: nematode（线虫）是更精确的生物学名称；ascarid（蛔虫类线虫）仅指其中一类寄生线虫；eelworm（鳗形线虫）常用于某些细小线虫，尤其植物相关线虫。roundworm 是普通名称，不能一律缩窄为“蛔虫”。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Nematode is the more precise biological term; ascarid denotes a particular group of parasitic roundworms; eelworm commonly refers to certain small nematodes, especially those associated with plants. Roundworm is the general everyday name and does not refer exclusively to intestinal ascarids.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: round 指横截面圆，不是身体盘成圆圈：圆截面的虫＝线虫。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Round describes the cross section, not a curled-up posture: a round-bodied worm is a roundworm.

etymology_story.zh: 该词出现于19世纪初的美国英语，由 spit 与名词性词尾 -oon 构成，用来指接唾液的容器。它与嚼烟等历史生活习惯密切相关，此类容器也曾称为 spitting boxes。
etymology_story.en: The word appeared in early nineteenth-century American English, formed from spit with the noun-forming ending -oon to name a receptacle for saliva. Such containers, also called spitting boxes, were closely associated with practices such as chewing tobacco.

morphology_enriched.zh: spit（吐唾液）+ -oon（本词中的名词性词尾）→ spittoon，拼写中有双写 t；-oon 不是现代英语中可自由套用的常见容器后缀。直接词形：spittoons；相关基础词族：spit、spits、spitting、spat，以及美式英语中也使用的过去式和过去分词 spit；spitter 指吐唾液的人。
morphology_enriched.en: Spit + the noun-forming ending -oon gives spittoon, spelled with double t; -oon is not a freely productive modern suffix for containers. The direct plural is spittoons; the related base-word family includes spit, spits, spitting, spat, and the alternative American past and participial form spit, plus spitter for someone who spits.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: cuspidor（痰盂）与 spittoon 基本同义，尤其见于美式英语，现较少用；spitting bowl（吐唾液用的碗）是描述性名称，通常突出碗状外形。spittoon 可指不同形状和材质的专用容器。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Cuspidor is a close synonym, especially in American English, though now uncommon; spitting bowl is a descriptive expression that usually suggests a bowl-shaped vessel. Spittoon can refer to purpose-made receptacles of various shapes and materials.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住 spit“吐”：专门接住吐出来的唾液的容器，就是 spittoon。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with spit: a spittoon is the container that catches it.

senses.english_definition: A stereotactic procedure uses a three-dimensional coordinate system to locate and reach or treat a precise target inside the body.

senses.sentence_en: The team used a stereotactic technique to guide the biopsy needle.
senses.sentence_zh: 团队采用立体定向技术引导活检针。

etymology_story.zh: 该词属于由希腊语 stereos“立体的、坚实的”和 taxis“排列、定位”构成的医学词族，与 stereotaxis 和 stereotaxic 密切相关。它以三维空间中的排列定位为核心，发展为医学中的精确靶点定位用语。
etymology_story.en: The word belongs to a medical family built from Greek stereos 'solid, three-dimensional' and taxis 'arrangement or positioning,' closely related to stereotaxis and stereotaxic. Its central idea of positioning in three-dimensional space became a term for precise medical targeting.

morphology_enriched.zh: stereo-（三维的）+ -tactic（与排列、定位有关的）→ stereotactic；也可按词干 stereotact- + 形容词后缀 -ic 理解，此处 tactic 不表示日常所说的“战术”。核心词族：stereotactically（以立体定向方式）；相关名词 stereotaxis、stereotaxy（立体定向技术）；同义形容词 stereotaxic 及其副词 stereotaxically。
morphology_enriched.en: Stereo- 'three-dimensional' + -tactic 'relating to arrangement or positioning' forms stereotactic; alternatively, analyze it as stereotact- + adjectival -ic. Tactic here does not carry its everyday military meaning. The core family includes stereotactically, the related nouns stereotaxis and stereotaxy, and the synonymous adjective stereotaxic with its adverb stereotaxically.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: stereotaxic（立体定向的）通常与 stereotactic 同义；image-guided（影像引导的）范围更广，并不一定采用立体坐标定位；targeted（靶向的）仅强调针对特定目标，不说明定位方法。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Stereotaxic is generally synonymous with stereotactic; image-guided is broader and does not necessarily imply stereotactic coordinate localization; targeted merely indicates a specific intended target without specifying how it is located.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: stereo- 想成立体空间，-tactic 想成排列定位：在三维坐标中精准找点。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think stereo for three-dimensional space and -tactic for positioning: locate one precise point in three dimensions.

etymology_story.zh: 医学英语将拉丁语来源的 sub-“在……下面”与 arachnoid“蛛网膜”组合成此词。arachnoid 最终来自表示“蜘蛛”和“形似”的希腊语成分，名称源于该膜及其相关细丝结构的蛛网状外观。
etymology_story.en: Medical English formed the word by combining Latin-derived sub- 'beneath' with arachnoid, the name of a meningeal membrane. Arachnoid ultimately contains Greek elements meaning 'spider' and 'resembling,' referring to the web-like appearance of the membrane and its associated fine strands.

morphology_enriched.zh: sub-（在……下）+ arachnoid（蛛网膜的；蛛网膜）→ subarachnoid；arachnoid 可进一步历史分析为 arachn-（蜘蛛）+ -oid（似……的）。相关词族：arachnoidal（蛛网膜的）、arachnoiditis（蛛网膜炎）；subarachnoidal 是较少见的同义形容词。
morphology_enriched.en: Sub- 'beneath' + arachnoid forms subarachnoid; arachnoid can be further analyzed historically as arachn- 'spider' + -oid 'resembling.' Related family members include arachnoidal 'relating to the arachnoid' and arachnoiditis 'inflammation of the arachnoid'; subarachnoidal is a less common synonymous adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: subarachnoidal（蛛网膜下的）是较少见的同义形式；intrathecal（鞘内的）强调位于鞘内，在脊柱给药等语境中通常涉及蛛网膜下腔，但不能在所有解剖语境中与 subarachnoid 自由互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Subarachnoidal is a less common synonymous form; intrathecal emphasizes location within a sheath and, in contexts such as spinal drug administration, usually involves the subarachnoid space, but it is not freely interchangeable with subarachnoid in every anatomical context.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: sub-＝下面，arachnoid＝蛛网膜：蛛网膜下面，就是 subarachnoid。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Sub- means beneath and arachnoid names the membrane: subarachnoid means beneath the arachnoid.

etymology_story.zh: 英语 toque 借自法语 toque，通常追溯至西班牙语 toca（头饰），更早的来源尚不确定。它原指一种帽子，后来用于厨师帽；加拿大英语中的毛线帽义与法语 tuque 有关，通常读作 /tuːk/。
etymology_story.en: English toque was borrowed from French toque, generally traced to Spanish toca, meaning a head covering, with an uncertain earlier origin. The hat name later acquired its chef's-hat sense; the Canadian knitted-hat sense is associated with French tuque and is usually pronounced /tuːk/.

morphology_enriched.en: Toque is a borrowed base without a regular internal English morphological breakdown; its plural is toques. The Canadian knitted-hat sense also has the spellings tuque and touque; toque blanche is a French phrase meaning 'white hat,' and blanche is not an English suffix.

etymology_story.en: Tryptophan entered English through German Tryptophan, combining an element associated with trypsin and a Greek stem meaning 'appear' or 'show.' The name reflects its early detection in products of protein digestion by trypsin.

morphology_enriched.zh: 科学构词可分析为 trypto-（与胰蛋白酶有关）+ -phan（历史上表示“显现”）；这些不是可自由套用的普通英语词缀。相关构词有 tryptophanyl（色氨酰基的）、tryptophanase（色氨酸酶，tryptophan + -ase），以及立体异构体名称 L-tryptophan 和 D-tryptophan。
morphology_enriched.en: The scientific formation can be analyzed as trypto- (associated with trypsin) + -phan (historically referring to appearing or showing); these are not freely productive everyday English affixes. Related formations include tryptophanyl, tryptophanase (tryptophan + -ase), and the stereoisomer names L-tryptophan and D-tryptophan.

synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no common exact synonym: L-tryptophan specifies the stereoisomer used in human protein synthesis; Trp and W are amino-acid codes rather than ordinary lexical synonyms; amino acid is a broader category term.

etymology_story.zh: cardiorespiratory 是由医学组合成分 cardio- 和 respiratory 构成的现代术语。前者源于希腊语 kardia（心脏），后者属于源自拉丁语 respirare（呼吸）的词族，合起来表示心脏与呼吸系统的共同作用。
etymology_story.en: Cardiorespiratory is a modern medical formation combining cardio- with respiratory. The first element comes from Greek kardia, meaning 'heart,' while the second belongs to the family derived from Latin respirare, meaning 'breathe,' bringing the two systems together.

morphology_enriched.zh: cardio-（心脏）+ respiratory（呼吸的）→ cardiorespiratory。相关词族包括 cardiac（心脏的）、cardiology（心脏病学）、cardiovascular（心血管的），以及 respire（呼吸）、respiration（呼吸作用）、respiratory（呼吸的）、respirator（呼吸器）；这些是构词成分的相关词，并非都由整个 cardiorespiratory 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Cardio- (heart) + respiratory (relating to breathing) forms cardiorespiratory. Related component families include cardiac, cardiology, and cardiovascular, together with respire, respiration, respiratory, and respirator; these are relatives of the components, not all derivatives of the complete word cardiorespiratory.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: cardiopulmonary（心肺的）最接近，直接指心脏和肺；cardiovascular（心血管的）涉及心脏与血管，并不明确包含呼吸系统；respiratory（呼吸的）只涉及呼吸系统，不包含心脏。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Cardiopulmonary is the closest equivalent and directly concerns the heart and lungs; cardiovascular concerns the heart and blood vessels without explicitly including breathing; respiratory concerns the breathing system alone.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: cardio- 心脏 + respiratory 呼吸：心跳与呼吸一起工作。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Cardio- is heart and respiratory is breathing: heartbeat and breath working together.

etymology_story.zh: 由 colic 加形容词后缀 -y 构成；colic 经法语和拉丁语追溯至希腊语 kōlikos，意为“结肠的”。这个原本与结肠有关的名称，后来用于腹部阵发性绞痛，也用于婴儿反复长时间哭闹的相关症状。
etymology_story.en: Colicky was formed from colic and the adjective suffix -y; colic came through French and Latin from Greek kōlikos, meaning 'of the colon.' The original association with the colon broadened to spasmodic abdominal pain and the associated syndrome of prolonged crying in infants.

morphology_enriched.zh: colic（腹绞痛）+ -y（有……特点的）→ colicky；在 -y 前加 k，以保持 c 的 /k/ 音。核心词族：colic（腹绞痛）、colicky（腹绞痛的）；colickiness（腹绞痛的状态）是少用的规则派生名词。
morphology_enriched.en: colic + -y → colicky; k is inserted before -y to preserve the /k/ sound of c. The core family consists of colic and colicky; colickiness is an uncommon, regularly formed noun denoting the condition.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: crampy（痉挛性疼痛的）强调肌肉收缩引起的疼痛；spasmodic（痉挛性的、阵发性的）强调突然反复发作；griping（腹部绞痛的）常描述肠道扭绞般的痛感。colicky 更明确地指向腹绞痛及婴儿肠绞痛症状。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Crampy emphasizes pain from muscular contraction; spasmodic emphasizes sudden, recurring contractions; griping describes a twisting abdominal pain. Colicky refers more specifically to colic, including the characteristic symptoms in infants.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: colic 是腹绞痛，-y 表示“有这种特点的”：colicky 就是“有腹绞痛症状的”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Colic names the condition; -y means 'having its characteristics': colicky means showing the symptoms of colic.

usage_note: 通常与 suspension、preservation、storage 连用。该词说明人体低温保存领域，不保证未来能够复苏。

senses.meaning_zh: 人体低温保存的；与人体低温保存技术有关的
senses.meaning_en: Relating to preserving people at extremely low temperatures in the hope of future revival.
senses.english_definition: Cryonic methods preserve a person's body or brain at extremely low temperatures after legal death, in the hope that future technology may make revival possible.
senses.collocation_zh: 人体低温保存；人体低温保存状态
senses.sentence_en: He arranged for cryonic preservation in the hope that future medicine might make revival possible.
senses.sentence_zh: 他安排了人体低温保存，希望未来的医学能够使复苏成为可能。

etymology_story.zh: cryonic 属于20世纪形成的人体低温保存术语词族，其 cryo- 源于希腊语 kryos，意为“严寒、冰冷”。它与 cryonics 密切相关，专指为可能的未来复苏而进行的低温保存。
etymology_story.en: Cryonic belongs to the twentieth-century vocabulary of cryonics, with cryo- deriving from Greek kryos, meaning 'icy cold' or 'frost.' Its specialized meaning concerns preservation at extremely low temperatures for possible future revival.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词关系为 cryonics（人体低温保存技术）↔ cryonic（相关的形容词），形式上可理解为 -ics 与 -ic 的对应；cryo- 表示“低温”，不宜把 n 单独解释成有固定意义的词缀。核心词族：cryonics、cryonic、cryonically（以人体低温保存方式）、cryonicist（人体低温保存的支持者或从业者）。cryogenic（低温技术的）共享 cryo-，但含义更广。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern relationship is cryonics ↔ cryonic, following the correspondence between -ics and adjectival -ic; cryo- means 'cold,' while n is not a separate affix with an independent meaning here. The core family includes cryonics, cryonic, cryonically, and cryonicist. Cryogenic shares cryo- but has a broader technical meaning.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: cryogenic（低温技术的）泛指极低温的产生、性质和应用；cryopreservative（用于低温保存的）强调保存生物材料的作用。两者都是相关词，不能完整替代 cryonic 所含的“为可能的未来复苏而保存人体”的专门含义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Cryogenic concerns the production, properties, or uses of extremely low temperatures; cryopreservative describes something serving to preserve biological material through cooling. Neither fully expresses the particular aim of possible future human revival conveyed by cryonic.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: cryo-＝严寒：cryonic 把“极低温”与“等待未来可能复苏的人体保存”联系起来。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Cryo- means extreme cold: connect cryonic with preserving a person in the hope of possible future revival.

meaning: 物种的地方特有性；特有分布

morphology.text: endemic（地方特有的）+ -ism（状态、现象）→ endemism（地方特有性），派生时替换词尾 -ic。

etymology.text: 英语由 endemic 派生；endemic 来自希腊语 endemos（本地的），由 en（在内）和 demos（人群、地区）组成。可联想只在这一地区自然生长。

usage_note: 生态学中指物种自然分布局限在某地；单说某地数量多并不能说明 endemism。

senses.meaning_zh: 地方特有性；物种仅自然分布于某一地区的现象
senses.meaning_en: The condition of a species being naturally restricted to a particular geographical area.
senses.english_definition: Endemism is the situation in which a species occurs naturally in one particular area and nowhere else.
senses.collocation_en: high levels of endemism; island endemism
senses.collocation_zh: 高度的物种特有性；岛屿物种特有现象
senses.sentence_en: The island's long isolation has contributed to its high level of endemism.
senses.sentence_zh: 这座岛屿长期与外界隔绝，因此拥有很高的物种特有程度。

etymology_story.zh: 由 endemic 派生，远源为希腊语 endēmos，意为“本地的、在当地人群中的”，由 en（在……之内）和 dēmos（人民）组成。endemic 曾用于描述某地常见的疾病，后来也用于当地特有的生物，endemism 则成为表达这种地理局限性的名词。
etymology_story.en: Endemism derives from endemic, ultimately from Greek endēmos, meaning 'native' or 'among the people,' formed from en, 'in,' and dēmos, 'people.' Endemic was used for locally occurring diseases and later for geographically restricted organisms; endemism names that restricted distribution.

morphology_enriched.zh: endem-（见 endemic）+ -ism（状态、现象）→ endemism；也可理解为 endemic 的 -ic 被 -ism 替换。核心词族：endemic（地方特有的；地方性流行的；特有物种）、endemically（地方特有地）、endemicity（地方特有性；地方性流行状态）、endemism；专业复合词包括 neoendemism（新特有现象）、paleoendemism（古特有现象）和 microendemism（极小地域特有现象）。
morphology_enriched.en: endem- as in endemic + -ism, denoting a condition → endemism; equivalently, replace the -ic of endemic with -ism. The core family includes endemic, endemically, endemicity, and endemism. Technical compounds include neoendemism, paleoendemism, and microendemism.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: restricted distribution（局限分布）描述分布范围有限，但未必明确排除其他地区；geographical exclusivity（地理独有性）突出只存在于某地；native status（本地原生属性）只说明原生于当地，不能保证别处没有。endemism 明确包含“自然分布仅限于该地区”。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Restricted distribution describes a limited range without always explicitly excluding other places; geographical exclusivity emphasizes occurrence in one place alone; native status indicates indigenous occurrence but does not imply absence elsewhere. Endemism specifically entails natural restriction to the area concerned.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从 endemic“本地特有的”到 endemism“本地特有性”：自然界中的“仅此一地”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Move from endemic, 'restricted to this place,' to endemism, the condition of occurring naturally only here.

pronunciation.note: 主重音见 ˈ，次重音见 ˌ；按本卡音标连读各音节。

usage_note: 常修饰 source、object、astronomy。本卡的参照系是我们所在的银河系；更宽语境也可指某个星系之外。

etymology_story.zh: 由拉丁语来源的 extra-（在……之外）与 galactic（银河系的）组成，用于描述银河系之外的天体和现象。galactic 经 galaxy 这一词族追溯至希腊语 gala、词干 galakt-（乳），呼应银河如乳白色光带的外观。
etymology_story.en: Extragalactic combines Latin-derived extra-, 'outside,' with galactic to describe objects and phenomena beyond the Milky Way. Galactic belongs to the galaxy word family, ultimately connected with Greek gala, stem galakt-, 'milk,' referring to the Milky Way's milky appearance.

morphology_enriched.zh: extra-（在……之外）+ galactic（银河系的）→ extragalactic。核心相关词族：galaxy（星系）、galactic（银河系的；星系的）、galactically（从星系角度）；extragalactically（在银河系外地）为少用副词。平行构词包括 intergalactic（星系之间的）和 intragalactic（星系内部的）。
morphology_enriched.en: extra-, 'outside,' + galactic → extragalactic. The related core family includes galaxy, galactic, and galactically; extragalactically is an uncommon adverb. Parallel formations include intergalactic, 'between galaxies,' and intragalactic, 'within a galaxy.'

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: beyond the Milky Way（银河系之外的）是直接释义；intergalactic（星系间的）强调星系之间的位置；extragalactic 强调位于银河系之外，也可以指其他星系内部的天体，因此不完全等于 intergalactic。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Beyond the Milky Way is a direct paraphrase. Intergalactic emphasizes the space between galaxies, whereas extragalactic includes objects within other galaxies as well as objects between galaxies.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: extra-＝外，galactic＝银河系的：把视线移到银河系之外。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Extra- means outside, and galactic points to our galaxy: look beyond the Milky Way.

etymology_story.zh: 英语借自意大利语 genovese，由地名 Genova（热那亚）与表示地域归属的 -ese 构成。英语保留了它对当地人、地方语言和地方特色的指称，在饮食名称中尤其常见。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed Genovese from Italian genovese, formed from Genova, 'Genoa,' and the suffix -ese indicating geographical association. English retains its uses for the people, local speech, and regional characteristics, particularly in culinary names.

morphology_enriched.zh: 借入形式的意大利语内部结构为 Genov(a) + -ese → genovese；在英语中通常作为完整借词使用。相关形式：Genova（意大利语地名）、Genoa（英语地名）、Genovese 和 Genoese（相关形容词及居民、语言名称）。表示居民时，Genovese 的单复数形式相同；英语中的地域名称及其派生词通常首字母大写。
morphology_enriched.en: Within Italian, the formation is Genov(a) + -ese → genovese; English generally treats it as a complete loanword. Related forms include Genova, the Italian place name; Genoa, the English place name; and Genovese and Genoese as geographical adjectives and names for residents or local speech. The noun for a resident has the same singular and plural form, Genovese, and English geographical derivatives normally take an initial capital.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Genoese（热那亚的；热那亚人；热那亚方言）是传统英语对应词；Ligurian（利古里亚的；利古里亚语）范围更广，热那亚及其地方语言属于这一地域和语言背景；Italian（意大利的；意大利人；意大利语）范围更广，不能表达具体的热那亚归属。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Genoese is the traditional English equivalent. Ligurian refers to the broader region or language to which Genoa and its local speech belong. Italian is broader still and does not identify a specifically Genoese origin or variety.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: Genova 是热那亚，-ese 标记地域归属：Genovese 可指当地特色、当地人和当地话。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Genova is Genoa, and -ese marks geographical association: Genovese can name its characteristics, people, or local speech.

usage_note: 本卡特指逾越节家宴读本，英文正常大写 Haggadah；也有指犹太传统中非律法叙事材料的较广用法。

senses.meaning_zh: 《哈加达》；犹太教逾越节家宴仪式读本
senses.meaning_en: the text used to guide the Jewish Passover seder
senses.english_definition: A Haggadah is a book containing the story, prayers, and instructions used during the Jewish ceremonial meal at Passover.
senses.collocation_en: read the Haggadah; an illustrated Haggadah
senses.collocation_zh: 诵读《哈加达》；插图版《哈加达》

senses.sentence_zh: 逾越节家宴上，每位宾客都有一本《哈加达》，以便跟随仪式进程。

etymology_story.zh: 英语借自希伯来语 haggādāh，意为“讲述、叙述”，与表示“告诉、讲述”的动词有关。它成为逾越节家宴读本的名称，因为讲述出埃及的故事是这一仪式的核心内容。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed Hebrew haggādāh, meaning 'telling' or 'narration' and related to a verb meaning 'to tell.' It became the name of the Passover seder text because recounting the Exodus is central to that ceremony.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中视为整体借词 Haggadah，不宜按英语词缀强行拆分。词形与相关形式：Haggadahs（英语规则复数）、Haggadot／Haggadoth（希伯来语来源的复数）；Haggadic（哈加达的；也用于较广义的犹太教叙事传统）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, Haggadah is an unanalyzed loanword rather than an English root-and-affix formation. Related forms include Haggadahs, the regular English plural; Haggadot or Haggadoth, Hebrew-derived plurals; and Haggadic, an adjective also used for the broader Jewish narrative tradition.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Passover Haggadah（逾越节《哈加达》）明确其仪式用途；seder text（逾越节家宴仪式文本）是解释性近义表达；ritual book（仪式读本）范围更广，并非专指《哈加达》。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Passover Haggadah explicitly identifies the ceremonial use; seder text is an explanatory near-equivalent; ritual book is a broader category and does not specifically identify the Haggadah.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: “讲述”→ 在逾越节餐桌上讲述出埃及故事的读本。
mnemonic_anchor.en: 'Telling' → the book that guides the telling of the Exodus story at the Passover table.

pronunciation.note: 主重音见 ˈ，次重音见 ˌ；按本卡音标连读各音节。

family: hare 野兔；brain 大脑；harebrained scheme 欠考虑的计划。

morphology.text: hare（野兔）+ brain（脑子）+ -ed（有……的）→ harebrained（像野兔般乱蹦乱跳、欠考虑的）。

etymology.text: 英语把 hare 与 brain 组合，再加 -ed，用“野兔脑子”打比方，形容念头跳跃而缺乏考虑。它不是 hair（头发）组成的词。

usage_note: 带贬义，常修饰 idea、scheme、plan；批评主意愚蠢轻率，不是赞美想象力。

senses.meaning_zh: 愚蠢轻率的；欠考虑而不切实际的
senses.meaning_en: foolish, poorly considered, and impractical
senses.english_definition: If you describe an idea or plan as harebrained, you think it is foolish because someone has not considered it carefully.
senses.collocation_en: a harebrained scheme; a harebrained idea
senses.collocation_zh: 轻率荒唐的计划；欠考虑的主意
senses.sentence_en: His harebrained scheme to save money ended up costing us more.
senses.sentence_zh: 他那个轻率荒唐的省钱计划，最后反而让我们花了更多钱。

etymology_story.zh: 这个词由 hare（野兔）和 brained（有……头脑的）组成，以野兔容易受惊、行动急促的形象比喻人的轻率。其构词依据是 hare，而非 hair（头发），尽管历史上也出现过 hairbrained 这一变体拼写。
etymology_story.en: The word combines hare with brained, drawing on the hare's reputation for being easily startled and behaving impulsively. Its underlying image is a hare, although the variant spelling hairbrained has also appeared historically.

morphology_enriched.zh: hare（野兔）+ brain（头脑）+ -ed（具有……的）→ harebrained。相关形式：hare-brained（连字符拼写）、harebrainedness（轻率、欠考虑，较少见）；基础词 brain 的相关词包括 brainy（聪明的）和 brainless（愚蠢的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Hare + brain + -ed, meaning 'having the specified kind of brain,' forms harebrained. Related forms include the hyphenated spelling hare-brained and the less common noun harebrainedness; the base brain also appears in brainy and brainless.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: foolish（愚蠢的）泛指判断欠佳；rash（轻率的）强调未经考虑便仓促行动；ill-conceived（构思欠周的）强调计划从设计之初就存在问题。harebrained 常带嘲讽或幽默色彩，尤指荒唐的主意和计划。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Foolish broadly describes poor judgment; rash emphasizes acting too quickly without considering consequences; ill-conceived emphasizes flaws in a plan's original design. Harebrained often sounds mocking or humorous and especially describes absurd ideas or schemes.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 野兔乱蹿，脑中主意也乱蹿 → 轻率欠考虑。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture ideas darting around like a startled hare: quick movement with little thought.

pronunciation.note: 主重音见 ˈ，次重音见 ˌ；按本卡音标连读各音节。

forms: 通常作不可数矿物名；英式拼写也作 haematite。
family: haematite 赤铁矿的英式变体；hematitic 赤铁矿的。

morphology.text: hemat-（血，指红色）+ -ite（矿物后缀）→ hematite（赤铁矿）；不要把 -ite 看作表示炎症的 -itis。

etymology.text: 希腊语 haimatites lithos 意为“血色的石头”，经拉丁语、法语进入英语。名字可用其红褐色粉末和条痕来记。

usage_note: 矿物名称，主要成分为氧化铁；hematite 与 haematite 是同一矿物的拼写变体。

senses.meaning_zh: 赤铁矿；主要成分为氧化铁的矿物
senses.meaning_en: an iron oxide mineral that is an important iron ore
senses.english_definition: Hematite is a mineral made of iron oxide that is an important source of iron and produces a reddish-brown streak when rubbed on a suitable surface.
senses.collocation_zh: 赤铁矿矿床；赤铁矿矿石
senses.sentence_en: The sample looked metallic, but its reddish-brown streak helped identify it as hematite.
senses.sentence_zh: 这块样品看起来具有金属光泽，但其红褐色条痕帮助人们确认它是赤铁矿。

etymology_story.zh: 这个词经法语和拉丁语追溯至希腊语 haimatitēs，意为“血色的”，与 haima（血）有关。名称指向赤铁矿的红色粉末或条痕，即使矿物表面呈灰黑色或具有金属光泽，这一特征仍然存在。
etymology_story.en: The word comes through French and Latin from Greek haimatitēs, meaning 'bloodlike,' related to haima, 'blood.' The name refers to its red powder or streak, which remains characteristic even when the mineral looks dark or metallic.

morphology_enriched.zh: 学术构词可分析为 hemat-（血）+ -ite（矿物名称中常见的后缀）。相关词形：haematite（英式变体拼写）、hematitic／haematitic（赤铁矿的；含赤铁矿的）、hematitization（赤铁矿化，地质学术语）；-ite 不等于表示炎症的 -itis。
morphology_enriched.en: As a learned formation, hematite can be analyzed as hemat-, 'blood,' plus -ite, a suffix common in mineral names. Related forms include the British spelling haematite, the adjectives hematitic and haematitic, and the geological noun hematitization; -ite is distinct from the inflammatory suffix -itis.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: red iron ore（红铁矿、赤铁矿）是描述性名称；specularite（镜铁矿）指具有闪亮金属光泽的赤铁矿变种；iron ore（铁矿石）是更广的类别，也包括磁铁矿等其他矿物。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Red iron ore is a descriptive name for hematite; specularite denotes a glittering, metallic variety of hematite; iron ore is a broader category that also includes other minerals, such as magnetite.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: hemat- 想到“血”，-ite 想到“矿石” → 留下血红色条痕的赤铁矿。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Hemat- suggests blood and -ite suggests a mineral: remember the mineral by its blood-red streak.

senses.meaning_zh: 水烟筒；水烟壶

senses.english_definition: A hookah is a smoking device with a water container and a tube through which someone draws smoke after it has passed through the water.

etymology_story.zh: 英语通过印度次大陆的印地语、乌尔都语用法借入这个词，最终源自阿拉伯语 ḥuqqa，意为“小盒子、小容器”。这个容器名称在相关语言中转而指整套水烟器具。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed the word through Hindi and Urdu usage in the Indian subcontinent, ultimately from Arabic ḥuqqa, meaning 'a small box or container.' The container name came to designate the complete water-pipe apparatus.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 hookah 是整体借词，不能拆成 hook + -ah。复数为 hookahs；常见复合表达包括 hookah pipe（水烟筒）、hookah bar（水烟馆）、hookah lounge（水烟休闲馆）和 hookah smoking（抽水烟），没有常用的单词式派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, hookah is an unanalyzed loanword, not hook plus -ah. Its plural is hookahs; common compounds include hookah pipe, hookah bar, hookah lounge, and hookah smoking, with no established common family of affixed derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: water pipe（水烟器）是较宽泛的描述性名称；narghile（水烟筒）常指同类器具，具有地域色彩；shisha（水烟、水烟烟草）在一些地区也指器具，但也常指所用的烟草。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Water pipe is a broader descriptive term; narghile is a regional name for the same general apparatus; shisha can name the apparatus in some varieties of English but also commonly refers to the tobacco used in it.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with the original 'small container,' picture the water vessel, then recall the whole smoking apparatus.

senses.meaning_zh: 较不易引起过敏的；低致敏性的
senses.meaning_en: less likely than comparable alternatives to cause an allergic reaction
senses.english_definition: Something described as hypoallergenic is considered less likely to cause an allergic reaction, although it can still cause one.
senses.collocation_zh: 低致敏性化妆品；低致敏性寝具
senses.sentence_en: She chose a hypoallergenic moisturizer because her skin was sensitive.
senses.sentence_zh: 由于皮肤敏感，她选择了一款低致敏性的保湿霜。

etymology_story.zh: 这个词在20世纪的英语中由希腊语来源的 hypo-（低于、较少）与 allergenic（致敏的）组合而成。它表达的是引起过敏的可能性较低，而不是保证完全不会引起过敏。
etymology_story.en: The word was formed in twentieth-century English by combining the Greek-derived prefix hypo-, 'below' or 'less,' with allergenic. It expresses a reduced likelihood of causing allergy rather than a guarantee that no reaction can occur.

morphology_enriched.zh: hypo-（较低、较少）+ allergenic（致敏的）→ hypoallergenic；allergenic 可进一步分析为 allergen（过敏原）+ -ic（……的）。相关词族：allergy（过敏）、allergic（过敏的）、allergen（过敏原）、allergenic（致敏的）、allergenicity（致敏性）、hypoallergenicity（低致敏性）和 allergist（过敏专科医生）。
morphology_enriched.en: Hypo- ('less') + allergenic forms hypoallergenic; allergenic can be further analyzed as allergen + -ic. The related word family includes allergy, allergic, allergen, allergenic, allergenicity, hypoallergenicity, and allergist.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: low-allergen（低过敏原的）强调过敏原含量或释放量较低；nonallergenic（不致敏的）表达更强的“不引起过敏”含义；anti-allergic（抗过敏的）强调预防或缓解过敏反应。三者都不能在所有语境中替换 hypoallergenic。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Low-allergen emphasizes a reduced amount or release of allergens; nonallergenic makes the stronger claim of not causing allergy; anti-allergic describes preventing or relieving allergic reactions. None is interchangeable with hypoallergenic in every context.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: hypo- = 较少；allergenic = 致敏的 → 较少致敏，不代表绝不致敏。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Hypo- means less; allergenic means allergy-causing: less likely to trigger allergy does not mean impossible.

etymology_story.zh: 英语直接借用了夏威夷语树名 koa，指夏威夷本土的寇阿相思树。这个名称也用于指这种树提供的珍贵木材。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed koa directly from Hawaiian as the name of a native Hawaiian tree. The name also came to denote the tree's valuable timber.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 koa 是不可再分的借词，没有可分析的英语前后缀。表示树木时可数，复数可用 koas；表示木材时通常不可数。常见复合表达有 koa tree（寇阿相思树）、koa wood（寇阿相思木）和 koa finch（寇阿雀）；这些是复合表达，不是后缀派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, koa is an unanalyzable loanword with no English prefix or suffix. It is countable for individual trees, with the plural koas, and normally uncountable for timber. Compounds include koa tree, koa wood, and koa finch; these are compounds rather than suffix-derived forms.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Hawaiian koa（夏威夷寇阿相思树）是强调产地的名称；Acacia koa（寇阿相思树）是精确的植物学名称；koa wood（寇阿相思木）只指木材。普通词 acacia（相思树）涵盖许多种，不能始终与 koa 互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Hawaiian koa emphasizes the tree's geographical identity; Acacia koa is its precise botanical name; koa wood specifies the timber. The broader word acacia covers many species and is not always interchangeable with koa.

etymology_story.zh: 英语在19世纪采用医学拉丁语 laryngitis，由源自希腊语 larynx 的词干 laryng-（喉）与表示炎症的 -itis 构成。其名称直接表示喉部发生炎症。
etymology_story.en: English adopted the medical Latin term laryngitis in the nineteenth century. It combines laryng-, the stem of Greek larynx, with the inflammation suffix -itis, literally identifying inflammation of the voice box.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：laryng-（喉）+ -itis（炎症）→ laryngitis（喉炎），通常作不可数名词。同根词族包括 larynx（喉）、laryngeal（喉的）、laryngology（喉科学）、laryngologist（喉科医师）、laryngoscope（喉镜）、laryngoscopy（喉镜检查）和 laryngectomy（喉切除术）；这些词共享词根，并非都由 laryngitis 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: laryng- (larynx) + -itis (inflammation) → laryngitis, normally an uncountable noun. The root family includes larynx, laryngeal, laryngology, laryngologist, laryngoscope, laryngoscopy, and laryngectomy. These share the same root rather than all deriving directly from laryngitis.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Laryngeal inflammation（喉部炎症）是医学性释义；inflammation of the voice box（发声器官喉部的炎症）是通俗释义。Hoarseness（声音嘶哑）只是可能出现的症状，不能作为该病名的严格同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Laryngeal inflammation is a technical equivalent; inflammation of the voice box is a plain-language equivalent. Hoarseness names a possible symptom rather than the condition itself.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: laryng- 是喉，-itis 是炎症：喉发炎，声音就可能变哑。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Laryng- means voice box and -itis means inflammation: an inflamed voice box can make your voice hoarse.

etymology_story.zh: Mescal 经墨西哥西班牙语 mezcal 进入英语，最终源于纳瓦特尔语 mexcalli，通常释为“熟制的龙舌兰”。名称从加工后的植物材料扩展到龙舌兰蒸馏酒；另有指佩奥特仙人掌的传统用法，属于不同的植物所指。
etymology_story.en: Mescal entered English through Mexican Spanish mezcal, ultimately from Nahuatl mexcalli, usually interpreted as 'cooked agave.' The name extended from prepared plant material to an agave spirit; its traditional use for peyote refers to a different plant.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语把 mescal 作为完整借词，不拆分为英语词根和词缀；mezcal 是同词的另一拼写。酒作为物质时通常不可数，表示份量、种类或植株时可用复数 mescals。相关词 mescaline（麦司卡林；美斯卡灵）与 mescal 的佩奥特义在词源上有关，不能据此把它理解为梅斯卡尔酒的成分。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English treats mescal as a whole loanword, with mezcal as an alternative spelling. The drink is normally uncountable as a substance; mescals can denote servings, varieties, or individual plants. The related word mescaline is historically connected with the peyote sense of mescal, so that relationship does not identify mescaline as an ingredient of the spirit.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Mezcal（梅斯卡尔酒）是酒义的同词异拼；agave（龙舌兰）是植物义的上位词，范围更广；peyote（佩奥特仙人掌）只对应较少见的仙人掌义。理解这些词时须先判断 mescal 指酒、龙舌兰还是仙人掌。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Mezcal is an alternative spelling for the spirit; agave is a broader term corresponding to the plant sense; peyote matches only the less common cactus sense. The appropriate equivalent depends on which meaning of mescal is intended.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Follow the main chain 'cooked agave → agave spirit'; mescal buttons signals the separate peyote sense.

etymology_story.zh: 英语短语 my lady 被法语借用并写作 milady，随后这一法语形式又进入英语。它保留了对英国贵妇人的尊称意味，后来也发展出戏谑或刻意恭敬的用法。
etymology_story.en: French borrowed the English phrase my lady as milady, and English subsequently borrowed that French form back. It retained its association with addressing an English noblewoman and later acquired playful or elaborately courteous uses.

morphology_enriched.zh: 词源结构是 my（我的）+ lady（夫人），经法语形式形成 milady；现代英语通常把它作为完整称呼词使用，复数为 miladies。对应的男性称呼是 milord（老爷；大人）。Lady（女士；夫人）、ladyship（贵妇人的身份；夫人尊称）和 ladylike（淑女般的）属于 lady 的相关词族，并非 milady 的直接派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Its historical structure is my + lady, reshaped through French into milady; modern English generally treats it as a complete title, with the plural miladies. The corresponding masculine title is milord. Lady, ladyship, and ladylike belong to the related lady family rather than being direct derivatives of milady.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: My lady（夫人）保留较明确的贵族称呼或历史语境；Your Ladyship（夫人阁下）更正式，适用于特定贵族身份；madam（女士；夫人）是较广泛的礼貌称呼，不必涉及贵族身份。Milady 在现代语境中尤其容易带出戏谑感。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: My lady retains a clearer aristocratic or historical setting; Your Ladyship is more formal and tied to particular titles; madam is a broader polite address that does not require noble status. Milady is especially liable to sound playful in modern contexts.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Hear milady as a fused my lady: a courteous title with an aristocratic or playful tone.

senses.meaning_zh: 神经毒素；损害神经细胞或干扰神经系统功能的毒性物质

etymology_story.zh: Neurotoxin 是现代科学英语中由 neuro-（神经）与 toxin（毒素）组成的词；neuro- 最终源于希腊语 neuron，其古义包括“筋、腱”，后来用于神经。这个组合把毒性作用的靶点直接写进名称。
etymology_story.en: Neurotoxin is a modern scientific formation combining neuro- with toxin. Neuro- ultimately comes from Greek neuron, meaning 'sinew' or 'tendon' and later associated with nerves, so the compound identifies the target of the poisonous action.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：neuro-（神经）+ toxin（毒素）→ neurotoxin（神经毒素），复数为 neurotoxins。相关词族包括 neurotoxic（具有神经毒性的）、neurotoxicity（神经毒性）、neurotoxicant（神经毒性物质）、neurotoxicology（神经毒理学）和 neurotoxicologist（神经毒理学家）；这些是共享构词成分的相关形式。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: neuro- (nerve) + toxin (poisonous substance) → neurotoxin; plural neurotoxins. Related family members include neurotoxic, neurotoxicity, neurotoxicant, neurotoxicology, and neurotoxicologist. These are related formations sharing the same combining elements.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Nerve poison（神经毒物）是通俗近义表达；neurotoxic substance（神经毒性物质）是较宽泛的描述；neurotoxicant（神经毒性物质）常见于毒理学，可强调环境或合成化学物质。严格用语中 toxin 常强调生物来源，但 neurotoxin 也存在较宽泛的实际用法。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Nerve poison is a plain-language near-equivalent; neurotoxic substance is a broad descriptive phrase; neurotoxicant is common in toxicology and may emphasize environmental or synthetic chemicals. Strict usage often reserves toxin for substances of biological origin, although neurotoxin also occurs more broadly.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: neuro- 锁定神经，toxin 表示毒素：专门干扰神经线路的毒。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Neuro- points to nerves and toxin means poison: picture a poison disrupting the body's nerve wiring.
