senses.meaning_zh: 三轮摩托车；机动三轮车，非正式用语
senses.meaning_en: An informal word for a three-wheeled motorcycle or similar motor vehicle.
senses.english_definition: A trike is a motor vehicle similar to a motorcycle but with three wheels.
senses.collocation_en: a motor trike; ride a trike
senses.collocation_zh: 一辆机动三轮车；驾驶三轮摩托车
senses.sentence_en: He toured the coast on a three-wheeled motor trike.
senses.sentence_zh: 他驾驶一辆三轮摩托车沿海岸旅行。

etymology_story.zh: Trike 由 tricycle 缩短并改拼而来，其形式与 bike 相似。原词 tricycle 中的 tri- 表示“三”，后半部分最终与表示“轮、圆”的希腊语词有关；简称后来也用于三轮摩托车。
etymology_story.en: Trike is a shortened and respelled form of tricycle, resembling bike in form. In tricycle, tri- means “three,” and the second element ultimately relates to a Greek word for “wheel” or “circle”; the shortened name also came to be used for three-wheeled motorcycles.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词方式：tricycle → 缩略并改拼 → trike，不能把现代 trike 硬拆成 tri- + -ke。复数为 trikes，没有广泛使用的普通派生词族；源词词族包括 tricycle（三轮车）和 tricyclist（三轮车骑行者），另有 electric trike（电动三轮车）和 recumbent trike（躺式三轮车）等复合表达。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: tricycle → shortening and respelling → trike; modern trike should not be forced into tri- + -ke. The plural is trikes, and there is no widely used general derivative family; the source-word family includes tricycle and tricyclist, while compounds include electric trike and recumbent trike.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: tricycle（三轮车）是较中性的完整名称；three-wheeler（三轮交通工具）范围较广，可指脚踏或机动车辆；motor tricycle（三轮摩托车）明确指机动车。trike 是较口语化的简称，具体类型依语境判断。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Tricycle is the more neutral full term; three-wheeler is broader and can refer to pedal-powered or motor vehicles; motor tricycle explicitly identifies a motor vehicle. Trike is the informal shortened term, with the vehicle type determined by context.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: tricycle 缩成 trike：抓住原词 tri- 的“三”，记住三个轮子。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Tricycle becomes trike: retain the source word's tri-, “three,” and picture three wheels.

meaning: 涂油礼；宗教仪式中的傅油

pronunciation.note: 采用词典所列读音；重音由 ˈ 标记。

forms: 此义通常不可数；指一种具体仪式时也可数。
family: unctionless 缺少宗教热忱的；anoint 涂油。

morphology.text: unction + -less → unctionless（缺少宗教热忱的）；unction 整词作为独立词素记忆。

etymology.text: 中古英语借自拉丁语 unctio，来自 ungere“涂抹、傅油”；从把油涂在身上的动作记宗教仪式。

usage_note: 正式宗教用语；另有过分殷勤、做作热忱的意思，须由上下文区分。

senses.meaning_zh: 傅油；傅油礼，尤指宗教仪式中的敷油
senses.meaning_en: anointing with oil, especially in a religious ceremony
senses.english_definition: Unction is the act of putting oil on someone as part of a religious ceremony.
senses.collocation_zh: 临终傅油礼；神圣傅油礼
senses.sentence_en: The priest administered extreme unction to the dying man.
senses.sentence_zh: 神父为那位垂危男子施行了临终傅油礼。

senses.meaning_zh: 【正式，贬义】虚情假意的热忱；谄媚圆滑的言谈举止
senses.meaning_en: exaggerated, insincere warmth or flattering earnestness
senses.english_definition: Unction is a way of speaking or behaving that seems warmly sincere but feels exaggerated or false.
senses.collocation_zh: 带着做作的热忱；过分的虚情假意
senses.sentence_en: He praised his employer with an unction that made his colleagues uncomfortable.
senses.sentence_zh: 他用一种做作而谄媚的热忱赞美雇主，让同事们感到不自在。

senses.meaning_zh: 【宗教】灵性热忱；言语中感人的宗教感染力
senses.meaning_en: spiritual fervour or an emotionally moving religious quality
senses.english_definition: Unction is a quality of deep religious feeling that gives someone's words spiritual force.
senses.collocation_zh: 满怀灵性热忱地布道；灵性的感染力
senses.sentence_en: The congregation remembered the unction with which she spoke.
senses.sentence_zh: 会众记得她讲话时那种感人的宗教热忱。

etymology_story.zh: 中古英语 unctioun 借自拉丁语 unctio“涂油”，其词干来自 ungere“涂抹、傅油”的过去分词 unctus。由实际的傅油仪式发展出“灵性热忱”，又进一步产生讽刺性的“做作热忱、圆滑谄媚”义。
etymology_story.en: Middle English unctioun was borrowed from Latin unctio, meaning anointing, formed from unctus, the past participle of ungere, to anoint. Religious anointing led to the sense of spiritual fervour and subsequently to the ironic sense of affected earnestness or oily flattery.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语通常整体识记；历史结构可辨为 unct-（傅油）＋-ion（行为名词后缀），不能拆成否定前缀 un-。直接派生有罕见的 unctional（傅油的）和 unctionless（缺乏灵性热忱或感染力的）；同源词有 unctuous（油滑谄媚的；油腻的）、unctuously（油滑谄媚地）、unctuousness（油滑谄媚）、unctuosity（油腻；油滑，较少用）和 unguent（软膏）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, learn the word largely as a whole; its historical structure is unct- meaning anoint, plus the action-noun suffix -ion, rather than negative un-. Direct derivatives include rare unctional and unctionless; related words include unctuous, unctuously, unctuousness, the less common unctuosity, and unguent.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: anointing（傅油）突出实际仪式或动作；fervour（热忱）突出强烈而通常真诚的感情；smarminess（油滑谄媚）只对应贬义用法，突出令人反感的虚假亲切。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Anointing names the physical act or ritual; fervour emphasizes intense and usually sincere feeling; smarminess matches the disapproving sense and stresses unpleasantly false friendliness.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 给身体“抹油”是傅油；给话语“抹油”便可能是油滑谄媚。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Oil applied to the body suggests anointing; imagined oil applied to speech suggests slippery flattery.

meaning: 好地；顺利地（苏格兰用语，相当于 well）

pronunciation.note: 采用词典所列读音；重音由 ˈ 标记。

forms: 作副词不变形；标准英语对应形式为 well。
family: weel-kent 众所周知的（苏格兰用语）。

morphology.text: weel + kent（known 的苏格兰形式） → weel-kent（众所周知的）；weel 整词作为独立词素记忆。

etymology.text: 苏格兰语中相当于 well 的形式，与古英语 wel 一脉相承；读苏格兰对白时把它和 well 联系起来。

usage_note: 苏格兰地域用语，适合识读文学对白；普通英语写作使用 well。

senses.meaning_zh: 【苏格兰语】好地；顺利地；充分地，相当于 well
senses.meaning_en: well, successfully, or thoroughly in Scots
senses.english_definition: In Scots, if someone does something weel, they do it well or successfully.
senses.collocation_zh: 做得好；很了解某人
senses.sentence_en: Ye did weel to finish before dark.
senses.sentence_zh: 你赶在天黑前完成了，做得很好。

senses.meaning_zh: 【苏格兰语】健康的；安好的；状况良好的
senses.meaning_en: healthy or in a satisfactory condition in Scots
senses.english_definition: In Scots, someone who is weel is healthy or feeling all right.
senses.collocation_zh: 感觉身体好；保持安康
senses.sentence_en: I'm no weel today.
senses.sentence_zh: 我今天身体不舒服。

senses.meaning_zh: 【苏格兰语】哎呀；好嘛，表示惊讶、责备或催促
senses.meaning_en: well, used in Scots to express surprise, reproach, or impatience
senses.english_definition: In Scots, you can say weel to show surprise or to urge someone to answer.
senses.collocation_zh: 哎呀，哎呀！；嗯，怎么说？
senses.sentence_en: Weel, weel! I never expected to see you here.
senses.sentence_zh: 哎呀，哎呀！真没想到会在这里见到你。

senses.meaning_zh: 【苏格兰语】嗯；那么；好吧，用于引出话语或回应
senses.meaning_en: well, used in Scots to introduce a remark or response
senses.english_definition: In Scots, you can use weel at the beginning of a remark while deciding what to say or introducing a response.
senses.collocation_zh: 那么；嗯，我想
senses.sentence_en: Weel, we can try again tomorrow.
senses.sentence_zh: 好吧，我们明天可以再试一次。

etymology_story.zh: weel 是苏格兰语中与标准英语 well 对应的形式，两者都承自古英语 wel。现代用法保留了“好地、健康的”等意义，也用于引出话语或表达感叹。
etymology_story.en: Weel is the Scots counterpart of standard English well, both continuing Old English wel. It retains meanings concerning successful action and good health, alongside conversational and exclamatory uses.

morphology_enriched.zh: weel 是单纯词，无现代前后缀；weel＋kent（苏格兰语“已知的”）→ weel-kent（众所周知的），weel＋being → weel-being（安康）。对应 well 的比较级和最高级通常使用不规则形式 better、best，具体拼写可随苏格兰语变体而异。
morphology_enriched.en: Weel is a simple word without modern prefixes or suffixes. Compounds include weel-kent, meaning well-known, and weel-being, meaning welfare; comparison generally uses irregular better and best, with spelling varying across Scots varieties.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: well（好地；健康的）是标准英语中的直接对应词；successfully（成功地）只对应副词中“取得好结果”的意义；healthy（健康的）只对应形容词的身体状况义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Well is the direct standard-English counterpart; successfully covers only the adverbial sense of achieving a good result; healthy covers only the adjective referring to physical condition.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 weel 直接连到 well：事情做得好、人身体好，开口也能说“嗯，好吧”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link weel directly to well: doing well, feeling well, and beginning a reply with 'well'.

pronunciation.note: 采用词典所列读音；重音由 ˈ 标记。

morphology.text: yttr-（关联 yttria，氧化钇） + -ium（元素名词尾） → yttrium（钇）。

etymology.text: 19世纪的新拉丁语元素名，以瑞典村庄 Ytterby 命名；把村名与元素符号 Y 联系起来。

usage_note: 名称通常小写，符号写 Y；不要与 ytterbium（镱）混淆。

senses.meaning_zh: 钇：符号 Y、原子序数 39 的银白色金属元素
senses.meaning_en: a silvery metallic element with symbol Y and atomic number 39
senses.english_definition: Yttrium is a silvery metal that is used in alloys, lasers, and other specialized materials.
senses.collocation_zh: 氧化钇；钇铝石榴石
senses.sentence_en: Yttrium oxide is added to some optical glasses to improve their resistance to heat.
senses.sentence_zh: 某些光学玻璃中会加入氧化钇，以提高其耐热性。

etymology_story.zh: yttrium 最终得名于瑞典村庄 Ytterby，当地矿物促成了钇的发现。这个地名也体现在其氧化物名称 yttria 中，后来元素名称采用了金属元素常见的 -ium 词尾。
etymology_story.en: Yttrium ultimately takes its name from Ytterby, the Swedish village whose minerals led to its discovery. The place name also appears in yttria, the oxide name, while the element name carries the familiar metallic-element ending -ium.

morphology_enriched.zh: 可辨识为 yttr-（地名来源的化学词干）＋-ium（元素名词尾）；yttr- 不是可独立使用的普通英语词。相关词有 yttria（氧化钇）、yttric（钇的，较少用）、yttriferous（含钇的，专业用语）；常见复合结构有 yttrium-containing（含钇的）、yttrium-doped（掺钇的）。
morphology_enriched.en: The recognizable structure is yttr-, a place-name-derived chemical stem, plus the element ending -ium; yttr- is not an independent ordinary English word. Related forms include yttria, the less common adjective yttric, the specialist adjective yttriferous, and compounds such as yttrium-containing and yttrium-doped.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Y（钇的元素符号）是同一元素的符号写法；element 39（第39号元素）是描述性同指表达；rare-earth metal（稀土金属）是包含钇的上位类别，不是其同义词。yttria 指氧化钇，不能与 yttrium 互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Y is the symbol for the same element, and element 39 is a descriptive equivalent. Rare-earth metal is a broader category rather than a synonym; yttria means yttrium oxide and is not interchangeable with yttrium.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: Ytterby 的 Y，连到 yttrium 的元素符号 Y。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect the Y of Ytterby with yttrium and its symbol Y.

pronunciation.note: 采用词典所列读音；重音由 ˈ 标记。

forms: 可数名词；复数 analytes。
family: analysis 分析；analyst 分析人员。

morphology.text: ana-（取自 analysis 或 analyze） + -lyte（化学名词成分） → analyte（被分析的物质）。

etymology.text: 20世纪英语化学术语，由 analysis 或 analyze 的截短形式与 -lyte 组合而成；把它记成分析工作所针对的物质。

usage_note: 化学与检测专业用语；一个样品可含多个 analytes，本词指具体被测物。

senses.english_definition: An analyte is the substance in a sample that a test is intended to identify or measure.

senses.sentence_zh: 葡萄糖是这些血液样本中的目标被测物。

etymology_story.zh: analyte 是20世纪出现的分析化学术语，由 analysis 或 analyze 的截短成分与 -lyte 组合而成。它专指分析所针对的物质，而不是从事分析的人。
etymology_story.en: Analyte arose in twentieth-century analytical chemistry from a shortened form of analysis or analyze combined with -lyte. It names the substance targeted by analysis, rather than the person performing it.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词来源可写作 ana(lysis) 或 ana(lyze)＋-lyte；这里的 ana- 是截短成分，不能单独解释成具有固定意义的普通前缀。复数为 analytes；常见复合形式有 multi-analyte（多分析物的）。相关词族包括 analyse/analyze（分析）、analysis（分析；复数 analyses）、analyst（分析人员）、analytic/analytical（分析的）、analytically（从分析角度）；这些相关词并非都由 analyte 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Its formation can be represented as ana(lysis) or ana(lyze) plus -lyte; ana- here is a clipped element, not a separately meaningful ordinary prefix. The plural is analytes, and multi-analyte is a useful compound; related forms include analyse/analyze, analysis with plural analyses, analyst, analytic/analytical, and analytically, rather than all being derivatives of analyte.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: target compound（目标化合物）适用于被测物确为化合物时，范围比 analyte 窄；measurand（被测量）指拟测定的量，如葡萄糖浓度，而不是葡萄糖本身；sample（样本）指送检材料，通常包含分析物及其他成分。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Target compound is a narrower near-equivalent when the analyte is a compound. Measurand names the quantity being measured, such as glucose concentration; sample names the tested material, which may contain the analyte and many other components.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 分析对象是 analyte；分析人员是 analyst。
mnemonic_anchor.en: The analyte is what you analyze; the analyst is who analyzes it.

etymology_story.zh: bactericide 是19世纪形成的科学词，由 bacteri- 与 -cide 组合而成。前者最终源自希腊语 baktērion“小杆”，与早期观察到的杆状细菌有关；后者源自拉丁语 caedere“杀死”。
etymology_story.en: Bactericide was formed in nineteenth-century scientific vocabulary from bacteri- and -cide. The first element ultimately reflects Greek baktērion, meaning a small rod, associated with rod-shaped bacteria; the second comes from Latin caedere, to kill.

morphology_enriched.zh: bacteri-（细菌）＋-cide（杀灭剂）→ bactericide（杀细菌剂）；复数为 bactericides。直接派生词有 bactericidal（杀细菌的）和 bactericidally（以杀细菌的方式）；较少见的变体为 bacteriocide。相关词有 bacterium（单个细菌）、bacteria（细菌的复数）和 bacterial（细菌的）；表示“杀细菌的”通常用 bactericidal。
morphology_enriched.en: Bacteri- meaning bacteria plus -cide meaning a killing agent forms bactericide; its plural is bactericides. Direct derivatives are bactericidal and bactericidally, and bacteriocide is a less common variant; related forms include singular bacterium, plural bacteria, and bacterial. The usual adjective meaning bacteria-killing is bactericidal.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: antibacterial agent（抗细菌剂）范围较广，可杀死细菌，也可只抑制其生长；germicide（杀微生物剂）不限于细菌；bacteriostat（抑菌剂）强调抑制细菌生长，不一定杀死细菌。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Antibacterial agent is broader and may either kill bacteria or inhibit their growth. Germicide is not restricted to bacteria; bacteriostat specifically emphasizes growth inhibition rather than necessarily killing bacteria.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: bacteri-＝细菌，-cide＝杀灭：直接锁定“杀细菌的药剂”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Bacteri- means bacteria and -cide signals killing: an agent that kills bacteria.

senses.meaning_zh: 走开！滚开！（旧式、文学或诙谐用语）
senses.meaning_en: Go away! Used in old-fashioned, literary, or humorous commands.

etymology_story.zh: 源自命令式短语 be gone，字面意思是“处于已经离开的状态”。合写后成为带有旧式或戏剧性色彩的驱逐用语。
etymology_story.en: Begone developed from the imperative phrase be gone, literally commanding someone to be absent. The joined form became an old-fashioned or theatrical command to leave.

morphology_enriched.zh: 历史构成为 be + gone；现代英语中通常把它看作凝固的感叹词，而不是可自由变化的普通动词。无常用派生词，也不用作带有 -s、-ed 或 -ing 形式的规则动词。
morphology_enriched.en: Historically be + gone; in modern use, it is generally a fixed interjection rather than a freely inflected verb. It has no common derivatives and does not take regular verbal forms in -s, -ed, or -ing.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: go away（走开）最普通直接；get out（出去、滚出去）强调离开某个地方，往往更强硬；be off（走吧、走开）较口语化。begone 带明显的古雅、戏剧或诙谐色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Go away is the ordinary direct command; get out stresses leaving a place and is often more forceful; be off is more conversational. Begone sounds distinctly archaic, theatrical, or humorous.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: be + gone：“我要你已经不在这里了”→走开！
mnemonic_anchor.en: Be + gone: 'Be absent from here' → 'Go away!'

senses.meaning_zh: 删改作品中被认为冒犯、不雅或不宜的内容
senses.meaning_en: Remove or alter supposedly offensive or unsuitable material in a work.
senses.english_definition: If someone bowdlerises a book, play, or other work, they remove or change parts that they consider offensive or unsuitable, often weakening the original.
senses.chinese_definition: 如果某人 bowdlerises 一本书、一部戏剧或其他作品，就是删去或改动其中被认为冒犯或不适宜的部分，而且往往损害原作。
senses.collocation_en: bowdlerise a text; a bowdlerised version
senses.collocation_zh: 删改文本；经过删改的版本
senses.sentence_en: The publisher bowdlerised the novel for younger readers, removing its sexual references.
senses.sentence_zh: 出版商为适应年幼读者而删改了这部小说，去掉了其中涉及性的内容。

etymology_story.zh: 来自英国编辑托马斯·鲍德勒（Thomas Bowdler）的姓氏，与鲍德勒家族删去被认为不适合家庭阅读内容的莎士比亚版本有关。这个姓氏后来变成动词，通常含有因道德顾虑而损害原作的贬义。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Thomas Bowdler's surname and the Bowdler family's editions of Shakespeare that removed material considered unsuitable for family reading. It became a usually disapproving verb for expurgation that damages an original work.

morphology_enriched.zh: Bowdler（人名词基）+ -ise（构成动词）；bowdlerize 是美式常用拼写，也见于采用 -ize 的英式写法。词族：bowdlerises、bowdlerised、bowdlerising；bowdlerisation（删改）、bowdleriser（删改者）、bowdlerism（此类删改的做法）；相应 -ize 形式为 bowdlerizes、bowdlerized、bowdlerizing、bowdlerization、bowdlerizer。
morphology_enriched.en: Bowdler, a personal-name base, + the verb-forming suffix -ise. Bowdlerize is the usual American spelling and also occurs in British -ize usage. Family: bowdlerises, bowdlerised, bowdlerising; bowdlerisation, bowdleriser, and bowdlerism; corresponding -ize forms include bowdlerizes, bowdlerized, bowdlerizing, bowdlerization, and bowdlerizer.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: expurgate（删除不宜内容）最接近，较正式；censor（审查并删禁）范围更广，可涉及政治、安全或道德理由；sanitize（净化、美化）强调去掉令人不快或有争议的细节。bowdlerise 尤其暗示为迎合道德标准而损害作品。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Expurgate is the closest formal synonym; censor covers broader suppression for political, security, or moral reasons; sanitize emphasizes removing disturbing or controversial details. Bowdlerise particularly suggests damaging a work to satisfy standards of propriety.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 鲍德勒姓氏变动词：把作品删成“全家都能读”的版本。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Bowdler's name becomes an action: edit a work into a supposedly family-safe version.

senses.meaning_zh: 玉髓；由极细微二氧化硅晶体构成的矿物材料
senses.meaning_en: A microcrystalline silica material used as an ornamental stone.
senses.english_definition: Chalcedony is a mineral material made of very small silica crystals that is often used to make jewellery and decorative objects.
senses.chinese_definition: 玉髓是一种由极细微二氧化硅晶体构成的矿物材料，常用于制作首饰和装饰品。
senses.collocation_zh: 蓝玉髓；一颗玉髓珠

etymology_story.zh: 经拉丁语及法语形式传入英语，最终可追溯到希腊语 khalkēdōn，一种古代宝石的名称。它常被联系到古城 Chalcedon（迦克墩），但这种联系以及古代名称所指的具体矿物都存在不确定性。
etymology_story.en: The word reached English through Latin and French forms and ultimately goes back to Greek khalkēdōn, the name of an ancient gemstone. It is often associated with the city of Chalcedon, although both that connection and the precise ancient mineral identification are uncertain.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中作为整体借词处理，没有可独立用于释义的常用前后缀拆分。词族：chalcedonies（指不同种类或不同块玉髓时的复数）、chalcedonic（玉髓的、含玉髓的）；另有罕见形容词 chalcedonous（玉髓质的）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, this is a whole borrowed word without a useful everyday prefix-and-suffix analysis. Family: chalcedonies, a plural for varieties or specimens; chalcedonic, meaning relating to or containing chalcedony; and the rare adjective chalcedonous.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有严格对应的常用同义词。microcrystalline silica（微晶质二氧化硅）是描述性近称；agate（玛瑙）通常指有条带的玉髓；carnelian（红玉髓）指红色至橙红色的玉髓，后两者都是更具体的品种名称。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no exact everyday synonym. Microcrystalline silica is a descriptive near-equivalent; agate usually names banded chalcedony; carnelian names a red to orange-red variety. The latter two are more specific variety names.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 整词连接“细晶成玉”：晶体细到肉眼难辨，形成温润的玉髓。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link the whole word to 'tiny crystals, smooth gemstone': crystals too small to distinguish form chalcedony.

etymology_story.zh: 这是晚期中古英语复合词，由 cod 与 piece 构成；cod 在这里用的是“袋、阴囊”的古义，与“鳕鱼”无关。这个名称原指男装前部起遮盖作用的部分，后来也用于显眼的填充式装饰。
etymology_story.en: This late Middle English compound joins piece to cod in its old sense of 'bag' or 'scrotum,' unrelated to the fish name. It named a covering at the front of men's clothing and later also applied to conspicuous padded forms.

morphology_enriched.zh: cod（古义：袋、阴囊）+ piece（片、部分）构成复合名词。词形与词族：codpieces（复数）、codpieced（带有前裆盖片的，罕见形容词）；没有常用的动词或副词派生形式。
morphology_enriched.en: A compound noun: cod, an old word for a bag or scrotum, + piece. Forms and family: codpieces, the plural, and the rare adjective codpieced, meaning fitted with a codpiece. There are no common derived verbs or adverbs.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有严格对应的常用同义词。crotch flap（裆部盖片）是较宽泛的描述；genital pouch（生殖器遮袋）强调袋状结构；groin guard（护裆）强调保护功能，通常指不同的装备。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no exact everyday synonym. Crotch flap is a broader description; genital pouch emphasizes the pouch shape; groin guard emphasizes protection and usually denotes a different item.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: cod 是古义“袋”，piece 是“片”：男装前裆的一片遮盖物。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Old cod means 'bag'; piece means 'part': a covering piece at the front of men's clothing.

senses.meaning_en: A fish belonging to an ancient group of lobe-finned fishes with fossil and living members.
senses.english_definition: A coelacanth is a large lobe-finned fish belonging to a group that was known only from fossils before a living example was identified in 1938.
senses.chinese_definition: 腔棘鱼是一类大型肉鳍鱼；在1938年发现并确认活体之前，人们只通过化石认识这一类群。

etymology_story.zh: 经新拉丁语属名 Coelacanthus 而来，由源自希腊语的“中空”与“棘”两个成分构成，指最初命名所依据的化石鱼的中空鳍棘。这个名称先用于化石鱼，后来也用于同一演化类群的现生成员。
etymology_story.en: The word comes through the New Latin genus name Coelacanthus, formed from Greek elements meaning 'hollow' and 'spine,' referring to hollow fin spines in the fossil fish originally named. A name first applied to fossil fishes later also covered living members of the same evolutionary group.

morphology_enriched.zh: 学术构词可分析为 coel-（中空，来自希腊语 koilos）+ acanth（棘，来自希腊语 akantha）；现代日常使用中通常作为整体名词记忆。词族：coelacanths（复数）、coelacanthine（腔棘鱼类的，专业形容词）、coelacanthiform（腔棘鱼目的，专业形容词）。
morphology_enriched.en: The learned formation combines coel-, 'hollow,' from Greek koilos, with acanth, 'spine,' from Greek akantha; ordinary modern use treats it as a whole noun. Family: coelacanths, the plural; coelacanthine, a technical adjective meaning relating to coelacanths; and coelacanthiform, a technical adjective relating to their order.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有严格对应的常用同义词。lobe-finned fish（肉鳍鱼）是更大的类别；Latimeria（矛尾鱼属）是现生腔棘鱼所属的属，并不包括所有化石腔棘鱼；living fossil（活化石）是常用描述性称呼，并不表示它们从未发生演化。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no exact everyday synonym. Lobe-finned fish names a broader group; Latimeria is the genus containing living coelacanths and excludes other fossil members; living fossil is a common descriptive label, not a claim that these fishes have never evolved.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: coel- 中空 + acanth 棘 →“腔棘”；词形与中文名直接对应。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Coel- means 'hollow' and acanth means 'spine': remember the fish through its name, 'hollow spine.'

morphology.text: cruiser（巡洋舰） + weight（体重级别） → cruiserweight（次重量级）；借舰船级别比喻拳击级别。

etymology.text: 20世纪英语以 cruiser 的舰船等级作比喻，与 weight 合成拳击级别名称；联想排在最大舰船级别之下的巡洋舰。

usage_note: 本课采用现代拳击语境，级别位于轻重量级与重量级之间；具体限制依赛事规则。旧英式用法可指轻重量级。

etymology_story.zh: 该词在20世纪初出现，由 cruiser（巡洋舰）与 weight（体重级别）合成，以巡洋舰相对于更大型军舰的位置比喻拳击中的体重级别；英国早期用法也曾指轻重量级。[词源说明](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/cruiserweight)
etymology_story.en: The compound appeared in the early twentieth century, comparing a boxing weight class with a cruiser's position below larger warships. Earlier British usage could refer to light heavyweight. [Word history](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/cruiserweight)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：cruiser（巡洋舰）+ weight（体重级别）；cruiser 本身可分析为 cruise + -er，但合成词采用的是已形成的舰船名称。复数：cruiserweights。相关基础词族：cruise（巡航）、cruiser（巡洋舰；巡航工具）、cruising（巡航）；weigh（称重）、weight（重量）、weighted（加重的）、weighty（沉重的；重大的）。cruiserweight title 等结构通常是名词作定语，不必另立形容词词性。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: cruiser + weight. Cruiser can itself be analyzed as cruise + -er, but the compound uses the established ship name. Plural: cruiserweights. Related base families include cruise, cruiser, cruising, weigh, weight, weighted, and weighty. Uses such as cruiserweight title normally involve an attributive noun rather than a separate adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: junior heavyweight（次重量级）在拳击中可作近义名称，但不同项目或组织的界定可能不同；cruiserweight boxer（次重量级拳击手）明确指人；cruiserweight division（次重量级组别）明确指级别。light heavyweight（轻重量级）在现代拳击中通常是另一个级别。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Junior heavyweight can be an alternative boxing label, although definitions vary across sports and organizations; cruiserweight boxer explicitly denotes the person, while cruiserweight division denotes the class. Light heavyweight normally names a separate division in modern boxing.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 巡洋舰有舰船级别，拳击手有体重级别：cruiser + weight → 次重量级。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A cruiser has a place among warship classes; a cruiserweight has a place among boxing weight classes.

etymology.text: 晚期中古英语由 dis- 与 compose 组成；compose 的“使镇定”义加上反向前缀，就成了扰乱心神。

etymology_story.zh: 该词在晚期中古英语中已有使用，由表示逆转或破坏的 dis- 与 compose 构成；其意义包括打乱秩序，以及打破一个人的镇定。[词源与释义](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/discompose)
etymology_story.en: Recorded in late Middle English, discompose combines reversive dis- with compose. Its meanings include disrupting an arrangement and disrupting a person's emotional composure. [Word history and senses](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/discompose)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：dis-（逆转；破坏）+ compose（使镇定；安排）。屈折形式：discomposes、discomposed、discomposing；discomposed 也可作分词形容词，表示“心神不定的”；派生名词 discomposure 表示“慌乱；失去镇定”。核心相关词族：compose（组成；创作；使镇定）、composed（镇定的）、composure（镇定）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: dis- meaning reversal or disruption + compose. Inflections: discomposes, discomposed, and discomposing. Discomposed also functions as a participial adjective meaning unsettled; the derived noun discomposure means loss of calmness. The core related family includes compose, composed, and composure.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: disconcert（使窘迫；使不知所措）侧重意外情况打乱思路；fluster（使慌乱）侧重紧张导致的忙乱；unsettle（使不安）可指持续的心理不稳定。discompose 较正式，突出镇定或自持受到破坏。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Disconcert emphasizes being thrown off balance by something unexpected; fluster suggests nervous confusion; unsettle can describe a more lasting loss of emotional security. Discompose is more formal and specifically emphasizes disrupted composure.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: composed 是“镇定的”；加上逆转前缀 dis-，就是“使不再镇定”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Composed means calm; dis- reverses that calm: discompose means to undo composure.

Idiot ultimately comes through Latin idiota from Greek idiōtēs, whose earlier meanings included a private person or layperson before developing the sense of an ignorant or foolish person. [Regional usage and etymology](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/eejit)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中作为不可再分析的单纯词处理，不拆成 ee + jit。复数：eejits；无须补造常用动词、形容词或副词形式。idiot（傻瓜）、idiotic（愚蠢的）、idiotically（愚蠢地）、idiocy（愚蠢行为；愚蠢）属于其来源词的相关词族，并非由 eejit 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Treat eejit as a simple, synchronically unanalyzable word, not as ee + jit. Its plural is eejits; it has no established common verb, adjective, or adverb derivatives. Idiot, idiotic, idiotically, and idiocy belong to the related source-word family rather than being direct derivatives of eejit.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: idiot（笨蛋）最接近，但直接称呼他人时可能更刺耳；fool（傻瓜）常指判断不明智的人；numpty（笨蛋）是英国非正式用语，常侧重笨拙或无能。eejit 带鲜明地域色彩，常用于打趣，但仍可能冒犯。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Idiot is the closest equivalent but can sound harsher when addressed directly to someone; fool often emphasizes poor judgment; numpty is informal British English and often suggests clumsiness or incompetence. Eejit is strongly regional and often teasing, though it can still offend.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 eejit 直接连到熟词 idiot：地域口音变了，“笨蛋”的意思没变。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link eejit directly to idiot: the regional pronunciation changes, but the foolish-person meaning remains.

etymology_story.zh: 英语在18世纪从西班牙语借入 fandango，更早的词源尚无定论；它先指舞蹈及其音乐，后来也被引申用于热闹聚会或胡闹折腾。[历史来源](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/us/dictionary/english/fandango)；[词义与用例](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/fandango)
etymology_story.en: English borrowed fandango from Spanish in the eighteenth century; its earlier origin remains uncertain. From the dance and its music, usage extended to festive gatherings and foolish or elaborate activity. [Historical origin](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/us/dictionary/english/fandango); [senses and usage](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/fandango)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是整词借入的单纯词，不分析为 fan、dan 与 go。复数：fandangos。没有需要列作常用词族成员的标准派生词；fandango-like（像凡丹戈舞的）是可临时组成的比较形式。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, fandango is a borrowed simple word, not a combination of fan, dan, and go. Its plural is fandangos. It has no standard common derivatives requiring a separate word-family entry; fandango-like is a possible freely formed comparison.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: dance（舞蹈）是舞蹈义的上位词，并不特指凡丹戈；fuss（大惊小怪；折腾）接近其比喻义，侧重不必要的忙乱；rigmarole（繁琐程序）侧重冗长复杂的手续。fandango 的比喻用法更富戏谑和表演感。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Dance is a broader term for the literal sense rather than an exact synonym; fuss overlaps with the figurative sense and emphasizes unnecessary agitation; rigmarole emphasizes tedious complexity or procedure. Figurative fandango is more playful and theatrical.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 先记“一场热闹的西班牙舞”：舞蹈带出舞曲，热闹表演再联想到一番折腾。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a lively Spanish dance: it brings its music, and its bustle suggests an elaborate fuss.

senses.english_definition: A floribunda is a cultivated rose that produces many flowers in clusters.

etymology_story.zh: 该词借自新拉丁语 floribunda，是 floribundus 的阴性形式，含义为“繁花盛开的”；原本用于植物命名，后来成为一类成簇开花的栽培月季的名称。[词源与园艺义](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/floribunda)
etymology_story.en: Floribunda was borrowed from New Latin as the feminine form of floribundus, meaning flowering freely. Originally used in botanical naming, it became the name of a cultivated rose group characterized by clustered flowers. [Etymology and horticultural sense](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/floribunda)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中作为借入的完整名词使用；词源结构可识别为 flori-（花）+ -bunda（拉丁语形容词形式），但 -bunda 不是现代英语中能自由构词的后缀。复数：floribundas。相关拉丁词根词族包括 floral（花的）、florist（花商）、floriculture（花卉栽培）、floriferous（多花的），它们不是由 floribunda 直接派生。floribunda rose 通常是名词作定语。[构词来源](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/floribunda)
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English uses floribunda as a borrowed whole noun. Its learned structure is recognizable as flori- referring to flowers + -bunda, a Latin adjectival form rather than a productive modern English suffix. Plural: floribundas. Related Latin-root vocabulary includes floral, florist, floriculture, and floriferous; these are not direct derivatives of floribunda. Floribunda rose normally contains an attributive noun. [Formation](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/floribunda)

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: floribunda rose（丰花月季）是明确的同义全称；cluster-flowered rose（簇花月季）是范围更宽的描述性表达，并非严格同义词。polyantha rose（多花月季）是相关但不同的园艺类别，不能直接替换 floribunda。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Floribunda rose is an explicit equivalent; cluster-flowered rose is a broader descriptive expression rather than an exact synonym. Polyantha rose names a related but distinct horticultural group and cannot simply replace floribunda.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: flori- 联想到花，整词抓住“繁花成簇”：一枝不是一朵，而是一簇。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Let flori- cue flowers, then picture profuse clusters: several blooms together on a stem.

etymology_story.zh: 英语借自法语 gigot，通常分析为 gigue“腿”的指小形式；它与表示古代弦乐器的 gigue 之间的历史联系尚不完全确定，不宜把“小提琴形状”当作确凿词源。服装中的“羊腿袖”义来自衣袖与羊腿相似的轮廓。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed French gigot, generally analysed as a diminutive of gigue, meaning “leg”; its historical connection with gigue as the name of an old stringed instrument is not fully certain. The clothing sense refers to a sleeve whose outline resembles a leg of mutton.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是不可再按常用词缀拆分的借词：gigot；复数 gigots。常见组合有 gigot of lamb“羔羊腿”和 gigot sleeve“羊腿袖”；后者的 gigot 是名词作定语，并非独立的常用形容词。没有常用的英语派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, gigot is an unsegmented loanword; its plural is gigots. Established combinations include gigot of lamb and gigot sleeve; in the latter, gigot is a noun modifier rather than a separate common adjective. It has no established common family of English derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: leg of lamb“羔羊腿”明确指羔羊肉；leg of mutton“成年羊腿”明确指成年绵羊肉；leg-of-mutton sleeve“羊腿袖”对应服装义。gigot 在烹饪中可指前两者，通常带法式菜单或烹饪用语色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Leg of lamb specifically identifies meat from a young sheep, while leg of mutton identifies meat from an adult sheep. Leg-of-mutton sleeve matches the clothing sense; gigot can cover either meat term and often has a French culinary flavour.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“羊腿轮廓”：餐桌上是羊腿，衣服上是上宽下窄的羊腿袖。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a leg of mutton: on a plate it is the meat; on a dress it is a sleeve that is wide above and narrow below.

etymology_story.zh: 糖浆义借自法语 grenadine，与 grenade“石榴”有关，名称反映其传统原料。织物义通常追溯到法语中的同形词，并与西班牙城市 Granada 的法语名称 Grenade 联系起来，不能用“石榴糖浆”的来历解释。
etymology_story.en: The syrup sense comes from French grenadine, related to grenade, meaning “pomegranate,” and reflects its traditional ingredient. The fabric sense is generally traced to a French homonym associated with Grenade, the French name for Granada in Spain, rather than with the syrup.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常整词分析：grenadine；不能按英语 grenade“手榴弹”加后缀来理解。糖浆义和织物义通常均为不可数名词；表示不同品种时可见 grenadines。常见组合有 grenadine syrup“石榴糖浆”和 grenadine tie“网眼丝织领带”，无常用英语派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English normally treats grenadine as a whole loanword, not as English grenade plus a suffix. Both the syrup and fabric senses are usually uncountable, though grenadines can refer to varieties. Established combinations include grenadine syrup and grenadine tie; there are no common English derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: pomegranate syrup“石榴糖浆”强调石榴原料，而商业 grenadine 不一定含石榴；cordial“浓缩甜饮料”范围更广，不能精确替换。织物义可用 open-weave silk“疏松网眼丝织物”作描述，但并非所有此类丝织物都是 grenadine。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Pomegranate syrup explicitly identifies the fruit ingredient, whereas commercial grenadine need not contain pomegranate. Cordial is a broader category of concentrated sweet drinks; for the fabric sense, open-weave silk is a useful description but does not identify grenadine exclusively.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 饮料义抓“石榴红糖浆”；织物义另记“透着网眼的丝领带”，两条来源分开记。
mnemonic_anchor.en: For drinks, picture pomegranate-red syrup; for fabric, picture the open texture of a silk tie. Keep the two origins separate.

pronunciation.note: 采用词典所列读音；重音由 ˈ 标记。

forms: 植物名可作不可数集合用法；单株可说 a guar plant。
family: guar gum 瓜尔胶。

morphology.text: guar + gum → guar gum（瓜尔胶）；guar 整词作为独立词素记忆，gum 表示由它制得的胶。

etymology.text: 19世纪从印地语 guar 借入英语，是印度豆科植物的名称；从瓜尔豆到瓜尔胶连起来记。

usage_note: 本课指植物；食品标签中的 guar gum 指瓜尔胶，guar 也可简称这种胶。

etymology_story.zh: guar 借自印地语中这种豆科作物的名称。英语随后也用植物名指其种子提取的胶，因此 guar 可以指植物，也可以在相关语境中简称瓜尔胶。
etymology_story.en: Guar was borrowed from the Hindi name of the leguminous crop. English also extended the plant name to the gum extracted from its seeds, so guar can name either the plant or, in context, guar gum.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 guar 是不可再拆分的借词，没有常用派生词。guar + gum 构成 guar gum“瓜尔胶”，guar + seed 构成 guar seed“瓜尔豆种子”；这些是复合组合，不是后缀派生。作作物名称或胶的名称时通常为不可数名词，单株常说 a guar plant。
morphology_enriched.en: Guar is an unsegmented loanword in modern English and has no common derivatives. Guar + gum forms guar gum, and guar + seed forms guar seed; these are compounds rather than suffixal derivatives. As a crop or gum name it is normally uncountable; an individual specimen is usually called a guar plant.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: cluster bean“簇生豆；瓜尔豆”是植物的另一名称；guar gum“瓜尔胶”明确指种子提取物。guaran“瓜尔多糖”主要指构成瓜尔胶的多糖成分，化学指向比一般商品名称更具体。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Cluster bean is another name for the plant, while guar gum explicitly identifies the seed-derived product. Guaran refers more specifically to the polysaccharide component of guar gum and is a chemical term rather than a general crop name.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 一条链记住：瓜尔豆 → 种子 → 瓜尔胶 → 增稠。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember the chain: guar plant → seeds → guar gum → thickening.

usage_note: 本课读音采用 Collins 英式形式；常见组合有 silver halide、alkyl halide。

senses.meaning_zh: 卤化物；卤素与另一元素或基团形成的化合物
senses.meaning_en: a compound of a halogen with another element or group
senses.english_definition: A halide is a compound in which a halogen is combined with another element or a group of atoms.
senses.collocation_zh: 金属卤化物；卤代烷

senses.meaning_en: a singly charged negative ion formed from a halogen atom
senses.english_definition: A halide is also a negatively charged ion formed when a halogen atom gains one electron.
senses.collocation_zh: 卤离子；卤离子浓度
senses.sentence_en: Chloride and bromide are halide ions.

etymology_story.zh: halide 是近代化学术语，由 halogen“卤素”的词干部分与化学词尾 -ide 构成。halogen 的希腊语词源含“盐”和“生成”之意，原本强调这类元素形成盐的性质。
etymology_story.en: Halide was formed in modern chemical terminology from the stem of halogen and the chemical ending -ide. Halogen contains Greek elements meaning “salt” and “producing,” referring to the salt-forming properties of these elements.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：hal-（取自 halogen“卤素”）+ -ide（用于某些阴离子及化合物名称的化学词尾）→ halide；复数 halides。相关词族有 halogen“卤素”、halogenate“使卤化”、halogenation“卤化作用”和 halogenated“卤化的”；这些与 halide 同属术语词族，但并非都由 halide 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: hal- from halogen + -ide, a chemical ending used in names of certain anions and compounds → halide; plural halides. The related family includes halogen, halogenate, halogenation, and halogenated; these belong to the same terminology family but are not all derived directly from halide.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: halogen compound“卤素化合物”范围更广，并非全部都称为 halides；halide ion“卤离子”明确限定为离子义；halogen anion“卤素阴离子”可解释该离子义。这些名称不能与表示元素类别的 halogen“卤素”混用。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Halogen compound is broader, since not every compound containing a halogen is called a halide. Halide ion explicitly selects the ionic sense, and halogen anion describes that sense; halogen itself names the element category and is not interchangeable with halide.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: halogen 是“卤素元素”，halide 是它形成的“卤化物或卤离子”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Halogen names the element; halide names a resulting compound or negative ion.

senses.meaning_zh: 赫柏木；园艺上称为 Hebe 的一类常绿灌木，多原产于新西兰
senses.meaning_en: an evergreen shrub of the garden group known as Hebe, chiefly native to New Zealand
senses.english_definition: A hebe is an evergreen shrub, usually from New Zealand, that is grown for its leaves and clusters of flowers.
senses.collocation_zh: 开花的赫柏木；赫柏木灌木
senses.sentence_en: We planted a hebe beside the path for its evergreen leaves and purple flowers.
senses.sentence_zh: 我们在小径旁种了一株赫柏木，看中的是它的常绿叶片和紫色花朵。

etymology_story.zh: 园艺名称 hebe 来自植物属名 Hebe，属名取自希腊神话中的青春女神赫柏。女神的名字与希腊语中表示“青春、盛年”的词有关；“常绿像青春常驻”适合作为记忆联想，但不是命名动机已经证实的说明。
etymology_story.en: The garden name hebe comes from the botanical genus name Hebe, named after the Greek goddess of youth. Her name is associated with the Greek word for youth or the prime of life; linking evergreen foliage with lasting youth is a memory aid, not an established explanation of the naming decision.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代普通名词 hebe 由植物学专名 Hebe 转为普通名称，没有可拆分的常用英语词根和词缀；复数为 hebes。常见组合包括 hebe shrub“赫柏木灌木”和 dwarf hebe“矮生赫柏木”，无常用派生词族；大写 Hebe 还可指女神或植物学属名。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern common noun hebe comes from the botanical proper name Hebe and has no productive English root-and-affix breakdown; its plural is hebes. Combinations include hebe shrub and dwarf hebe, but there is no common derivative family. Capitalized Hebe can also name the goddess or the botanical genus.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: shrubby veronica“灌木状婆婆纳”是园艺中的近义名称；veronica“婆婆纳”范围更广，也包括许多草本植物；evergreen shrub“常绿灌木”只是上位描述，并不能单独确定为 hebe。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Shrubby veronica is a close horticultural alternative. Veronica is broader and also includes many herbaceous plants, while evergreen shrub is only a general category and does not identify a hebe specifically.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: Hebe 是青春女神：把 hebe 的常绿叶片联想成“青春常驻”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Hebe is the goddess of youth: connect the shrub’s evergreen leaves with staying youthful.

etymology.text: 中古英语复合词，由 horn 与古义“树木”的 beam 组成；名字形容木头硬得像角。

usage_note: 树名指鹅耳枥，也可指其木材；beam 在该词里不是“光束”。

senses.meaning_zh: 鹅耳枥；鹅耳枥属的落叶乔木，木质坚硬，叶有锯齿
senses.meaning_en: A deciduous tree of the genus Carpinus, with hard wood and toothed leaves.
senses.english_definition: A hornbeam is a tree with very hard wood and leaves with toothed edges.

senses.meaning_zh: 鹅耳枥木；取自鹅耳枥的坚硬木材
senses.meaning_en: The hard, tough wood of a hornbeam tree.
senses.english_definition: Hornbeam is the hard wood of this tree, used for objects that need to resist wear.

senses.sentence_en: The mallet head was made of hornbeam.
senses.sentence_zh: 这把木槌的槌头是用鹅耳枥木制成的。

etymology_story.zh: 这是由 horn“角”和 beam“树木”的古义构成的英语本族复合词，名称形容其木材像角一样坚硬。这里的 beam 保留了早于现代常用义“梁”的树木义。
etymology_story.en: This native English compound combines horn with beam in its old sense of “tree,” describing wood as hard as horn. Beam preserves a tree-related meaning older than its familiar modern sense of a structural timber.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：horn“角”＋beam“树木，古义”→hornbeam“鹅耳枥”。它是复合名词，beam 不是词缀；主要相关形式为复数 hornbeams，以及 hornbeam wood“鹅耳枥木”、hornbeam hedge“鹅耳枥绿篱”等名词组合，没有常用的派生动词或副词。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: horn + beam, using beam in its historical sense “tree,” → hornbeam. It is a compound noun, and beam is not an affix; related forms include the plural hornbeams and noun combinations such as hornbeam wood and hornbeam hedge, with no common derived verb or adverb.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有覆盖全部词义的精确常用同义词。ironwood“铁木”也可指鹅耳枥，但还用于多种其他硬木树；common hornbeam“欧洲鹅耳枥”专指 Carpinus betulus，范围更窄；hardwood“硬木”是更宽泛的木材类别。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no exact everyday synonym covering every use. Ironwood can name hornbeam but also several unrelated hard-wooded trees; common hornbeam specifically means Carpinus betulus; hardwood is a much broader timber category.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: horn＝角，beam＝古义“树”：木头硬得像角的树。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Horn + beam “tree”: a tree with wood as hard as horn.

etymology.text: 来自中古拉丁语 immurare，由表示“在内”的 im- 与 murus“墙”组成；想象被关在墙内。

usage_note: 正式或文学用语，常用 immure someone in a place；可比喻闭门不出。

senses.meaning_en: To confine someone within an enclosed place or isolate them from the outside world, especially in formal or literary use.

etymology_story.zh: 该词最终源自拉丁语 immurare“用墙围住”，由 in-“在……内”和 murus“墙”构成，前缀在 m 前同化为 im-。它从“围在墙内”发展出“禁闭、隔绝”的字面义及比喻义。
etymology_story.en: The word ultimately comes from Latin immurare, “to enclose within walls,” formed from in- “in” and murus “wall,” with in- assimilating to im- before m. Physical enclosure developed into literal and figurative senses of confinement and isolation.

morphology_enriched.zh: 历史词根辅助分析：im-“在内”＋mur“墙”＋英语动词结尾 -e；现代英语中宜把 immure 作为整体动词掌握，不能把它拆成 im-＋独立英语单词 mure 来推导常用义。主要词族：immures“禁闭，第三人称单数”、immured“被禁闭的；过去式及过去分词”、immuring“正在禁闭；现在分词”、immurement“禁闭；围禁”，其中名词较少见。
morphology_enriched.en: Historical root analysis: im- “in” + mur “wall” + the English verbal ending -e. In modern English, learn immure as a whole verb rather than relying on mure as a familiar independent base. Principal family members are immures, immured, immuring, and the less common noun immurement, meaning confinement or enclosure.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: confine“限制、禁闭”适用范围最广；imprison“监禁”通常强调囚禁或剥夺自由；seclude“使隐居、隔离”强调远离他人，未必出于强迫。immure 更突出被封闭空间困住的感觉，语体较文学化。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Confine broadly means to restrict or keep within limits; imprison emphasizes captivity or loss of liberty; seclude emphasizes separation from other people and need not imply force. Immure particularly evokes enclosure and has a literary tone.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: mur＝墙：关到墙里面，就是 immure“禁闭”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Mur means “wall”: put someone inside the walls → immure.

etymology.text: 19世纪从波兰语借入，与波兰 Mazur／Mazovia 地区名称相关；从波兰舞蹈联想到三拍子的舞曲。

usage_note: 既指波兰舞蹈，也指相应舞曲；本课主句教舞曲义。

etymology_story.zh: 该词于19世纪进入英语，其名称最终与波兰语 mazurek 及 Mazur“马佐夫舍地区居民”有关。它先指波兰舞蹈，也用于这种舞蹈的伴奏音乐及由其节奏发展出的独立器乐作品。
etymology_story.en: The word entered English in the nineteenth century, with its name ultimately related to Polish mazurek and Mazur, an inhabitant of Mazovia. It names both the Polish dance and its music, including independent instrumental compositions developed from the dance rhythm.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 mazurka 是整体借入的名词，不宜拆成英语词根和词缀，-ka 也不是这里可自由使用的英语后缀。主要相关形式：mazurkas“玛祖卡舞／舞曲，复数”、mazurka-like“像玛祖卡舞／舞曲的”，以及 mazurka rhythm“玛祖卡节奏”等组合；没有常用的独立派生动词或副词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, mazurka is a borrowed noun treated as a whole; it has no productive English root-and-affix breakdown, and -ka is not a freely usable English suffix here. Related forms include the plural mazurkas, the transparent adjective mazurka-like, and combinations such as mazurka rhythm; there is no common independently derived verb or adverb.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有完全等义的常用替换词。Polish dance“波兰舞蹈”是上位概念；waltz“华尔兹”也通常是三拍子，但节奏重心和舞步不同；polonaise“波洛奈兹舞／波兰舞曲”也是波兰三拍子舞蹈或乐曲，但通常更庄重，具有行进感。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no exact common substitute. Polish dance is a broader category; a waltz is also usually in triple time but has different rhythmic emphasis and steps; a polonaise is another Polish dance or composition in triple time, typically more stately and processional.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 马佐夫舍的舞名：记住“波兰＋三拍子＋第二或第三拍重音”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A dance name linked to Mazovia: Poland + triple time + a second- or third-beat accent.

meaning: 旧人类分类中所谓“尼格罗人种的”（过时且具冒犯性）

pronunciation.note: 采用词典所列读音；重音由 ˈ 标记。

forms: 形容词不变形；历史文献中常以大写 N 开头。
family: Negroidal 同类过时分类形容词；仅供识读。

morphology.text: Negro（旧称） + -oid（像……的） → Negroid（旧人种分类词）；该构词反映历史用语。

etymology.text: 19世纪由旧称 Negro 与源自希腊语的 -oid“像……的”构成；这是旧分类留下的词，不代表现代科学认可这种人种划分。

usage_note: 通常写 Negroid；只用于批判性识读和引用历史材料。该词已不用于科学分类，且可能冒犯，不用来描述现实中的人。

senses.collocation_zh: 名词“Negroid”；被划为所谓“Negroids”的人

senses.sentence_zh: 作者仅在讨论过时的人种分类时引用名词“Negroid”。

etymology_story.zh: 该词形成于19世纪，由旧称 Negro 与源自希腊语、表示“像……的”的 -oid 构成；Negro 经西班牙语或葡萄牙语追溯至拉丁语 niger“黑的”。它被用于现已废弃的人种类型学，其历史用法不代表现代科学认可这种分类。
etymology_story.en: The word was formed in the nineteenth century from Negro and the Greek-derived suffix -oid, “resembling”; Negro traces through Spanish or Portuguese to Latin niger, “black.” It belonged to now-discredited racial typologies, and its historical use does not validate those classifications.

morphology_enriched.zh: 历史构词公式：Negro“旧时种族称谓”＋-oid“像……的”→Negroid，连接时合并相邻的 o。主要形式为形容词及由形容词转用的名词 Negroid、名词复数 Negroids；相关历史词形 Negroidal 罕见且同样过时、具冒犯性，不宜作为现代中性词汇使用。
morphology_enriched.en: Historical formation: Negro, an old racial designation, + -oid “resembling” → Negroid, with the adjacent o vowels merged. Principal forms are the adjective and converted noun Negroid and the plural noun Negroids; the related historical adjective Negroidal is rare and likewise outdated and offensive.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有可直接替换的现代中性同义词。Negro 是相关的旧称，作为当代人物称谓通常不合适；Black“黑人／黑人的”是当代身份用语，不能等同于旧分类；sub-Saharan African“撒哈拉以南非洲人／该地区的”表示地理关联，也不与该旧标签一一对应。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no directly equivalent neutral modern synonym. Negro is a related outdated designation generally unsuitable for referring to people today; Black is a contemporary identity term, not an equivalent of the obsolete category; sub-Saharan African indicates geographical association and does not map directly onto the old label.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 旧称＋-oid“像……的”：识别历史分类标签，同时记住“过时、具冒犯性”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: An old label + -oid “resembling”: recognize the historical classification and remember “outdated and offensive.”

etymology.text: 20世纪英语生化术语，把核相关的 nucleo-、糖名成分 -ose 与化合物词尾 -ide 组合；联想碱基和糖相连的结构。

usage_note: 生化术语；与 nucleotide 相差的关键是磷酸基团。

etymology_story.zh: 该词是20世纪初形成的生物化学术语，由表示细胞核或核酸关联的 nucleo- 与糖苷命名成分 -oside 构成。名称反映了核苷既与核酸有关，又具有碱基与糖结合的结构。
etymology_story.en: This biochemical term arose in the early twentieth century from nucleo-, referring to nuclei or nucleic acids, and -oside, associated with glycoside naming. The name reflects both its connection with nucleic acids and its structure as a base joined to a sugar.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词可理解为 nucleo-“核；核酸相关”＋-oside“糖苷命名成分”，连接处合并 o，形成 nucleoside；不宜机械拆成三个彼此独立的现代英语词缀 nucleo-＋-ose＋-ide。主要词族及复合形式：nucleosides“核苷，复数”、ribonucleoside“核糖核苷”、deoxyribonucleoside“脱氧核糖核苷”、nucleosidase“核苷酶”、nucleoside analogue“核苷类似物”；nucleotide“核苷酸”是相关但不同的术语。
morphology_enriched.en: Analyze the formation as nucleo- “nuclear; related to nucleic acids” + -oside, a glycoside-related naming element, with the adjacent o vowels merged. Avoid treating it mechanically as three independent modern English affixes, nucleo- + -ose + -ide. Principal family members and compounds include nucleosides, ribonucleoside, deoxyribonucleoside, nucleosidase, and nucleoside analogue; nucleotide is a related but distinct term.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有通用的精确同义词。glycoside“糖苷”是相关的更宽泛结构术语；nucleotide“核苷酸”比相应核苷多一个或多个磷酸基团；nucleobase“核碱基”仅指碱基部分，不包括糖。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no general exact synonym. Glycoside is a related, broader structural term; a nucleotide has one or more phosphate groups in addition to the corresponding nucleoside structure; a nucleobase is only the base component, without the sugar.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 碱基＋糖＝核苷；再接磷酸基团＝核苷酸。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Base + sugar = nucleoside; add phosphate group(s) = nucleotide.

etymology_story.zh: 英语在18世纪借入马来语 pengguling，意思与“滚动、蜷卷者”有关，源自动词 guling“滚动”。这个名字描绘了穿山甲遇险时蜷成球的行为。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed the word in the eighteenth century from Malay pengguling, referring to something that rolls or curls up, from guling, meaning 'to roll'. The name describes the animal's habit of curling into a ball when threatened.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 pangolin 是不可再按英语词根、词缀拆分的借入名词。相关形式：pangolins（复数）；pangolin-like（像穿山甲的，透明的临时复合形式）；没有常用的派生动词或副词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, pangolin is a borrowed noun with no productive English root-and-affix breakdown. Related forms are pangolins, the plural, and pangolin-like, a transparent descriptive compound; there are no common derived verbs or adverbs.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: scaly anteater（有鳞食蚁兽）是穿山甲的另一名称；anteater（食蚁兽）通常指另一类哺乳动物，不能作为准确同义词。pangolin 是最明确、最常用的名称。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Scaly anteater is an alternative name for a pangolin. Anteater normally refers to a different group of mammals and is not an exact synonym; pangolin is the clearest standard term.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 名字里的历史线索是“滚”：披鳞的小兽遇险蜷成球。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember the historical idea of rolling: a scaly mammal rolls itself into a protective ball.

pronunciation.note: 采用词典所列读音；重音由 ˈ 标记。

forms: 此义通常不可数。
family: perspicuous 清晰易懂的；perspicuously 清晰地。

morphology.text: perspicuous（去 -ous） + -ity → perspicuity（明晰）；词尾变为 -uity。

etymology.text: 来自拉丁语 perspicuitas，与 perspicuus“透明、清楚”相关；把“看得透”联想到文章让人一看就明白。

usage_note: 正式、较少见；一般交流常用 clarity。本课教表达清晰义。

senses.meaning_zh: 表达的明晰；清楚易懂
senses.meaning_en: clarity and ease of understanding, especially in speech or writing
senses.english_definition: Perspicuity is the quality of expressing ideas so clearly that people can easily understand them.
senses.collocation_en: perspicuity of expression; clarity and perspicuity
senses.collocation_zh: 表达的明晰；清楚明白
senses.sentence_en: The perspicuity of her explanation made a difficult argument easy to follow.
senses.sentence_zh: 她的解释清晰明白，使一个复杂的论证变得容易理解。

etymology_story.zh: 该词源自拉丁语 perspicuitas“明晰”，与 perspicuus“透明的、清楚的”及 perspicere“看透、看清”有关。由视觉上的“看得透”，发展出语言和思想“容易理解”的含义。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Latin perspicuitas, meaning 'clearness', related to perspicuus, 'transparent or clear', and perspicere, 'to see through or see clearly'. Visual transparency became a way of describing language and ideas that are easy to understand.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代词族关系：perspicuous（清晰易懂的）→ perspicuity（明晰），可理解为以名词词尾 -ity 替换形容词词尾 -ous，并伴随词干形式变化。词族还包括 perspicuously（清晰地）和 perspicuousness（明晰，较少用）；perspicacity（敏锐洞察力）是同源相关词，但含义不同。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern family links perspicuous, 'clear and understandable', with perspicuity, formed through replacement of adjectival -ous by nominal -ity with a stem adjustment. Other derivatives are perspicuously and the less common perspicuousness; perspicacity is historically related but means perceptiveness.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: clarity（清晰）最通用；lucidity（明晰）强调思想或解释条理清楚；intelligibility（可理解性）强调能否被理解。perspicuity 较正式，尤其强调表达清楚易懂。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Clarity is the broad everyday term; lucidity emphasizes clear, orderly thought or explanation; intelligibility emphasizes whether something can be understood. Perspicuity is formal and especially concerns clear expression.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: “看得透”→“读得懂”：表达透明，就是 perspicuity。
mnemonic_anchor.en: See through it, then understand it: transparent expression gives perspicuity.

etymology.text: 名称关联希腊神话中的 Phaethon，英语从拉丁语人名及法语车名获得这一用法；联想神话人物驾车的画面。

usage_note: 历史交通工具名；另可用于早期敞篷汽车，本课选马车义。

senses.meaning_zh: 轻型敞篷四轮马车
senses.meaning_en: a light, open, four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage
senses.english_definition: A phaeton is a light carriage with four wheels and an open body that is pulled by one or more horses.
senses.collocation_en: a horse-drawn phaeton; a high-perch phaeton
senses.collocation_zh: 马拉的轻型敞篷四轮车；高座轻型敞篷四轮马车
senses.sentence_en: They drove through the estate in a phaeton drawn by two horses.
senses.sentence_zh: 他们乘坐一辆由两匹马拉着的轻型敞篷四轮马车穿过庄园。

senses.meaning_zh: 早期的敞篷旅游汽车
senses.meaning_en: an early type of open touring car
senses.english_definition: A phaeton is an early type of open car, usually with more than one row of seats and without permanent side windows.
senses.collocation_en: a four-door phaeton; a vintage phaeton
senses.collocation_zh: 四门敞篷旅游汽车；老式敞篷旅游汽车
senses.sentence_en: The museum displayed a beautifully restored phaeton from the 1920s.
senses.sentence_zh: 博物馆展出了一辆修复精美的20世纪20年代敞篷旅游汽车。

etymology_story.zh: 该词经法语 phaéton 进入英语，名称来自希腊神话中驾驭太阳车的法厄同 Phaethon。它先用于轻型马车，后来沿用于早期敞篷汽车。
etymology_story.en: The word entered English through French phaéton, named after Phaethon, the figure in Greek mythology who drove the sun's chariot. It first named a light carriage and was later applied to an early open automobile.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 phaeton 是整体借入的名词，不宜拆成英语词根与词缀。相关形式包括 phaetons（复数）和 phaeton-bodied（采用此类敞篷车身的复合形容词）；Phaethon 是与其历史来源有关的专名，并非现代派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, phaeton is a borrowed noun without a productive English root-and-affix analysis. Related forms include the plural phaetons and the compound adjective phaeton-bodied; Phaethon is the historical source name, not a modern derivative.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: carriage（马车）是上位词；buggy（轻便马车）通常较小，常为两人乘坐，与 phaeton 并非完全相同；touring car（旅游汽车）与其汽车义接近，但涵盖范围更广。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Carriage is the broader horse-drawn category; buggy usually suggests a smaller carriage, often seating two, and is not an exact equivalent; touring car overlaps with the automobile sense but covers a broader category.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 神话里的太阳车→现实中的敞篷车：先是马车，后来是汽车。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture the sun's chariot becoming an open vehicle: first a carriage, later a car.

meaning: 撞车；车辆或飞机的碰撞事故

pronunciation.note: 采用词典所列读音；重音由 ˈ 标记。

forms: 名词复数 prangs；动词另有 pranged、pranging。
family: prang 也可作动词，指撞坏车辆。

morphology.text: prang + -prone → prang-prone（容易发生碰撞事故的）；prang 整词作为独立词素记忆。

etymology.text: 20世纪在英语俚语中出现，常被解释为模仿碰撞声的词；可用突然“砰”地撞上的声音助记，较早来源没有定论。

usage_note: 主要为英式、澳式非正式用语；可作可数名词，也可作动词。

senses.meaning_zh: 撞车事故；飞机碰撞事故〔英式非正式〕
senses.meaning_en: a vehicle crash, especially a car or aircraft accident, in informal British English
senses.english_definition: A prang is an accident in which a vehicle crashes into something, especially a relatively minor car accident.
senses.collocation_en: a minor prang; have a prang
senses.collocation_zh: 轻微撞车事故；发生撞车事故
senses.sentence_en: I had a minor prang in the car park, but nobody was hurt.
senses.sentence_zh: 我在停车场发生了一起轻微的撞车事故，不过没有人受伤。

senses.meaning_zh: 撞坏车辆；使车辆发生碰撞〔英式非正式〕
senses.meaning_en: to crash a vehicle or damage it in a collision, in informal British English
senses.english_definition: If you prang a vehicle, you crash it or damage it by hitting something.
senses.collocation_en: prang a car; prang an aircraft
senses.collocation_zh: 撞坏汽车；使飞机发生碰撞
senses.sentence_en: He pranged his car while reversing out of the garage.
senses.sentence_zh: 他从车库倒车出来时把汽车撞坏了。

etymology_story.zh: 该词在第二次世界大战期间的英国皇家空军俚语中流行，起初常指飞机坠毁或撞坏，后来也用于汽车事故。它的更早来源尚不确定，可能模仿碰撞的声音。
etymology_story.en: The word became established in British Royal Air Force slang during the Second World War, initially referring especially to aircraft crashes or damage, and later to car accidents. Its earlier origin is uncertain, though it may imitate the sound of a collision.

morphology_enriched.zh: prang 是现代英语中的单纯词，名词与动词形式相同。屈折形式：prangs（名词复数、动词第三人称单数）、pranged（过去式和过去分词）、pranging（现在分词）；prang-prone（容易撞车的）可作为临时复合形容词。
morphology_enriched.en: Prang is a simple modern English base used as both a noun and a verb. Its inflected forms are prangs, the plural noun or third-person singular verb, pranged, the past tense and past participle, and pranging, the present participle; prang-prone is a possible descriptive compound.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: crash（碰撞；撞毁）适用范围最广，也可指严重事故；collision（碰撞）较中性、正式，强调相撞事件；smash（猛撞；撞毁）通常暗示更猛烈的撞击。prang 带英式口语色彩，谈汽车时常指较轻的碰撞。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Crash is broad and can describe a serious accident; collision is more neutral and formal, emphasizing the impact itself; smash usually suggests a more violent impact. Prang is informal and British, and often suggests a relatively minor accident when used of cars.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 prang 想成一声“砰”：名词是这一撞，动词是撞上或撞坏。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Imagine prang as the sound of an impact: the noun names the crash, and the verb means to cause one.

pronunciation.note: 采用词典所列读音；重音由 ˈ 标记。

family: propene 丙烯（同义名称）；polypropylene 聚丙烯。

morphology.text: propyl（丙基） + -ene（烯类词尾） → propylene（丙烯）；这是沿用的化学名称。

etymology.text: 19世纪英语由 propyl 与 -ene 组合而来；-ene 常见于烯烃名称中，可与塑料原料联系记忆。

usage_note: 与 propene 指同一物质；不要与 polymer polypropylene 混淆。

senses.meaning_zh: 丙烯，化学式为 C₃H₆
senses.meaning_en: a flammable gaseous alkene, C₃H₆, used to manufacture plastics and other chemicals
senses.english_definition: Propylene is a colourless, flammable gas that is used to make plastics and other chemicals.
senses.collocation_zh: 丙烯生产；丙烯聚合
senses.sentence_en: The plant uses propylene to manufacture polypropylene.
senses.sentence_zh: 这家工厂用丙烯生产聚丙烯。

etymology_story.zh: 该词在19世纪由 propyl“丙基”与化学名称词尾 -ene 组合形成；propyl 的名称又与 propionic acid“丙酸”有关。propylene 沿用至今，同一化合物也称 propene。
etymology_story.en: The word was formed in the nineteenth century from propyl and the chemical ending -ene; propyl itself is connected with the name propionic acid. Propylene remains in use alongside propene as a name for the same compound.

morphology_enriched.zh: 名称构成：propyl（丙基）+ -ene（烯类名称词尾）→ propylene（丙烯），这是传统化学名称，不能据此把它理解为丙基与另一物质的组合。相关形式：propene（同义名称）、polypropylene（poly- + propylene，聚丙烯）；相关复合术语包括 propylene oxide（环氧丙烷）和 propylene glycol（丙二醇）。
morphology_enriched.en: The name combines propyl with the chemical ending -ene to form propylene; this is a traditional naming construction, not a description of propyl combined with another substance. Related forms include the equivalent name propene and polypropylene, formed with poly-; associated compound terms include propylene oxide and propylene glycol.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: propene（丙烯）是系统命名形式，与 propylene 指同一化合物；methylethylene（甲基乙烯）是较旧的同义名称，突出其乙烯骨架上的甲基。工业语境常用 propylene，系统化学命名中常用 propene。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Propene is the systematic name for the same compound; methylethylene is an older equivalent name that describes a methyl group attached to an ethylene framework. Propylene is common in industrial usage, while propene is usual in systematic chemical naming.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: prop- 联想三个碳，-ene 联想碳碳双键：三个碳的烯烃就是丙烯。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect prop- with three carbons and -ene with a carbon–carbon double bond: a three-carbon alkene is propylene.

senses.meaning_zh: 玫瑰（Rosa rugosa）；由该种培育的园艺月季
senses.meaning_en: A rose of the species Rosa rugosa or a garden rose derived from it.
senses.english_definition: A rugosa is a hardy shrub rose with wrinkled leaves, or a garden variety developed from this rose.
senses.collocation_zh: 玫瑰；玫瑰杂交品种
senses.sentence_en: We planted rugosas along the boundary to form a flowering hedge.
senses.sentence_zh: 我们沿地界种了玫瑰，形成一道开花的绿篱。

etymology_story.zh: 来自植物学名 Rosa rugosa 中的拉丁语种加词 rugosa，意为“多皱的”，指其表面明显起皱的叶片。英语后来用这个种加词单独指称该植物及其园艺后代。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from rugosa, the Latin specific epithet in Rosa rugosa, meaning “wrinkled” and referring to its distinctly textured leaves. English adopted the epithet as a noun for the species and garden roses descended from it.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 rugosa 是整体借入的名词，不宜拆成英语词根和词缀；复数为 rugosas。常见组合为 rugosa rose（玫瑰）和 rugosa hybrid（玫瑰杂交品种）；rugose（多皱的）及 rugosity（皱褶；多皱性）属于同源词，并非由英语 rugosa 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, rugosa is a borrowed noun treated as a single base; its plural is rugosas. Common combinations include rugosa rose and rugosa hybrid; rugose and rugosity are etymologically related words, rather than direct English derivatives of rugosa.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: rugosa rose（玫瑰）是更完整、明确的常用名称；Japanese rose（日本玫瑰）和 beach rose（海滨玫瑰）也是该物种的俗名，但地域用法可能不同，且不能准确涵盖所有园艺杂交后代。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Rugosa rose is the fuller, more explicit everyday name. Japanese rose and beach rose are alternative common names for the species, but regional usage varies, and these names do not precisely cover every garden hybrid.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 拉丁语“多皱的” → 叶片有明显皱纹的玫瑰。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Latin “wrinkled” → the rose with conspicuously wrinkled leaves.

usage_note: 专指《古兰经》的一章；通名一般小写，作为具体章标题一部分时按标题写法处理。

senses.meaning_zh: 《古兰经》的一章
senses.meaning_en: A chapter of the Quran.
senses.english_definition: A sura is one of the chapters into which the Quran is divided.
senses.collocation_en: the opening sura; recite a sura
senses.collocation_zh: 开篇章；诵读《古兰经》的一章
senses.sentence_en: The teacher explained the meaning of the opening sura.
senses.sentence_zh: 老师讲解了《古兰经》开篇章的含义。

etymology_story.zh: 借自阿拉伯语 sūra，指《古兰经》的一章；surah 是另一种英语拼写。这个词进入英语后保留了其宗教文本中的专门含义。
etymology_story.en: Sura was borrowed from Arabic sūra, meaning a chapter of the Quran; surah is an alternative English spelling. In English, the word has retained this specialized religious meaning.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 sura 是不可进一步拆分的借入词，复数为 suras；异体拼写 surah 的复数为 surahs。它没有常用的英语派生词族；sura-like（像《古兰经》章篇的）只能视为按语境临时组成的形式。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, sura is an unanalyzed borrowing, with the plural suras; the alternative spelling surah has the plural surahs. It has no established common English derivative family; sura-like is a possible contextual formation rather than a standard derivative.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: surah（《古兰经》的一章）与 sura 完全同义，只是拼写不同；chapter（章）是通用词，只有在《古兰经》的语境中才能替换；ayah（阿亚；节）指章内的一节，不是同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Surah is an exact spelling variant. Chapter is a general equivalent only when the Quran is the understood context; ayah means a verse within a chapter and is not a synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 sura 直接对应到《古兰经》的“章”，再与章内的 ayah“节”区分。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor sura to a Quranic chapter, then distinguish it from an ayah, a verse within that chapter.

meaning: 呼格的；用于直接称呼的

pronunciation.note: 采用词典所列读音；重音由 ˈ 标记。

forms: 形容词不变形；另可作名词，复数 vocatives。
family: vocatively 用呼格地；vocation 职业，历史同源。

morphology.text: vocat-（拉丁语“呼唤”的词干） + -ive（形容词尾） → vocative（用于呼唤的；呼格的）。

etymology.text: 来自拉丁语 vocativus casus“呼唤的格”，与 vocare“呼叫”相关；想到直接叫出对方名字。

usage_note: 语法术语，可作形容词或名词；英语称呼语通常靠语序、语调和标点体现。

senses.meaning_zh: 呼格的；用于直接称呼的
senses.meaning_en: Relating to a grammatical case or expression used in direct address.
senses.english_definition: A vocative form or expression is used when you speak directly to someone and call them by a name or title.
senses.collocation_en: the vocative case; a vocative expression
senses.collocation_zh: 呼格；称呼语
senses.sentence_en: In some languages, a name takes a special vocative form when you address its owner.
senses.sentence_zh: 在某些语言中，直接称呼一个人时，其姓名要使用专门的呼格形式。

senses.meaning_zh: 呼格；呼格形式；称呼语
senses.meaning_en: The case used for direct address, or a word or phrase used to address someone.
senses.english_definition: A vocative is a word or phrase used to address someone directly, and the vocative is the grammatical case used for this purpose in some languages.
senses.collocation_en: use a vocative; a noun in the vocative
senses.collocation_zh: 使用称呼语；处于呼格的名词
senses.sentence_en: In the sentence “Anna, please sit down,” “Anna” is a vocative.
senses.sentence_zh: 在“安娜，请坐下”这句话中，“安娜”是称呼语。

etymology_story.zh: 源自拉丁语 vocativus，与 vocare“呼叫；召唤”有关；拉丁语语法用 casus vocativus 表示直接称呼时使用的“格”。英语沿用其语法意义，并可用作名词，表示呼格或称呼语。
etymology_story.en: Vocative comes from Latin vocativus, related to vocare, “to call”; Latin grammarians used casus vocativus for the case of direct address. English retained the grammatical meaning and also uses the word as a noun for the case or an expression of address.

morphology_enriched.zh: 可作学习性分析：vocat-（呼叫，黏着词干）＋ -ive（形容词后缀）→ vocative；不过全词在历史上是借入形式。直接词族包括 vocative（形容词、名词）、vocatives（名词复数）和 vocatively（以呼格形式；作为称呼语）；vocation（职业；使命）、invoke（援引；祈求）及 evoke（唤起）与它同源，但不是它的直接派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: A useful learning analysis is vocat- (“call,” a bound stem) + -ive → vocative, although the word was historically borrowed as a whole. Its direct family includes the adjective and noun vocative, plural vocatives, and adverb vocatively; vocation, invoke, and evoke share its historical root but are not direct derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: term of address（称呼语）强调称呼所用的词；form of address（称谓形式）常强调姓名、头衔或礼貌等级的选择；direct address（直接称呼）强调语言功能，而 vocative 还可专指某些语言中的语法格。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Term of address emphasizes the expression used to name the addressee; form of address often concerns the choice of name, title, or level of politeness. Direct address describes the function, whereas vocative can also identify a specific grammatical case.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: vocat-＝“呼叫”：直接叫对方的名字，就是呼格的核心用途。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Vocat- means “call”: calling someone by name captures the central function of the vocative.

pronunciation.note: 采用词典所列读音；重音由 ˈ 标记。

forms: 通常不可数。
family: albinistic 白化的；albino 白化个体（用作人的称谓时宜谨慎）。

morphology.text: albin(o)（白化个体，去 o） + -ism（状态） → albinism（白化状态）。

etymology.text: 19世纪英语由 albino 与 -ism 构成；albino 的更早词根关联拉丁语 albus“白”，从色素减少的表现联系记。

usage_note: 描述人时优先用 person with albinism；不是所有白色动物都有白化现象。

senses.meaning_zh: 白化病；白化现象
senses.meaning_en: An inherited condition involving reduced or absent normal pigmentation.
senses.english_definition: Albinism is an inherited condition in which a person or animal produces little or none of the usual pigment in some tissues, and in people it affects the eyes and often the skin and hair.
senses.collocation_en: a person with albinism; oculocutaneous albinism
senses.collocation_zh: 白化病患者；眼皮肤白化病
senses.sentence_en: People with albinism often need protection from the sun and support for vision problems.
senses.sentence_zh: 白化病患者往往需要注意防晒，并获得针对视力问题的支持。

etymology_story.zh: 由 albino 加表示状态的后缀 -ism 构成；albino 经葡萄牙语传入英语，最终与拉丁语 albus“白色的”有关。这个名称从外观上的色素浅淡发展为描述一组遗传性色素生成异常的术语。
etymology_story.en: Albinism was formed from albino and the condition-forming suffix -ism; albino entered English through Portuguese and ultimately relates to Latin albus, “white.” A name based on pale appearance became a term for a group of inherited conditions affecting pigment production.

morphology_enriched.zh: albino（白化个体，去掉词尾 -o）＋ -ism（状态）→ albinism。主要词族包括 albino（白化的人或动物；白化的）、albinos（复数）、albinism（白化病）、albinistic（白化的）及 albinotic（白化的，较专业）；描述人时，person with albinism（白化病患者）通常更合适。
morphology_enriched.en: Albino, with its final -o removed, + -ism (“condition”) → albinism. The principal family includes albino, plural albinos, albinism, albinistic, and the more technical albinotic; when referring to a person, person with albinism is generally preferable.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有完全对应的日常同义词。hypopigmentation（色素减退）是范围更广的描述，不一定由遗传因素引起；depigmentation（脱色；色素丧失）强调色素缺失或减少；leucism（白变）是相关但不同的色素异常，不能与 albinism 互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no exact everyday synonym. Hypopigmentation is a broader description of reduced pigmentation and need not be inherited; depigmentation emphasizes pigment loss or absence. Leucism is a related but distinct pigmentation abnormality and is not interchangeable with albinism.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: alb- 联想到“白”，-ism 表“状态”：记住色素生成减少这一核心。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect alb- with “white” and -ism with “condition”: the central idea is reduced pigment production.

pronunciation.note: 采用词典所列读音；重音由 ˈ 标记。

forms: 物质名通常不可数。
family: albumin 白蛋白（注意与蛋清整体区分）。

morphology.text: alb-（白，拉丁语词干，以 u 连接） + -men（拉丁语名词尾） → albumen（卵白）；现代英语中整词记忆。

etymology.text: 来自拉丁语 albumen“蛋清”，与 albus“白”相关；打蛋时透明、加热后变白的部分便是记忆线索。

usage_note: 较正式或生物学用语，日常烹饪常说 egg white；albumin 通常指白蛋白类蛋白质。

senses.meaning_zh: 蛋清；卵白
senses.meaning_en: The clear substance surrounding the yolk of an egg.
senses.english_definition: Albumen is the clear part inside an egg that surrounds the yolk and usually turns white when cooked.
senses.collocation_zh: 蛋清；浓蛋清
senses.sentence_en: The albumen turned white as the egg cooked.
senses.sentence_zh: 随着鸡蛋煮熟，蛋清变成了白色。

senses.meaning_zh: 胚乳（植物学术语）
senses.meaning_en: Nutritive tissue in a seed, especially the endosperm.
senses.english_definition: In botanical writing, albumen is food-storing tissue in a seed that nourishes the developing embryo.
senses.collocation_zh: 种子胚乳；胚乳中的营养储备
senses.sentence_en: The embryo draws on the albumen reserves during germination.
senses.sentence_zh: 萌发过程中，胚利用胚乳中的营养储备。

etymology_story.zh: 直接来自拉丁语 albumen“蛋清”，与 albus“白色的”有关，名称对应蛋清受热后呈白色的特点。植物学后来也用它指种子中为胚提供营养的组织。
etymology_story.en: Albumen comes directly from Latin albumen, “egg white,” related to albus, “white,” reflecting the substance’s white appearance when cooked. Botanical usage later extended the term to nutritive tissue surrounding the embryo in a seed.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 albumen 是整体借入词，不宜把 -men 当作可自由使用的英语后缀。相关词族包括 albumen、albumenize／albumenise（用蛋清处理或涂覆）和 albumenization／albumenisation（蛋清处理）；植物学中有 albuminous（具胚乳的）与 exalbuminous（无胚乳的）。albumin（白蛋白）是历史相关但意义不同的词，不能与 albumen 混用。
morphology_enriched.en: Albumen is a whole-word borrowing in modern English; -men is not a freely usable English suffix. Related forms include albumenize/albumenise and albumenization/albumenisation; botanical vocabulary includes albuminous and exalbuminous. Albumin is historically related but denotes a protein category and must not be confused with albumen.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: egg white（蛋清）是日常生活和烹饪中的常用说法；white（蛋清）是在鸡蛋语境中的简略表达；endosperm（胚乳）对应植物学义。albumin（白蛋白）是蛋白质名称，不是“蛋清”的准确同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Egg white is the usual everyday and culinary equivalent; white is a shortened form when an egg is already understood. Endosperm corresponds to the botanical sense. Albumin names a category of proteins and is not an exact synonym for egg white.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: alb-＝“白”：想到加热后变白的蛋清；再把植物学义联系到种子中的营养组织。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Alb- means “white”: picture egg white becoming white when heated, then connect the botanical sense with a seed’s food-storing tissue.

forms: 可数名词；复数 boudins。

morphology.text: boudin + noir（法语：黑） → boudin noir（法式血肠）；boudin 整词作为独立词素记忆。

usage_note: 法语借词，读音可保留法语鼻元音；noir 指血肠，blanc 指白肠；不同地区配方可能不同。

etymology_story.zh: 英语从法语借入 boudin，保留了其“香肠”的含义；法语词的更早来源尚不确定。在路易斯安那的法语饮食传统中，这个名称又用于当地常见的猪肉米饭香肠。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed boudin from French with the meaning 'sausage'; the French word's earlier origin is uncertain. In Louisiana's French culinary tradition, the name also came to denote the local pork-and-rice sausage.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中，boudin 是整体借入的词，不能可靠地拆成英语词根和词缀。通常作物质名词，也可按种类或数量使用复数 boudins；相关组合有 boudin noir（血肠）、boudin blanc（白肠）、boudin balls（香肠馅炸丸），没有常用的英语派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, boudin is an unanalyzed borrowing, with no productive English root-and-affix breakdown. It is usually a mass noun, though boudins can refer to varieties or individual sausages; related expressions include boudin noir, boudin blanc, and boudin balls, rather than a productive English derivational family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: sausage（香肠）是上位词；blood sausage（血肠）仅对应含血的品种；black pudding（英式血肠）通常指英国或爱尔兰传统血肠，不能泛指白肠或路易斯安那式猪肉米饭香肠。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Sausage is the broader category; blood sausage covers only blood-containing varieties; black pudding usually denotes a British or Irish blood sausage and does not cover white boudin or Louisiana pork-and-rice boudin.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 boudin 整词系在“法语香肠”上：法国看黑白，路易斯安那想猪肉加米饭。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor the whole word to 'French sausage': black or white in France, pork and rice in Louisiana.

meaning: 阉伶（历史上经阉割保留高音的男歌手）

pronunciation.note: 采用词典所列读音；重音由 ˈ 标记。

forms: 可数名词；复数 castrati，也见 castratos。
family: castrati 复数形式；castrate 阉割（同源动词）。

morphology.text: castrat-（拉丁语“阉割”的词干） + -o（意大利语阳性形式） → castrato（阉伶）；英语中整体借入。

etymology.text: 18世纪从意大利语 castrato 借入，源自拉丁语 castratus“被阉割的”；名称来自这类历史歌手遭受的身体处理。

usage_note: 音乐史用语；现代 countertenor 是不同概念，不应与之混称。

senses.meaning_zh: 阉伶；幼年遭阉割以保留高音域的历史男歌手
senses.meaning_en: A historical male singer castrated before puberty to preserve a high vocal range.
senses.english_definition: A castrato was a male singer who had been castrated before puberty so that his voice would remain high.
senses.collocation_zh: 著名阉伶；阉伶歌手
senses.sentence_en: Farinelli was one of the most celebrated castrati of the eighteenth century.
senses.sentence_zh: 法里内利是十八世纪最负盛名的阉伶之一。

etymology_story.zh: 英语从意大利语借入 castrato，其本义是“被阉割的”，是 castrare（阉割）的过去分词形式，最终源自拉丁语 castrare。这个分词被用作名词，指通过青春期前阉割而保留高音域的男歌手。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed Italian castrato, literally 'castrated,' the past participle of castrare, ultimately from Latin castrare. The participle became a noun for a male singer whose high range had been preserved through castration before puberty.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语将 castrato 作为完整借词使用；castrat- + -o 反映意大利语形式，不是英语中能自由套用的构词公式。复数为 castrati，也可用 castratos；同源英语词包括 castrate（阉割）、castrated（被阉割的）、castrating（阉割的）、castration（阉割）和 castrator（实施阉割者或工具）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English treats castrato as a whole-word borrowing; castrat- + -o reflects its Italian form rather than a productive English construction. Its plurals are castrati and castratos; related English words include castrate, castrated, castrating, castration, and castrator.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: male soprano（男高音域歌手，尤指男声女高音）描述音域，不必指阉伶；countertenor（假声男高音）通常指主要运用假声等方式演唱高音域的成年男歌手；eunuch（阉人）描述身体状况，不表示具有歌唱职业或能力。这些词都不能与 castrato 完全互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Male soprano describes vocal range without necessarily implying castration; countertenor usually denotes an adult male singer using falsetto or related techniques for a high range; eunuch describes a castrated male without implying a singing career. None is fully interchangeable with castrato.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 castrato 与 castration（阉割）相连：身体处理留下了高音域。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect castrato with castration: the physical intervention preserved the high range.

pronunciation.note: 采用美式读音；依据词典注音转写为 IPA。

forms: 形容词，无时态或复数变化。
family: confocally 共焦地；focal 焦点的

morphology.text: con-（共同）+ focal（焦点的）→ confocal（共焦的）。

etymology.text: 19世纪英语把表示“共同”的拉丁来源前缀 con- 与 focal 结合，形成“共用焦点”的术语；想象两套镜头对准同一个点。

usage_note: 用于几何和光学，常修饰 ellipses、lenses、microscope。

senses.meaning_zh: 共焦的；具有共同焦点的
senses.meaning_en: Having the same focus or foci.
senses.english_definition: Geometrical figures or optical systems are confocal if they share the same focus or foci.
senses.collocation_zh: 共焦椭圆；共焦圆锥曲线
senses.sentence_en: These confocal ellipses share the same two foci.
senses.sentence_zh: 这些共焦椭圆具有相同的两个焦点。

senses.meaning_zh: 共焦显微成像的；利用共轭焦面及空间滤波抑制离焦光的
senses.meaning_en: Relating to microscopy that uses conjugate focal planes and spatial filtering to reject out-of-focus light.
senses.english_definition: A confocal microscope forms images using a focused illumination point and a detection aperture in a corresponding focal plane to reduce light from outside the plane being examined.
senses.collocation_zh: 共焦显微术；共焦成像
senses.sentence_en: The researchers used confocal microscopy to examine the fluorescent cells.
senses.sentence_zh: 研究人员利用共焦显微术观察这些带有荧光的细胞。

etymology_story.zh: confocal 由表示“共同”的拉丁来源前缀 con- 与 focal（焦点的）构成，最初的构词含义就是“具有共同焦点的”。这个几何与光学概念后来也用于共焦显微成像，其照明焦点与探测孔径所在平面在光学上相互对应。
etymology_story.en: Confocal combines the Latin-derived prefix con-, meaning 'together,' with focal, giving the literal sense 'sharing a focus.' The geometrical and optical concept was later applied to confocal microscopy, in which the illumination focus and the detection aperture occupy optically corresponding planes.

morphology_enriched.zh: con-（共同）+ focal（焦点的）→ confocal；focal 可进一步分析为 foc-（与 focus“焦点”有关的词干）+ -al（形容词后缀）。直接派生词有 confocally（以共焦方式）和 confocality（共焦性）；相关词族包括 focus、focused、focusing、focal、focally、focalize/focalise 和 focalization/focalisation。
morphology_enriched.en: Con- ('together') + focal → confocal; focal can be analyzed as foc-, the stem associated with focus, + the adjective suffix -al. Direct derivatives include confocally and confocality; the wider family includes focus, focused, focusing, focal, focally, focalize/focalise, and focalization/focalisation.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: cofocal（共焦的，较少见）可作近义词；coaxial（同轴的）指共享轴线；concentric（同心的）指共享中心。共享轴线或中心本身并不等于共享焦点。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Cofocal is a less common synonym; coaxial means sharing an axis; concentric means sharing a center. Sharing an axis or center does not by itself mean sharing a focus.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: con- 表“共同”，focal 表“焦点的”：共同对焦，记住“共焦”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Con- means 'together' and focal points to a focus: bring the focus together.

meaning: 十分位组（按数值排序后均分成十组中的一组）

pronunciation.note: 采用美式读音；依据词典注音转写为 IPA。

forms: 可数名词，复数 deciles。
family: decile 十分位的（形容词用法）

morphology.text: dec-（十）+ -ile（分位组名称中的构词成分）→ decile（十分位组）。

etymology.text: 词根来自拉丁语 decem“十”，19世纪进入英语统计术语；把排好队的人均分成十组，就能理解本课的 decile。

usage_note: 统计用语。top/bottom decile 常指最高／最低的10%人群；本课选“组”义，区别于分界值。

senses.meaning_zh: 十分位数；将有序数据划分为十个等份的九个分界值之一
senses.meaning_en: One of nine cut points dividing an ordered distribution into ten equal-proportion parts.
senses.english_definition: A decile is one of the nine values that divide an ordered set of data into ten parts containing equal proportions of the observations.

senses.meaning_en: One of ten groups formed by ranking observations and dividing them into equal-proportion groups.
senses.english_definition: A decile is one of ten groups into which people or things are divided according to their position in an ordered distribution.

etymology_story.zh: decile 是以拉丁语表示“十”的词干为基础、参照 quartile（四分位数）等词形成的统计术语。它既可指划分十等份的分界值，也可指这些分界值划出的组。
etymology_story.en: Decile is a statistical formation based on the Latin stem meaning 'ten,' modeled on terms such as quartile. It came to denote both a cut point separating tenths and a group defined by those divisions.

morphology_enriched.zh: dec-（十，与拉丁语 decem 有关）+ -ile（参照 quartile 等分位术语形成的词尾）→ decile；这里的 -ile 不是可任意套用的“组”义后缀。复数为 deciles；常用组合有 income decile（收入十分位组）、decile rank（十分位等级）和 decile ranking（十分位分级），没有常用的直接派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: Dec- ('ten,' related to Latin decem) + -ile, by analogy with quantile terms such as quartile, → decile; -ile is not a freely productive suffix meaning 'group.' The plural is deciles; common combinations include income decile, decile rank, and decile ranking, with no substantial common family of direct derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: quantile（分位数）是上位术语，不限定分成多少份；percentile（百分位数）按百分之一划分；quartile（四分位数）按四分之一划分。三者强调的划分粒度不同，不能在数值解释中随意替换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Quantile is the general term without a fixed number of divisions; percentile uses hundredths; quartile uses quarters. These terms specify different divisions and cannot be freely substituted when interpreting numerical results.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: dec- 就是“十”：先排序，再分十份；注意区分分界点与分出的组。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Dec- signals ten: rank the data, then divide into tenths; distinguish the boundaries from the groups.
